nabonidus.s: Nabonidus was the last king of the Chaldean or Neo-Babylonian Empire. He alienated Babylon's religious establishment by neglecting the cult of Marduk and spent about a decade at the Arabian oasis of Tayma, during which the New Year festival was not held.

nabonidus-chronicle.s: The Nabonidus Chronicle is an ancient Babylonian cuneiform text recording the reign of Nabonidus, last king of the Chaldean Empire, and the Persian conquest of Babylon. It notes repeated years in which the New Year festival was not held because the king was absent.

nabopolassar.s: Nabopolassar was a Chaldean leader who seized Babylon in 626 BCE and founded the Neo-Babylonian or Chaldean Empire. He took advantage of succession disputes in Assyria after Ashurbanipal's death and allied with Cyaxares of Media.

nader-shah.s: Nader Shah was a military commander from the Turkic Afshar tribe of Khorasan who founded the Afsharid Empire and reigned as Shah of Iran from 1736 to 1747. Rising in the service of the late Safavid Empire, he expelled Afghan, Ottoman and Russian occupiers and later sacked…

nader-shahs-invasion-of-india.s: Nader Shah's invasion of India was the 1738–1739 campaign in which the founder of the Afsharid Empire crossed the Khyber Pass, defeated the Mughal army and sacked Delhi. The plunder, including the Mughal imperial treasury, was so vast that Nader cancelled Iranian taxes for…

nagasaki.s: Nagasaki is a port city on the island of Kyushu in south-western Japan. Under the Tokugawa Shogunate it was the only permitted point of contact with European traders, through the Dutch post at Dejima, and a centre of controlled Chinese trade.

nahuatl.s: Nahuatl is a Uto-Aztecan language spoken by the Mexica and other peoples of central Mexico. The Aztec Empire spread its use across Mesoamerica, and it carried a rich tradition of poetry and learning.

naletale.s: Naletale is an archaeological site in present-day Zimbabwe with an elaborately decorated dry-stone enclosure. It is one of the stone-walled centres, alongside Danangombe and Khami, associated with the Rozvi Empire.

nanda-dynasty.s: The Nanda dynasty was a ruling house of the kingdom of Magadha in north-eastern India in the fourth century BCE. It controlled a large and wealthy state in the Ganges basin.

nanna.s: Nanna was the Sumerian moon god, known in Akkadian as Sin, whose principal temple stood at the city of Ur. Sargon of Akkad appointed his daughter Enheduanna as high priestess of Nanna at Ur.

nanren.s: Nanren, meaning southerners, was the term for the former subjects of the Southern Song in the ethnic hierarchy of the Yuan Dynasty. They formed the lowest of four tiers, below the Mongols, the Semu of Central and Western Asia, and the northern Chinese Hanren.

napata.s: Napata was an ancient city in Nubia near the Fourth Cataract of the Nile, in present-day Sudan. It became a principal centre of the Kushite Empire after Kerma and before Meroë, and housed an important cult of Amun that legitimised royal power.

napoleon.s: Napoleon Bonaparte was a French military leader who seized power after the French Revolution and ruled as Emperor of the French. His conquests reshaped Europe: he dissolved the Holy Roman Empire, invaded Russia in 1812, and his occupation of Spain helped trigger the collapse…

napoleon-iii.s: Napoleon III, nephew of Napoleon Bonaparte, was President of France and then Emperor of the French during the Second Empire from 1852 to 1870. He built specialised colonial troops for overseas campaigns.

napoleonic-code.s: The Napoleonic Code is the French civil code issued under Napoleon in 1804, codifying law on persons, property and contracts. It was exported across continental Europe during the First Empire's period of dominance.

naqsh-e-jahan-square.s: Naqsh-e Jahan Square is a large public square in Isfahan, Iran, laid out under Shah Abbas I when he made the city the Safavid capital. It is framed by major monuments including royal mosques and the Ali Qapu palace.

naqsh-e-rostam.s: Naqsh-e Rostam is an ancient necropolis near Persepolis in the province of Fars, Iran. It contains the rock-cut tombs of Achaemenid kings and later Sasanian rock reliefs.

narada-smriti.s: The Narada Smriti is a Sanskrit legal text in the Dharmashastra tradition. According to the site's Gupta Empire profile, it was compiled or refined during the Gupta period alongside the Brihaspati Smriti.

naram-sin.s: Naram-Sin was a king of the Akkadian Empire who reigned from 2254 to 2218 BCE and was the grandson of Sargon. His campaigns brought the empire to its greatest extent, and he claimed divine status, a major innovation in Mesopotamian kingship.

nasir-khusraw.s: Nasir Khusraw was an eleventh-century Persian poet, philosopher and traveller who later became an Ismaili missionary. He visited Fatimid Egypt around 1047 and described Cairo's wealth in his travel account.

national-debt.s: A national debt is the total borrowing of a state, typically funded through government bonds. Britain's funded national debt, developed from the late seventeenth century, was a pillar of the fiscal-military state that financed the British Empire's wars and expansion.

nationalism.s: Nationalism is the political idea that a nation, defined by shared language, culture or history, should possess its own state or self-government. From the nineteenth century it undermined multinational empires.

nationalism-and-independence-movements.s: Nationalism and independence movements are a recurring cause of imperial decline, as subject peoples organise around shared identity to demand autonomy or full sovereignty. Such movements are especially damaging to multinational and overseas empires whose legitimacy rests on…

nationality-question.s: The nationality question was the problem of how to accommodate the many national groups within the Habsburg monarchy. The 1867 Compromise satisfied the Hungarians but left Czechs, Poles, Slovenes, Croats and others in subordinate positions.

natron.s: Natron is a naturally occurring mixture of sodium salts, used historically in cleaning, preservation, glassmaking and medicine. Deposits in the Sahara and Sahel made it a trade good.

nau-nihal-singh.s: Nau Nihal Singh was a grandson of Ranjit Singh and briefly a ruler of the Sikh Empire. He died in 1840 when a gateway collapsed on him on the same day as his father Kharak Singh's death, in circumstances regarded as suspicious.

naval-blockade.s: A naval blockade is the use of warships to stop shipping from reaching or leaving an enemy's ports. Naval supremacy allowed the British Empire to blockade opponents in its wars and enforce the suppression of the Atlantic slave trade.

naval-power.s: Naval power is a recurring factor in imperial rise, as control of sea-lanes allows states to move armies, protect trade and project force across great distances. Maritime empires built their wealth and reach on fleets and ports.

navigation-acts.s: The Navigation Acts were a series of English laws from the mid-seventeenth century that restricted colonial trade to English ships and English ports. Aimed in large part at Dutch commercial dominance, they were a cornerstone of English mercantilism.

nazim.s: A nazim was a provincial governor in the Sikh Empire. Nazims were theoretically accountable to the court at Lahore under Ranjit Singh.

nazism.s: Nazism, or National Socialism, was the far-right ideology of Adolf Hitler's party, which ruled Germany from 1933 to 1945. It combined extreme nationalism, racism and antisemitism with authoritarian rule.

ndebele-kingdom.s: The Ndebele Kingdom was a state established by Mzilikazi on the south-western Zimbabwean plateau around 1840. Its arrival from the south completed the military occupation of the former heartland of the Rozvi Empire.

ndiadiane-ndiaye.s: Ndiadiane Ndiaye is a semi-legendary figure credited in oral tradition with founding the Jolof Empire in the Senegambian region in the mid-fourteenth century. He is said to have unified the Wolof-speaking states of Waalo, Cayor, Baol and Sine.

near-east.s: The Near East is a historical term for the region of western Asia and north-eastern Africa, including Mesopotamia, the Levant, Anatolia, Iran and Egypt. The ancient Near East was home to many of the earliest states and empires, including the Akkadian, Babylonian, Assyrian,…

nebuchadnezzar-i.s: Nebuchadnezzar I was a king of Babylon in the late twelfth century BCE, of the Second Dynasty of Isin. After the Elamite overthrow of the Kassite dynasty, he led a Babylonian revival.

nebuchadnezzar-ii.s: Nebuchadnezzar II was the most famous king of the Chaldean or Neo-Babylonian Empire, who died in 562 BCE. As crown prince he defeated Egypt at Carchemish in 605 BCE, securing the Levant.

necho-ii.s: Necho II was a pharaoh of Egypt's Twenty-sixth Dynasty in the late seventh and early sixth centuries BCE. He intervened in the Levant in support of the collapsing Assyrian state.

negus-nagast.s: Negus nagast, meaning king of kings, was the title of the Aksumite and later Ethiopian monarchs. In the Aksumite Empire it signalled a federal structure in which tributary rulers acknowledged Aksumite suzerainty while keeping local authority.

neo-assyrian-empire.s: The Neo-Assyrian Empire was the final and greatest phase of Assyrian power, beginning with a revival after 911 BCE and ending with the fall of Nineveh in 612 BCE. It built a tribute-extraction system based on conquest, mass deportation and provincial administration, and under…

neo-confucianism.s: Neo-Confucianism is a revived form of Confucian philosophy that incorporated metaphysical ideas in response to Buddhism and Daoism. Its most influential synthesis was developed by Zhu Xi under the Song Dynasty.

neo-elamite-period.s: The Neo-Elamite period is the final phase of Elamite history, from the early first millennium BCE to the sixth century BCE. Elam could still defeat Assyria, as at the Battle of Der in 721 BCE, but between 699 and 646 BCE some twelve kings reigned in rapid succession amid…

neo-hittite-states.s: The Neo-Hittite states were city-states in northern Syria and south-eastern Anatolia, such as Carchemish and Malatya, that emerged after the collapse of the Hittite Empire around 1200 BCE. They preserved elements of Hittite political and artistic tradition, including…

neo-sumerian-empire.s: The Neo-Sumerian Empire, also known as the Third Dynasty of Ur, was a Mesopotamian state that emerged around 2112 BCE after the collapse of the Akkadian Empire. Its founder Ur-Nammu expelled the Gutians and reasserted Sumerian political and cultural identity.

nepal.s: Nepal is a Himalayan country between Tibet and the plains of northern India. In the late eighteenth century the Gorkha kingdom of Nepal clashed with Tibet, prompting Qing intervention.

new-amsterdam.s: New Amsterdam was the Dutch colonial settlement on Manhattan Island, the chief town of the colony of New Netherland. It passed to England and was renamed New York, with the transfer confirmed in 1674.

new-christians.s: New Christians was the term used in Spain and Portugal for Jews and Muslims who had converted to Christianity, and their descendants. In Portugal they were the main target of the Inquisition, established in 1536, which suspected the sincerity of their conversion.

new-france.s: New France was the territory colonised by France in North America from the early seventeenth century, centred on the St Lawrence valley. Samuel de Champlain founded Quebec as its capital in 1608, and the colony was built around the fur trade.

new-hittite-kingdom.s: The New Hittite Kingdom is the term for the imperial phase of Hittite history, from about the fourteenth century BCE until the collapse around 1200 BCE. In this period the Hittite Empire became a great power of the Near East, expanding into Syria and contending with Egypt and…

new-julfa.s: New Julfa is the Armenian quarter of Isfahan, founded in 1604–1605 when Shah Abbas I relocated Armenian merchant communities from the Ararat region to his new capital. The Armenians brought commercial networks linking Iran to European markets.

new-kingdom-of-egypt.s: The New Kingdom of Egypt was the period of Egyptian history from about 1550 BCE to about 1070 BCE, covering the Eighteenth to Twentieth Dynasties. After Ahmose I expelled the Hyksos, Egypt became an imperial power, extending its rule into Nubia and the Levant and contending…

new-laws.s: The New Laws were a set of regulations issued by the Spanish crown in 1542 to govern the treatment of indigenous peoples in the Americas. Influenced by Bartolomé de las Casas and debates over the legitimacy of conquest, they sought to limit the encomienda system and prohibit…

new-oyo.s: New Oyo was the reduced successor state of the Oyo Empire, founded further south after the capital Oyo-Ile was abandoned around 1835–1836. The dynasty continued to rule from the new centre.

new-policies-song.s: The New Policies were reforms introduced by the chancellor Wang Anshi in the Song Dynasty between 1069 and 1076. They included government loans to peasants, a hired service system replacing labour conscription and other fiscal and military measures.

new-roman-empire.s: The New Roman Empire was the propaganda concept used by Fascist Italy to present its colonial expansion as a revival of ancient Roman greatness. Mussolini proclaimed the Italian Empire in 1936 after the conquest of Ethiopia.

new-york.s: New York is a major city in the United States and the home of the headquarters of the United Nations. The site's Hittite Empire profile notes that a reproduction of the treaty between the Hittites and Egypt, often cited as one of the earliest known peace treaties, hangs at the…

new-zealand.s: New Zealand is an island country in the south-western Pacific, colonised by Britain from the nineteenth century. It became one of the self-governing settler territories of the British Empire, later a dominion.

newfoundland.s: Newfoundland is a large island off the east coast of North America. The site's British Empire profile places the empire's conventional founding moment at Sir Humphrey Gilbert's formal claim of Newfoundland in 1583.

nezahualcoyotl.s: Nezahualcoyotl was a ruler of the city-state of Texcoco in the fifteenth century, also renowned as a poet and builder. As an exiled prince he joined the Mexica leader Itzcoatl and the city of Tlacopan in a coalition against Azcapotzalco.

ngazargamu.s: Ngazargamu was the capital of the Bornu phase of the Kanem-Bornu Empire, located west of Lake Chad in present-day north-eastern Nigeria. It replaced Njimi after the dynasty moved from Kanem to Bornu.

ngoni.s: The Ngoni are a Nguni-speaking people whose ancestors migrated northwards from south-eastern Africa during the upheavals of the Mfecane in the early nineteenth century. Led by Zwangendaba, Ngoni forces crossed the Zimbabwean plateau from about 1826.

nguni.s: The Nguni are a group of related Bantu-speaking peoples of south-eastern Africa, including the Zulu, Xhosa, Swati and Ndebele. During the Mfecane of the early nineteenth century, heavily armed Nguni-speaking groups moved north across the Zimbabwean plateau.

ngwana.s: Ngwana was a leader of one of the Nguni-speaking groups displaced during the Mfecane in southern Africa. His forces crossed the Zimbabwean plateau in the early 1820s.

nian-rebellion.s: The Nian Rebellion was a large armed uprising in northern China in the mid-nineteenth century, fought largely by mounted bands across the provinces north of the Huai River. Occurring alongside the Taiping and Dungan rebellions, it consumed imperial revenues and devastated…

nicholas-ii.s: Nicholas II was the last emperor of the Russian Empire, who abdicated in 1917. After the 1905 revolution he issued the October Manifesto creating the State Duma but consistently undermined its authority.

niger-bend.s: The Niger bend is the great northward curve of the Niger River in present-day Mali, where the river reaches the edge of the Sahara near Timbuktu and Gao. Its waterways and trading cities were key strategic assets.

niger-delta.s: The Niger Delta is the wide coastal delta of the Niger River in southern Nigeria, a region of creeks, mangroves and fertile soils. The Benin Empire's agricultural base in the delta region and surrounding forest produced yams, palm oil and kola nuts.

niger-river.s: The Niger River is the principal river of West Africa, flowing in a great arc from the Guinea highlands through the Sahel to the Atlantic in Nigeria. It was a vital artery for agriculture, trade and military movement.

nigeria.s: Nigeria is a country in West Africa, created as a British colony in the early twentieth century and independent since 1960. Its territory includes the heartlands of several empires covered on the site, among them the Benin Empire, the Oyo Empire and the Sokoto Caliphate.

nihil-novi.s: Nihil Novi was a constitutional act adopted in Poland in 1505, whose name means nothing new. It established that no new law could be enacted without the consent of the noble parliament, the Sejm.

nikephoros-i.s: Nikephoros I was a Byzantine emperor of the early ninth century. He refused to continue paying the tribute agreed by his predecessor to the Abbasid Caliphate, provoking a major invasion by Harun al-Rashid.

nile.s: The Nile is the longest river in Africa, flowing north through Sudan and Egypt to the Mediterranean. Its annual flood sustained the agricultural economy of Egypt and Nubia and made the valley one of the richest regions of the ancient and medieval world.

nile-cataracts.s: The Nile cataracts are a series of shallow, rocky stretches of rapids on the Nile between Aswan and Khartoum, traditionally numbered from the first in the north to the sixth. They formed natural frontiers between Egypt and Nubia.

nile-delta.s: The Nile Delta is the broad, fertile region of northern Egypt where the Nile divides into branches before reaching the Mediterranean. It has been one of the most productive agricultural areas in the world.

nimrud.s: Nimrud, ancient Kalhu, was a city on the Tigris in northern Mesopotamia that served as a royal capital of the Neo-Assyrian period. Ashurnasirpal II made it his capital in the ninth century BCE and built palaces decorated with stone reliefs.

nineveh.s: Nineveh was an ancient city on the Tigris opposite modern Mosul, and the last great capital of the Assyrian Empire. Ashurbanipal assembled his famous library of cuneiform tablets there.

ningbo.s: Ningbo, known in the Song period as Mingzhou, is a port city in Zhejiang province on China's east coast. Under the Song Dynasty it was one of the main ports, alongside Guangzhou and Quanzhou, for maritime trade.

nippur.s: Nippur was an ancient city in southern Mesopotamia, the religious centre of Sumer and home of the temple of the god Enlil. Rulers sought recognition there to legitimise their kingship.

nishapur.s: Nishapur is a city in Khorasan in north-eastern Iran, long a major centre on the Silk Road. The Seljuks captured it in 1037–1038 as they declared independence from the Ghaznavids.

nisibis.s: Nisibis was a fortress city in upper Mesopotamia, near modern Nusaybin in south-eastern Turkey, long contested between Rome and Persia. Rome gained it under the treaty of 299 CE.

nizam-al-mulk.s: Nizam al-Mulk was a Persian statesman who served as vizier of the Seljuk Empire from 1064 until his assassination in 1092. He fused Persian bureaucratic tradition with Turkic military rule, founded the Nizamiyya network of madrasas and wrote the Siyasat-nama, a treatise on…

nizam-of-hyderabad.s: The Nizam of Hyderabad was the title of the rulers of Hyderabad State in the Deccan, a dynasty founded by a former Mughal governor in the early eighteenth century. The Nizams were major rivals of the Maratha Empire, which fought them repeatedly and imposed tribute arrangements.

nizamiyya.s: The Nizamiyya were a network of madrasas, or institutions of higher learning, founded by the Seljuk vizier Nizam al-Mulk in Baghdad, Nishapur, Isfahan and other cities. They taught Shafi'i law and Sunni theology and trained the administrative and judicial class of the Seljuk…

nizari-ismaili-state.s: The Nizari Ismaili state was a network of mountain fortresses in Iran and Syria governed by the Nizari branch of Ismaili Shi'ism, centred on Alamut in the Alborz mountains from the late eleventh century. It resisted larger powers for over a century.

nizari-ismailism.s: Nizari Isma'ilism is a branch of Ismaili Shi'ism that arose from the Fatimid succession crisis of 1094, when supporters of the designated heir Nizar rejected the accession of al-Musta'li. Under Hasan-i Sabbah it established a state based at Alamut that opposed the Seljuk Empire.

nizari-mustali-schism.s: The Nizari–Musta'li schism was the division of the Ismaili Shi'a community following a succession crisis in the Fatimid Caliphate in 1094. The vizier al-Afdal bypassed the designated heir Nizar in favour of al-Musta'li, and the Nizari faction broke away.

njimi.s: Njimi was the early capital of the Kanem phase of the Kanem-Bornu Empire, located north-east of Lake Chad. It functioned as a commercial and administrative hub of the kingdom.

nkongolo-mwamba.s: Nkongolo Mwamba is a legendary figure credited in oral tradition with founding the first centralised Luba polity in central Africa. Scholars suggest he may be a symbolic figure rather than a single historical ruler.

nomadic-and-steppe-invasions.s: Nomadic and steppe invasions are a recurring factor in the decline of agrarian empires, as mounted peoples from the Eurasian steppe exploited their mobility to raid, extract tribute or conquer settled states. Defending long frontiers against them strained finances and armies.

nome.s: A nome was an administrative province of ancient Egypt, each governed by an official known to historians as a nomarch. Egypt was traditionally divided into some forty nomes along the Nile valley and delta.

north-africa.s: North Africa is the region of Africa along the Mediterranean coast, including Egypt, Libya, Tunisia, Algeria and Morocco, bordered by the Sahara to the south. It was the home of the Punic and Garamantian states and later a province of the Roman Empire.

north-african-elephant.s: The North African elephant was a population of elephants, now extinct, that lived in north-western Africa in antiquity. Carthage captured and trained them as war elephants.

north-america.s: North America is the continent comprising Canada, the United States, Mexico, Central America and the Caribbean. From the seventeenth century Britain and France competed there for colonies and trade.

north-china-plain.s: The North China Plain is a large, fertile lowland in northern China formed by the Yellow River. It has been a core agricultural region of Chinese states.

north-india.s: North India is the northern region of the Indian subcontinent, including the Indo-Gangetic plain. It has been the heartland of successive empires based at Delhi and Agra.

north-sea.s: The North Sea is a marginal sea of the Atlantic Ocean between Britain, Scandinavia, Germany, the Netherlands, Belgium and France. Its storms are notoriously unpredictable.

northern-europe.s: Northern Europe is the region comprising Scandinavia, the Baltic lands and neighbouring areas. In the early medieval period it was connected to the Islamic world by trade routes running along the Volga.

northern-nigeria-protectorate.s: The Northern Nigeria Protectorate was a British colonial territory proclaimed in 1900 under Frederick Lugard. It covered much of the lands of the Sokoto Caliphate, which British forces conquered in the following years.

northern-qi.s: The Northern Qi was a dynasty that ruled north-eastern China from 550 to 577 CE, one of the Northern Dynasties. It competed with the Northern Zhou for supremacy in the north.

northern-xiongnu.s: The Northern Xiongnu were the faction of the Xiongnu confederation that refused Han suzerainty after the empire split. When the Southern Xiongnu accepted Han client status in 48 CE, the Northern Xiongnu withdrew beyond the Gobi.

northern-yuan.s: The Northern Yuan was the regime maintained by the Mongol imperial line on the Mongolian steppe after the Yuan Dynasty lost China. The last Yuan emperor, Toghon Temur, fled Dadu in 1368 as Ming forces approached.

northern-zhou.s: The Northern Zhou was a dynasty that ruled north-western China from 557 to 581 CE, one of the Northern Dynasties. It conquered its rival the Northern Qi in 577 before being succeeded by the Sui.

norway.s: Norway is a Scandinavian country on the western side of the Scandinavian Peninsula, united with Denmark for much of the early modern period. The Swedish Empire won Norwegian provinces including Trondheim and Bohuslän from Denmark-Norway in the Treaty of Roskilde in 1658.

nova-scotia.s: Nova Scotia is a province on the Atlantic coast of Canada, originally part of French Acadia. Britain acquired it from France in the Treaty of Utrecht in 1713, along with Gibraltar, Hudson Bay and the asiento.

novellae.s: The Novellae, or Novels, are the new laws issued by the Byzantine emperor Justinian I after the completion of his legal code. Together with the Codex, Digest and Institutes they form the Corpus Juris Civilis.

novorossiysk.s: Novorossiysk is a port city on the Black Sea coast of southern Russia. In the late Russian Empire it developed as an outlet for exports, particularly grain from the fertile steppe of southern Russia.

nsundi.s: Nsundi was a province of the Kingdom of Kongo, located in the north of the kingdom in present-day Democratic Republic of the Congo. By the late fifteenth century it was one of the provinces, alongside Soyo and Mbata, under the authority of the manikongo.

ntim-gyakari.s: Ntim Gyakari was the ruler, or Denkyirahene, of the Denkyira state, which dominated the Akan region before the rise of Asante. He was killed in 1701 at the Battle of Feyiase, where a coalition led by Osei Tutu and Okomfo Anokye defeated Denkyira.

nubia.s: Nubia is the region along the Nile south of Egypt, covering southern Egypt and northern Sudan. It was rich in gold and controlled trade routes to tropical Africa.

numidians.s: The Numidians were Berber peoples of the North African interior west of Carthage, in present-day Algeria and Tunisia. They were renowned light cavalry and served as a key part of the Punic Empire's armies.

nupe-kingdom.s: The Nupe Kingdom was a state in the middle Niger region of present-day central Nigeria, north-east of Yoruba country. It exerted persistent military pressure on the early Oyo Empire.

nur-al-din.s: Nur al-Din was a Zengid ruler of Syria, based at Damascus, who unified Muslim Syria and led opposition to the Crusader states. He sent forces to Egypt, where his officer Saladin rose to power, and Saladin remained nominally subordinate to him.

nur-ibn-mujahid.s: Nur ibn Mujahid was a ruler of the Adal Sultanate from 1550 to 1567, following the death of Imam Ahmad ibn Ibrahim. He governed from Harar and built its defensive wall, the Jugol.

nuremberg.s: Nuremberg is a city in Franconia, in southern Germany, which became one of the most important free imperial cities of the Holy Roman Empire. Along with Frankfurt and Augsburg it grew wealthy as a commercial centre exploiting the empire's central European transit position.

nurhaci.s: Nurhaci was a Jurchen chieftain who unified the Jurchen clans of Manchuria between 1583 and 1616 and laid the foundations of the Qing Empire. Around 1601 he created the Eight Banners, a military and administrative system organising the Jurchen population.

nutmeg.s: Nutmeg is a spice obtained from the seed of a tree native to the Banda Islands in the Moluccas of present-day Indonesia. It was among the most valuable commodities of the early modern spice trade.

nuzi.s: Nuzi was an ancient Hurrian town near modern Kirkuk in northern Iraq. Thousands of cuneiform tablets found there document its society and economy in the mid-second millennium BCE.

nyakunembire.s: Nyakunembire was a dissident claimant within the Mutapa state in the late seventeenth century. He appealed to Changamire Dombo for support against his rivals and their Portuguese allies.

nyamazana-dlamini.s: Nyamazana Dlamini was a Swati queen and military leader who led one of the groups that crossed the Zimbabwean plateau during the Mfecane. Her forces killed the last Changamire of the Rozvi Empire, Chirisamhuru II, in about 1836.

nyantio.s: The nyantio were the warrior aristocracy of the Kaabu Empire in the Senegambian region. Kaabu grew from a vassal of Mali into an autonomous empire under their leadership as Mali weakened in the fifteenth century.

nyatsimba-mutota.s: Nyatsimba Mutota was the founder of the Mutapa Empire in the fifteenth century. A prince of the declining Kingdom of Zimbabwe, he migrated northwards in search of salt and fertile land.

nzinga-a-nkuwu.s: Nzinga a Nkuwu was a king, or manikongo, of the Kingdom of Kongo in the late fifteenth century. He received Portuguese envoys and converted to Christianity in 1491, taking the name João I.

national-liberation-front-south-yemen.s: The National Liberation Front was a Marxist-leaning nationalist movement that fought British rule in Aden and the protectorates from 1963. In 1967 it defeated its rival FLOSY, overthrew the sultans and sheikhs of the Federation of South Arabia, and proclaimed the People's…

new-guinea.s: New Guinea is the world's second-largest island, north of Australia, with high mountain ranges and dense rainforest. Its western coasts were claimed by the Sultanate of Tidore.

new-england.s: New England is the north-eastern region of the United States, from Connecticut to Maine. It was settled from 1620 by English Puritans and other colonists who founded Plymouth, Massachusetts Bay, Connecticut, Rhode Island and New Hampshire.

new-hampshire.s: New Hampshire is a state in New England, settled by the English from the 1620s along the Piscataqua river. Its towns were governed by Massachusetts from 1641 until it became a separate royal province in 1679.

north-caucasus.s: The North Caucasus is the region on the northern slopes of the Greater Caucasus range, between the Black and Caspian seas, home to peoples such as the Chechens, Ingush, Ossetians, Circassians and the many peoples of Dagestan. It was the home of the medieval Alans and was…

nara-narayan.s: Nara Narayan was a king of the Koch dynasty whose reign, from 1540 to 1587, was the high point of the Koch kingdom in northern Bengal and western Assam. With his brother and general Chilarai he campaigned against the Ahom, Kachari, Jaintia and other neighbours.

nueva-planta-decrees.s: The Nueva Planta decrees were a series of laws issued by Philip V of Spain between 1707 and 1716, during and after the War of the Spanish Succession. Punishing the territories of the Crown of Aragon that had backed the Habsburg claimant, they abolished the separate laws,…

new-granada.s: New Granada was the Spanish name for the lands of present-day Colombia and Panama, after the New Kingdom of Granada founded in 1538. In 1717 it became the seat of the Viceroyalty of New Granada, separated from Peru and including Venezuela and Quito, re-established permanently…

nine-years-war-ireland.s: The Nine Years' War was a rebellion of Gaelic Irish lords against English rule, fought from 1593 to 1603. Led by Hugh O'Neill, Earl of Tyrone, and Red Hugh O'Donnell, with Maguire of Fermanagh and other Ulster lords, it won victories such as the Yellow Ford in 1598.

nine-years-war.s: The Nine Years' War was fought from 1688 to 1697 between Louis XIV of France and the Grand Alliance led by William III of England and the Dutch Republic, with the Holy Roman Emperor, Spain and Savoy. French armies devastated the Palatinate and the Rhineland, burning…

norodom-sihanouk.s: Norodom Sihanouk was King of Cambodia, placed on the throne by the French in 1941. He won independence from France in 1953, abdicated in 1955 to lead politics as prince and head of state, and kept Cambodia neutral during the Vietnam War until Lon Nol deposed him in 1970.

nakhon-si-thammarat.s: Nakhon Si Thammarat is a city on the east coast of the Malay Peninsula in southern Thailand, called Ligor by Europeans. It was the centre of the trading kingdom of Tambralinga and later of a kingdom that spread Sri Lankan Theravada Buddhism to Sukhothai.

napoleonic-wars.s: The Napoleonic Wars were a series of wars between Napoleon's France and shifting coalitions of European powers from 1803 to 1815. They ended with Napoleon's defeat at Waterloo and the Congress of Vienna.

nasir-al-dawla.s: Nasir al-Dawla was the Hamdanid ruler of Mosul from 929 and the head of the family that also ruled Aleppo through his brother Sayf al-Dawla. In 942 and 943 he controlled the Abbasid caliph in Baghdad as amir al-umara, before the Buyids took over Iraq.

nectanebo-ii.s: Nectanebo II was the last native king of ancient Egypt, of the Thirtieth Dynasty. He took the throne around 360 BCE, repelled a Persian invasion in 351 BCE and built many temples.

new-castle-delaware.s: New Castle is a town on the Delaware River in the US state of Delaware. The Dutch founded it as Fort Casimir in 1651, took it from the Swedes in 1655 and called it New Amstel; the English renamed it New Castle after 1664.

new-orleans.s: New Orleans is a port city on the Mississippi River near its mouth, founded in 1718 by Jean-Baptiste Le Moyne de Bienville. It became the capital of French Louisiana, passed to Spain in 1763 and returned briefly to France before the Louisiana Purchase of 1803.

njinga-of-ndongo-and-matamba.s: Njinga Mbande was queen of the Mbundu kingdoms of Ndongo and Matamba in what is now Angola. She negotiated with the Portuguese in 1622, became ruler of Ndongo in 1624 and, driven out, conquered Matamba around 1631.

novo-brdo.s: Novo Brdo is a fortress and mining town in eastern Kosovo. From the early 14th century it was one of the richest silver and gold mines in the Balkans, worked by Saxon miners and trading through Ragusa, and it financed the medieval Serbian state.

nabeshima-naoshige.s: Nabeshima Naoshige was a Japanese warlord of Hizen province in Kyushu. A leading retainer of the Ryuzoji clan, he took effective control of its lands after Ryuzoji Takanobu was killed at the Battle of Okitanawate in 1584.

nasir-al-din-mauritanian-cleric.s: Nasir al-Din was a Berber Muslim cleric of the Zawaya tribes of south-western Mauritania. In the early 1670s he led a reform movement that overthrew the kings of Waalo, Kajoor, Jolof and Futa Toro in the lower Senegal valley.

national-assembly-of-kuwait.s: The National Assembly of Kuwait is the country's elected parliament, created by the constitution of 1962 and first elected in 1963. It is the most powerful elected legislature in the Gulf, able to question and remove ministers.

national-assembly-of-hungary.s: The National Assembly is the single-chamber parliament of Hungary, meeting in the Parliament building in Budapest. Its history reaches back to the medieval diet, and since the free elections of 1990 it has elected the prime minister and the president.

national-assembly-of-bulgaria.s: The National Assembly is the single-chamber parliament of Bulgaria, first convened under the Tarnovo Constitution of 1879. Grand National Assemblies have been called for constitutional changes, including the one that adopted the democratic constitution of 1991.

national-assembly-of-france.s: The National Assembly is the lower house of the French parliament, taking its name from the assembly proclaimed by the Third Estate in 1789. Under the Fourth Republic from 1946 it held predominant power and could bring down governments, which fell frequently.

ngo-dinh-diem.s: Ngo Dinh Diem was a Vietnamese Catholic nationalist who became prime minister of the State of Vietnam in 1954. In 1955 he deposed the emperor Bao Dai through a referendum and proclaimed the Republic of Vietnam in the south, ruling as its first president with American support.

ngo-quyen.s: Ngo Quyen was a Vietnamese general who defeated a fleet of the Southern Han at the Battle of Bach Dang in 938, luring its ships onto iron-tipped stakes planted in the river bed. The victory ended about a thousand years of Chinese rule over northern Vietnam.

niccolo-i-gattilusio.s: Niccolò I Gattilusio was a Genoese lord of Ainos (Enez) at the mouth of the Maritsa in Thrace. A brother of Francesco I Gattilusio, lord of Lesbos, he took control of Ainos around 1384 and also acted as regent on Lesbos.

niccolo-gattilusio-lord-of-lesbos.s: Niccolò Gattilusio was the last Genoese lord of Lesbos, who seized power by murdering his brother Domenico in 1458. A tributary of the Ottoman Empire, he could not resist when Mehmed II besieged Mytilene in 1462.

niall-of-the-nine-hostages.s: Niall of the Nine Hostages was a legendary Irish king of Tara, said to have reigned in the late 4th or early 5th century. He was the ancestor of the Uí Néill dynasties, whose northern branches founded Ailech, Tír Chonaill and Tír Eoghain and whose southern branches ruled Mide…

nizhny-novgorod.s: Nizhny Novgorod is a city at the confluence of the Oka and Volga rivers in Russia, founded in 1221 by Grand Prince Yuri II of Vladimir. In the 14th century it was the capital of the Grand Principality of Nizhny Novgorod-Suzdal before passing to Moscow in 1392.

northern-cameroons.s: The Northern Cameroons was the northern part of the British Cameroons, a League of Nations mandate and later United Nations trust territory carved from German Kamerun. It bordered Bornu and Adamawa and was administered as part of Northern Nigeria.

north-west-frontier-province.s: The North-West Frontier Province was a province created by the British in 1901 from the frontier districts of the Punjab, with Peshawar as its capital. Princely states such as Swat, Dir, Amb and Chitral lay alongside it, and the tribal areas beyond.

nuevo-leon.s: Nuevo León is a region of north-eastern Mexico with its capital at Monterrey. It grew from the New Kingdom of León, a frontier province of New Spain granted to Luis de Carvajal in 1579, and supplied settlers for neighbouring Nuevo Santander.

nuno-de-guzman.s: Nuño Beltrán de Guzmán was a Spanish conquistador and colonial official in Mexico. As governor of Pánuco he raided the Huastec region for slaves, and as president of the first Audiencia of New Spain he clashed with Hernán Cortés.

nursultan-nazarbayev.s: Nursultan Nazarbayev became first secretary of the Communist Party of the Kazakh SSR in 1989 and led Kazakhstan to independence in December 1991. As president until 2019 he dominated politics, built a new capital at Astana and steered an oil-based economy.

nagarakretagama.s: The Nagarakretagama, or Desawarnana, is an Old Javanese poem written in 1365 by the court poet Mpu Prapanca in praise of King Hayam Wuruk of Majapahit. It describes the court, royal tours and religious life, and lists nearly a hundred places across the archipelago claimed as…

na-gbewaa.s: Na Gbewaa is the founding ancestor of the Mole-Dagbani kingdoms of northern Ghana in oral tradition, said to have settled at Pusiga, probably in the 14th or 15th century. His sons and grandsons are credited with founding Mamprugu, Dagbon and Nanumba, and through a daughter the…

nachi-cocom.s: Nachi Cocom was the halach uinic, or supreme lord, of the Maya province of Sotuta in Yucatán. In 1536 he had an embassy of the rival Xiu of Maní, including Ah Dzun Xiu, killed at Otzmal.

naresh-chandra-singh.s: Naresh Chandra Singh was the last ruling raja of Sarangarh, a small feudatory state in Chhattisgarh, before its merger into the Central Provinces and Berar in 1948. He went on to a career in state politics and served briefly as Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh in 1969.

navarrese-company.s: The Navarrese Company was a band of mercenaries from Navarre and Gascony that fought in Greece in the late 14th century. Hired for campaigns in the Balkans, it seized Thebes from the Catalans in 1379 and then took over much of the Principality of Achaea, whose princely title…

neferhotep-iii.s: Neferhotep III was a king of the Theban Sixteenth Dynasty of Egypt during the Second Intermediate Period, when the Hyksos ruled the north. He is one of the better-attested rulers of the dynasty: a stela from his reign boasts that he rescued Thebes in a time of hunger and war.

nelson-mandela.s: Nelson Mandela was a South African anti-apartheid leader born into a junior branch of the Thembu royal house. A leader of the African National Congress, he was imprisoned from 1962 to 1990.

new-jersey.s: New Jersey is a state of the United States between the Hudson and Delaware rivers. Taken by England from the Dutch in 1664, it was granted to Lord Berkeley and Sir George Carteret and divided into East and West Jersey before being reunited as a royal province in 1702.

new-phocaea.s: New Phocaea, today Yeni Foça in western Turkey, was a fortified town on the Aegean coast founded by the Genoese Zaccaria family in the late 13th century to protect the nearby alum mines. Alum made it one of the most valuable Genoese possessions in the east.

new-providence.s: New Providence is the most populous island of the Bahamas, home of the capital Nassau. Settled from Eleuthera in the 17th century, it was repeatedly raided by the Spanish and French, and in the early 18th century became the base of the pirates' republic.

new-westminster.s: New Westminster is a city on the Fraser River in British Columbia, Canada. Royal Engineers under Richard Clement Moody founded it in 1859 as the capital of the mainland Colony of British Columbia.

nguyen-kim.s: Nguyen Kim was a Vietnamese general who led the loyalists of the Later Le dynasty against the Mac dynasty, which had usurped the throne in 1527. He restored a Le emperor in Thanh Hoa in 1533.

nguyen-nhac.s: Nguyen Nhac was the eldest of the three Tay Son brothers who led the revolt of 1771 against the Nguyen lords from Tay Son village in Binh Dinh. He proclaimed himself emperor in 1778 and ruled central Vietnam from Qui Nhon, while his brother Nguyen Hue took the north.

nguyen-van-thinh.s: Nguyen Van Thinh was a Saigon physician and politician who became the first president of the French-backed Autonomous Republic of Cochinchina in June 1946. The government had little popular support and was denounced by nationalists as a French creation.

nicobar-islands.s: The Nicobar Islands are an archipelago in the eastern Indian Ocean, today part of India's union territory of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. Denmark claimed them from the 18th century and made several failed attempts at settlement before giving up the claim in 1868-1869.

nicolae-ceausescu.s: Nicolae Ceaușescu was the communist leader of Romania from 1965 to 1989. He won Western praise for keeping distance from Moscow, but his rule became one of Eastern Europe's harshest dictatorships, with a pervasive secret police, a personality cult and severe austerity to repay…

nikephoros-ii-phokas.s: Nikephoros II Phokas was a Byzantine general and emperor from 963 to 969. He reconquered Crete from the Arabs in 961 after the siege of Chandax, sacked Aleppo in 962 and later took Cilicia and Antioch.

nikola-altomanovic.s: Nikola Altomanović was a Serbian magnate who built the largest lordship in western Serbia as the empire of Stefan Dušan broke up. By about 1371 he held lands from Rudnik and Užice to the borders of Ragusa.

nikolay-chkheidze.s: Nikolay Chkheidze was a Georgian Menshevik leader who chaired the Petrograd Soviet in 1917. Returning to the Caucasus, he chaired the Sejm of the Transcaucasian Democratic Federative Republic in 1918 and then the constituent assembly of the Democratic Republic of Georgia.

nino-visconti.s: Nino Visconti was the last judge of Gallura in Sardinia and a leading figure in Pisan politics. Expelled from Pisa in 1288 during the struggle involving his grandfather Ugolino della Gherardesca, he lost Gallura to the Pisan commune.

nobel-peace-prize.s: The Nobel Peace Prize is one of the prizes established by the will of Alfred Nobel and awarded annually since 1901 by a committee of the Norwegian parliament. Laureates who led modern states include Óscar Arias of Costa Rica in 1987, Juan Manuel Santos of Colombia in 2016 and…

noguera-pallaresa.s: The Noguera Pallaresa is a river of the Catalan Pyrenees, rising near the French border and flowing south past Sort and Tremp to join the Segre. Its valley formed the heart of the medieval County of Pallars, which in 1011 was divided into an upper county, Pallars Sobirà, and a…

north-channel.s: The North Channel is the strait between north-east Ireland and south-west Scotland, only about 20 kilometres wide between Antrim and Kintyre. In antiquity and the early Middle Ages it was a highway rather than a barrier: the Gaelic kingdom of Dál Riata spanned both shores,…

north-west-company.s: The North West Company was a fur-trading partnership based in Montreal that competed fiercely with the Hudson's Bay Company across western Canada. Its traders and Métis allies pushed far inland and opposed the Red River Colony, a conflict that led to the Battle of Seven Oaks…

northern-expedition.s: The Northern Expedition was the military campaign of the Kuomintang's National Revolutionary Army, led by Chiang Kai-shek, to defeat the northern warlords and reunify China. Launched from Guangzhou in 1926, it took the Yangtze valley, split the Nationalist–Communist alliance…

northern-mariana-islands.s: The Northern Mariana Islands are a chain of islands in the western Pacific north of Guam. Spanish until 1899, they were sold to Germany, taken by Japan in 1914 and placed under American administration as part of the Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands in 1947.

numa-pompilius.s: Numa Pompilius was, according to Roman tradition, the second king of Rome, a Sabine from Cures chosen after Romulus. Legend credits him with founding Rome's religious institutions, including the priesthoods, the Vestal Virgins and the religious calendar.

nuri-al-said.s: Nuri al-Said was an Iraqi soldier and statesman who served as prime minister of the Kingdom of Iraq many times between 1930 and 1958. A veteran of the Arab Revolt, he favoured close ties with Britain and took Iraq into the Baghdad Pact in 1955.

nyaungyan-min.s: Nyaungyan Min was a son of Bayinnaung who rebuilt royal power in Upper Burma after the First Toungoo Empire collapsed in 1599. Ruling from Ava, he restored control over the dry zone and the Shan states, founding the Restored Toungoo dynasty, which his son Anaukpetlun extended…

nafusa-mountains.s: The Nafusa Mountains are an upland range in north-western Libya, south-west of Tripoli, long inhabited by Amazigh (Berber) communities. From the 8th century the region became a stronghold of Ibadi Islam, supporting the Ibadi imamate of Tripolitania and later the Rustamid…

narai.s: Narai was king of Ayutthaya from 1656 to 1688. He opened Siam to wide foreign contacts, exchanging embassies with Louis XIV of France and employing the Greek adventurer Constantine Phaulkon, and he made Lopburi a second royal residence.

na-atabia.s: Na Atabia was a ruler (nayiri) of Mamprugu, the oldest of the Mossi-Dagomba kingdoms in northern Ghana, around 1700. Under him the royal capital moved from Gambaga to Nalerigu, which remains the seat of the Mamprugu king, while Gambaga continued as a centre for Muslim traders…

na-zangina.s: Na Zangina was ya-na (king) of Dagbon in northern Ghana in the early 18th century and is remembered as the first king to adopt Islam at court. His reign strengthened ties with Muslim traders and scholars who linked Dagbon to the kola routes between Hausaland and the Akan forest.

nabeshima-naomasa.s: Nabeshima Naomasa was daimyo of the Saga domain in Kyushu from 1830 to 1861. Responsible for guarding Nagasaki, he promoted Western learning, built Japan's first reverberatory furnace in 1850 and cast iron cannon, giving Saga some of the most modern weapons in Japan.

nachan-kaan.s: Nachan Kaan was the Maya lord of Chetumal, on the south-east coast of the Yucatán peninsula, at the time of the Spanish conquest. The shipwrecked Spaniard Gonzalo Guerrero married his daughter, adopted Maya customs and led Chetumal's warriors against Spanish expeditions.

nagabhata-ii.s: Nagabhata II was a king of the Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty of northern India in the early 9th century. Around 816 he defeated Chakrayudha of the Ayudha dynasty, a client of the Pala Empire, and took Kannauj, which became the Pratihara capital.

najaf-qoli-khan-donboli.s: Najaf Qoli Khan Donboli was a chief of the Kurdish Donboli family who governed Tabriz in the later 18th century. In the turmoil after Nader Shah's death he was confirmed as governor by Karim Khan Zand and ruled largely independently.

najda-ibn-amir-al-hanafi.s: Najda ibn Amir al-Hanafi was a Kharijite leader from the Banu Hanifa of al-Yamama in central Arabia. During the Second Fitna he broke with the extreme Azariqa and from about 686 built a short-lived state over al-Yamama, Bahrain and Oman.

nakhon-pathom.s: Nakhon Pathom is a town west of Bangkok in central Thailand and one of the largest centres of the Dvaravati culture between the 7th and 11th centuries. Silver coins found there and at other sites, inscribed with the merit of the king of Dvaravati, gave that culture its name.

nan-thip-chang.s: Nan Thip Chang was a hunter turned local leader who in 1732 drove a Burmese-backed governor out of Lampang in northern Thailand and was recognised as its ruler. His descendants, the Chet Ton or Chao Chet Ton dynasty, led the expulsion of the Burmese from Lan Na later in the…

nana-olomu.s: Nana Olomu was an Itsekiri merchant prince who served as governor of the Benin River in the Niger Delta from 1884 and controlled much of its palm-oil trade. His power over trade brought him into conflict with British officials, and in 1894 British forces destroyed his…

nanbu-nobunao.s: Nanbu Nobunao was head of the Nanbu warrior family of northern Mutsu in Japan. In 1590 Toyotomi Hideyoshi confirmed him in his lands, though he lost the Tsugaru region to his breakaway retainer Tsugaru Tamenobu.

nancen-pinco.s: Ñancen Pinco was a king of Chimor, the Chimú state on the north coast of Peru, known from a dynastic list recorded by the Spanish. Ruling from Chan Chan, he is credited with extending the kingdom by conquest over the neighbouring river valleys, from Saña to Santa.

narasimhavarman-ii.s: Narasimhavarman II, also called Rajasimha, was a Pallava king of south India who reigned in a time of relative peace around 700 to 728. He was a major builder in stone, credited with the Shore Temple at Mamallapuram and the Kailasanatha temple at Kanchipuram, and patronised…

narendra-shah.s: Narendra Shah was maharaja of Tehri Garhwal, a princely state in the Himalayas, from 1919 to 1946. He founded a new capital, Narendranagar, and introduced administrative reforms, but his government's forest policies provoked peasant protest, crushed with shooting at Tilari in…

narmer.s: Narmer was an Egyptian king of around 3100 BCE, the last ruler of the Thinite line of Dynasty 0 and usually counted as the founder of the First Dynasty. The Narmer Palette, a carved ceremonial slate, shows him wearing the crowns of both Upper and Lower Egypt and is often read…

naro-mahadev.s: Naro Mahadev was a Brahmin officer in Maratha service who at the end of the 17th century received Ichalkaranji, in present-day Maharashtra, as a grant. His descendants took the name Ghorpade and held Ichalkaranji as a feudatory of Kolhapur State until Indian independence.

naser-al-din-shah-qajar.s: Naser al-Din Shah was the Qajar shah of Iran from 1848 to 1896, the longest reign of the dynasty. His minister Amir Kabir founded the Dar ol-Fonun college, and the shah travelled to Europe, but he relied on foreign loans and concessions, provoking the tobacco protest of…

nasir-ibn-murshid.s: Nasir ibn Murshid was elected imam of Oman by Ibadi scholars at Rustaq in 1624, founding the Ya'aruba dynasty and ending Nabhani rule. He united the tribes of the interior and attacked the Portuguese forts on the coast, taking several of them.

nasir-khan-faruqi.s: Nasir Khan Faruqi was the second ruler of the Faruqi dynasty of Khandesh in the Tapti valley of central India, reigning from 1399 to 1437. He captured the hill fortress of Asirgarh and founded the city of Burhanpur, which became the Faruqi capital.

nasir-pasha-al-sadun.s: Nasir Pasha al-Sa'dun was a sheikh of the Sa'dun family, rulers of the Muntafiq tribal confederation of southern Iraq. Under the Ottoman reforms of the governor Midhat Pasha around 1870 he accepted office as the first governor of the new Muntafiq sanjak and founded the town of…

nasjonal-samling.s: Nasjonal Samling was the Norwegian fascist party founded in 1933 by Vidkun Quisling. It won little support at the polls, but when Germany invaded Norway on 9 April 1940 Quisling tried to seize power.

nasr-ibn-ali.s: Nasr ibn Ali was a Kara-Khanid ruler who in 999 captured Bukhara and ended the Samanid Empire, bringing Transoxiana under Turkic Muslim rule. His conquests made the Kara-Khanids neighbours and rivals of Mahmud of Ghazni along the Oxus.

national-guard-panama.s: The National Guard (Guardia Nacional) was Panama's armed force, created in 1953 from the National Police. In 1968 it overthrew President Arnulfo Arias, and its commander Omar Torrijos ruled the country and negotiated the Torrijos-Carter Treaties of 1977 for the canal's transfer.

national-guard-dominican-republic.s: The National Guard (Guardia Nacional Dominicana) was the constabulary created in 1917 by the US military government that occupied the Dominican Republic from 1916 to 1924. Trained and led by US Marines, it replaced the old regional armies.

national-hero-of-indonesia.s: National Hero of Indonesia (Pahlawan Nasional) is the highest honorary title awarded by the Indonesian government, given posthumously since 1959 to people who fought colonial rule or served the nation. Recipients include rulers of the older kingdoms of the archipelago, such as…

national-workshops.s: The National Workshops were a public works scheme set up by the Provisional Government of the French Second Republic in February 1848 to give work to the unemployed of Paris. Over 100,000 men enrolled, alarming conservatives.

native-hawaiians.s: Native Hawaiians are the Polynesian people of the Hawaiian Islands, who settled them roughly a thousand years ago and later formed the Kingdom of Hawaii. Disease cut their numbers sharply in the 19th century.

nazar-ali-khan-shahsevan.s: Nazar Ali Khan Shahsevan was a chief of the Shahsevan tribal confederation who ruled the Ardabil khanate in north-western Iran in the later 18th century. Relying on Shahsevan nomad cavalry from the Moghan steppe and the Sabalan mountains, he was drawn into the struggles of…

nchare-yen.s: Nchare Yen was, according to Bamum tradition, a Tikar prince who conquered the area around Foumban in the western grassfields of Cameroon and became the first mfon (king) of Bamum, traditionally in 1394. The dynasty he founded ruled continuously, and the later king Ibrahim…

ndewura-jakpa.s: Ndewura Jakpa was the founder of the Gonja kingdom in northern Ghana in the mid-17th century, according to Gonja tradition and its Arabic chronicle. Leading Mande cavalry from the Niger region, he conquered the lands between the Black and White Volta rivers and divided them…

negasi-krestos.s: Negasi Krestos was a Shewan noble claiming Solomonic descent who around 1682 established an autonomous lordship in northern Shewa, in central Ethiopia, as the Gondar emperors weakened. His successors, first called meridazmach and later negus, built Shewa into a powerful…

nelson-oduber.s: Nelson Oduber is an Aruban politician and leader of the People's Electoral Movement (MEP), who served as prime minister of Aruba from 1989 to 1994 and again from 2001 to 2009. His governments oversaw rapid tourism growth after the closure of the Lago oil refinery, and Aruba's…

nelsons-dockyard.s: Nelson's Dockyard is the Georgian naval dockyard at English Harbour in Antigua, built in the 18th century as the Royal Navy's chief base in the Leeward Islands. Horatio Nelson served there in the 1780s.

nepherites-ii.s: Nepherites II was the last pharaoh of the Twenty-ninth Dynasty of Egypt, son of Hakor. He reigned only a few months in 380 BCE before being deposed by Nectanebo I, a general from Sebennytos, who founded the Thirtieth Dynasty, the last native dynasty of ancient Egypt.

nestor-makhno.s: Nestor Makhno was a Ukrainian anarchist from Huliaipole who during the Russian Civil War led the Revolutionary Insurgent Army of Ukraine. His forces fought the Austro-German occupiers, the Ukrainian nationalists and the Whites, sometimes in alliance with the Red Army, and…

new-bern.s: New Bern is a town in eastern North Carolina founded in 1710 by Swiss and German settlers under Christoph von Graffenried at the meeting of the Neuse and Trent rivers. Its encroachment on Tuscarora land helped provoke the Tuscarora War of 1711.

new-delhi.s: New Delhi is the capital of India, a planned city designed by Edwin Lutyens and Herbert Baker south of old Delhi. The move of the capital of British India from Calcutta was announced at the Delhi Durbar of 1911, and the new city was inaugurated in 1931.

new-economic-mechanism.s: New Economic Mechanism is the name of market-oriented reforms in two communist states. In Hungary, introduced by János Kádár's government in 1968, it gave state enterprises more freedom and allowed some market prices, making Hungary the most liberal economy in the Soviet bloc.

new-testament.s: The New Testament is the second part of the Christian Bible, a collection of 27 books in Greek written in the 1st and early 2nd centuries, including the four Gospels, the letters of Paul and Revelation. Its translations shaped many languages: Martin Luther translated it into…

ngam-mueang.s: Ngam Mueang was king of Phayao in northern Thailand in the late 13th century and the best-known ruler of that Tai state. He was an ally of Mangrai of Lan Na and Ram Khamhaeng of Sukhothai; the three kings are said to have sworn friendship around 1287, an event commemorated by…

ngawang-namgyal.s: Ngawang Namgyal was a Tibetan lama of the Drukpa school who fled to Bhutan in 1616 after a dispute over his recognition as a reincarnation. There he built fortress-monasteries (dzongs), repelled Tibetan invasions and unified the country under a dual system of religious and…

ngo-xuong-van.s: Ngo Xuong Van was a son of Ngo Quyen, founder of the Ngo dynasty of Vietnam. After Duong Tam Kha usurped the throne following Ngo Quyen's death in 944, Ngo Xuong Van overthrew him in 950 and ruled jointly with his elder brother Ngo Xuong Ngap.

ngola-hari.s: Ngola Hari was a ruler of Ndongo in present-day Angola, installed by the Portuguese in 1626 as a rival to Queen Njinga. Based at the fortress of Pungo Andongo, he depended on Portuguese support while Njinga fought on from Matamba.

ngolo-diarra.s: Ngolo Diarra was a former war captive who rose to command the tonjon, the slave army of the Bamana Empire of Ségou on the middle Niger. In 1766 he seized the throne and founded the Diarra dynasty, which ruled until the conquest by Umar Tall in 1861.

nguyen-hoang.s: Nguyen Hoang was the first of the Nguyen lords of southern Vietnam. In 1558, to escape his rivals the Trinh lords, he had himself appointed governor of Thuan Hoa in central Vietnam.

nguyen-huu-tho.s: Nguyen Huu Tho was a South Vietnamese lawyer who chaired the National Liberation Front from 1962. When the Provisional Revolutionary Government of the Republic of South Vietnam was formed in 1969 he headed its advisory council.

nguyen-thi-binh.s: Nguyen Thi Binh is a Vietnamese communist politician who served as foreign minister of the Provisional Revolutionary Government of the Republic of South Vietnam. She led its delegation at the Paris peace talks and was the only woman to sign the Paris Peace Accords of 1973.

nguyen-van-thieu.s: Nguyen Van Thieu was a South Vietnamese general who rose among the officers ruling after the overthrow of Ngo Dinh Diem in 1963 and was president of the Republic of Vietnam from 1967 to 1975. He depended heavily on American military support.

niall-glundub.s: Niall Glúndub was a king of Ailech from the northern Uí Néill and High King of Ireland from 916. One of the most powerful Irish kings of his time, he led a campaign against the Vikings who had re-established themselves at Dublin and was killed fighting them at the Battle of…

niccolo-tommaseo.s: Niccolò Tommaseo was an Italian writer and lexicographer, born in Dalmatia, best known for his great dictionary of the Italian language. Imprisoned by the Austrians with Daniele Manin in January 1848, he was freed when Venice rose in March and served as a minister of the…

nicholas-ii-of-opava.s: Nicholas II of Opava was a Přemyslid duke of Opava in Silesia, a descendant of King Ottokar II of Bohemia. Married to a daughter of Duke Przemysław of Racibórz, he received the duchy of Racibórz after its Piast line died out in 1336, uniting it with Opava under Bohemian…

nicholas-the-child.s: Nicholas the Child was the last lord of Rostock, on the Baltic coast of Mecklenburg. Pressed by his Mecklenburg cousins and the town's own ambitions, he placed himself under Danish protection in 1300.

nicolaas-waterboer.s: Nicolaas Waterboer was kaptein (chief) of the Griqua of Griquatown in southern Africa from 1852. When diamonds were found in the late 1860s, rival claims to the diggings were settled by the Keate Award of 1871 in his favour.

nicolas-durand-de-villegaignon.s: Nicolas Durand de Villegaignon was a French naval officer and Knight of Malta who in 1555, backed by Admiral Gaspard de Coligny, founded France Antarctique in Guanabara Bay, Brazil. He built Fort Coligny on an island, but religious quarrels with Calvinist settlers divided the…

nicolas-grunitzky.s: Nicolas Grunitzky was a Togolese politician who led parties favouring close ties with France in French Togoland and became prime minister of the autonomous republic in 1956. Defeated by Sylvanus Olympio's Committee of Togolese Unity in the UN-supervised elections of 1958, he…

nicolaus-copernicus.s: Nicolaus Copernicus was an astronomer born in Toruń in Royal Prussia who proposed that the Earth and planets revolve around the Sun. He spent most of his life as a canon of the cathedral chapter of Frombork in the Prince-Bishopric of Warmia, also working as a physician,…

nicomedes-iv.s: Nicomedes IV Philopator was the last king of Bithynia in north-western Anatolia. Twice driven out by Mithridates VI of Pontus, he was restored each time by Rome.

nikol-pashinyan.s: Nikol Pashinyan is an Armenian journalist and politician who led the peaceful protests of 2018, the Velvet Revolution, which brought him to power as prime minister. His government faced defeat in the 2020 war with Azerbaijan over Nagorno-Karabakh and the loss of the region in…

nikola-i-of-montenegro.s: Nikola I Petrović-Njegoš ruled Montenegro as prince from 1860 and as king from 1910. Victories over the Ottomans won recognition of independence at the Congress of Berlin in 1878 and new territory including Nikšić, Podgorica and Bar.

nikola-karev.s: Nikola Karev was a Macedonian revolutionary of the Internal Macedonian-Adrianople Revolutionary Organisation. During the Ilinden Uprising of August 1903 he led the rebels who seized Kruševo and headed its ten-day provisional government, the Kruševo Republic, before Ottoman…

nikolai-avksentiev.s: Nikolai Avksentiev was a Russian Socialist Revolutionary politician who served as interior minister in the Provisional Government in 1917. In September 1918 he became chairman of the five-member Directory of the All-Russian Provisional Government formed at Ufa, which moved to…

nikolaus-federmann.s: Nikolaus Federmann was a German adventurer in the service of the Welser bank of Augsburg, which held the colony of Klein-Venedig in Venezuela. In search of gold and El Dorado he led long expeditions inland, the last of which crossed the Andes and reached the Muisca highlands…

niqmaddu-ii.s: Niqmaddu II was a king of Ugarit on the Syrian coast in the 14th century BCE. Formerly an Egyptian vassal, he submitted to the Hittite king Suppiluliuma I, making Ugarit a Hittite vassal for the rest of its history.

niqmepa-of-alalakh.s: Niqmepa was a king of Mukish, with its capital at Alalakh in the Amuq plain of south-eastern Turkey, in the 15th century BCE. Son and successor of Idrimi, he ruled as a vassal of the Hurrian kingdom of Mitanni.

niqmepa-of-ugarit.s: Niqmepa was a king of Ugarit, the trading city on the Syrian coast, in the late 14th and 13th centuries BCE, and son of Niqmaddu II. He ruled for several decades as a vassal of the Hittite Empire, under treaties with Mursili II, and many legal and diplomatic tablets from the…

niskala-wastu-kancana.s: Niskala Wastu Kancana was a Sundanese king of Galuh in western Java who ruled from Kawali in the 14th and 15th centuries. The Astana Gede inscriptions at Kawali record him fortifying the town and urging his successors to rule justly.

nissanka-malla.s: Nissanka Malla was a king of Polonnaruwa in Sri Lanka from 1187 to 1196, a prince from Kalinga in eastern India. He left more inscriptions than any other Sri Lankan king, proclaiming his piety, generosity and achievements, and built monuments such as the Nissanka Lata Mandapaya.

nitta-yoshisada.s: Nitta Yoshisada was a Japanese warrior of the Minamoto line who joined Emperor Go-Daigo against the Hojo regents. In 1333 he stormed Kamakura, destroying the Kamakura shogunate and opening the Kenmu Restoration.

nizam-ali-khan.s: Nizam Ali Khan, Asaf Jah II, was Nizam of Hyderabad from 1762 to 1803 and son of the dynasty's founder. He moved the capital from Aurangabad to Hyderabad in 1763.

nizami-ganjavi.s: Nizami Ganjavi was a Persian poet from Ganja in the Caucasus, regarded as the greatest master of the romantic epic in Persian. His Khamsa (Five Treasures) includes Layla and Majnun, dedicated to the Shirvanshah Akhsitan I, and Khosrow and Shirin, and he enjoyed the patronage…

noe-zhordania.s: Noe Zhordania was a Georgian Social Democrat (Menshevik) leader who headed the government of the Democratic Republic of Georgia from 1918 to 1921. His government held democratic elections, carried out land reform and adopted a constitution.

noman-celebicihan.s: Noman Celebicihan was a Crimean Tatar lawyer, poet and the first elected mufti of the Muslims of Crimea. In December 1917 the Kurultai at Bakhchysarai proclaimed the Crimean People's Republic with him as its leader.

norodom-sihamoni.s: Norodom Sihamoni has been king of Cambodia since 2004, chosen by the Throne Council after his father Norodom Sihanouk abdicated. Before his accession he was a ballet dancer and teacher in Prague and Paris and Cambodia's ambassador to UNESCO.

norodom-suramarit.s: Norodom Suramarit was king of Cambodia from 1955 to 1960. His son Norodom Sihanouk abdicated in his favour in 1955 to enter politics and lead the Sangkum movement, so Suramarit reigned while Sihanouk governed.

north-korea.s: North Korea, the Democratic People's Republic of Korea, is the state in the north of the Korean peninsula proclaimed in 1948. It grew out of the Soviet occupation zone north of the 38th parallel, where the Soviet authorities brought Kim Il Sung to power.

northern-dobruja.s: Northern Dobruja is the region between the lower Danube and the Black Sea, including the port of Constanța, which forms the south-east of Romania. Ottoman for over four centuries, it was awarded to Romania by the Congress of Berlin in 1878 in exchange for southern Bessarabia,…

northern-region-nigeria.s: The Northern Region was the largest of the regions of colonial and independent Nigeria, covering the former emirates of the Sokoto Caliphate and Borno, with its capital at Kaduna. Formed from the Northern Provinces, it became self-governing in 1959 under Ahmadu Bello.

nripendra-narayan.s: Nripendra Narayan was maharaja of Cooch Behar, a princely state in northern Bengal, from 1863 to 1911. Educated under British guardianship, he married Suniti Devi, daughter of the Brahmo reformer Keshab Chandra Sen, in 1878.

ntare-iv-of-ankole.s: Ntare IV, called Kitabanyoro, was a mugabe (king) of Ankole in south-western Uganda, remembered in tradition as a warrior king. His byname, meaning "killer of the Banyoro", recalls his victory over raiders from Bunyoro, the powerful northern neighbour that had long attacked…

ntare-iv-rugamba.s: Ntare IV Rugamba was mwami (king) of Burundi in the first half of the 19th century and its greatest conqueror. He doubled the size of the kingdom, absorbing parts of Bugesera and other neighbours to the north and east, and placed his sons as princes over the new lands.

nuba-mountains.s: The Nuba Mountains are a range of granite hills in South Kordofan in central Sudan, home to many Nuba peoples speaking different languages. Their hills long gave refuge from slave raiders.

nur-al-din-umar-ibn-rasul.s: Nur al-Din Umar ibn Rasul was a commander of Turkmen origin who founded the Rasulid dynasty of Yemen. Left as deputy when the last Ayyubid ruler departed for Egypt in 1229, he soon declared independence, took the title al-Mansur and obtained recognition from the Abbasid caliph.

nur-muhammad-taraki.s: Nur Muhammad Taraki was an Afghan writer and founder of the communist People's Democratic Party of Afghanistan, leading its Khalq faction. After the Saur Revolution of April 1978 he became head of state of the Democratic Republic of Afghanistan.

nurali-khan.s: Nurali Khan was khan of the Junior Juz of the Kazakhs from 1748, succeeding his father Abulkhair Khan. He depended increasingly on Russian support, which brought him into conflict with his own clans, and during the revolt of Syrym Datuly he was deposed and fled to Russia in 1786.

nurullah-bey.s: Nurullah Bey was the last emir of Hakkari, the Kurdish principality in the mountains of south-eastern Anatolia. In the 1840s he joined Bedir Khan Bey of Bohtan in attacks on the Assyrian Christians of the Hakkari mountains, which drew European protest.

niklot.s: Niklot was prince of the Obotrites, a West Slavic people on the Baltic coast of what is now Mecklenburg. He resisted the Wendish Crusade of 1147 and later the campaigns of Henry the Lion, Duke of Saxony, and was killed in battle in 1160.

najaf-qoli-khan-bakhtiari.s: Najaf-Qoli Khan Bakhtiari, known by his title Samsam al-Saltaneh, was a chief of the Bakhtiari tribes of south-western Iran. In 1909 he and Sardar As'ad II led Bakhtiari forces that took Tehran from Mohammad Ali Shah and restored the constitution.

nestor-lakoba.s: Nestor Lakoba was an Abkhaz Bolshevik who led Soviet Abkhazia from 1921 until his death in 1936. Close to Stalin, he slowed collectivisation and protected local landowners and customs, but saw Abkhazia reduced to an autonomous republic within Georgia in 1931.

naaman-river.s: The Na'aman is a short coastal river in northern Israel that flows into the Mediterranean just south of Acre. Its mouth lies beside Tel Akko, the mound of ancient Acre, which used it as a harbour in the Bronze Age.

ninhursag.s: Ninhursag was a Sumerian mother goddess associated with birth, fertility and the mountains. She was worshipped at Kesh and at Adab, whose main temple, the E-sar, was hers, and Sumerian kings described themselves as nourished by her milk.

numitor.s: Numitor is a legendary king of Alba Longa, the grandfather of Romulus and Remus in Roman tradition. Deposed by his younger brother Amulius, he was restored after his grandsons killed the usurper.

nahash-of-ammon.s: Nahash was a king of Ammon in the late 11th or early 10th century BCE, known from the Hebrew Bible. According to the Book of Samuel he besieged Jabesh-Gilead and was defeated by Saul, whose victory confirmed his kingship.

notsie.s: Notsie (Notsé) is a town in southern Togo, remembered in tradition as the ancestral walled home of the Ewe peoples. According to their histories, the Ewe fled from Notsie to escape the tyranny of King Agokoli, probably in the 17th century, and dispersed to found new states.

niketas-chalkoutzes.s: Niketas Chalkoutzes was a Byzantine military commander of the 10th century. In 965, while the emperor Nikephoros II Phokas campaigned in Cilicia, he led an expedition that took Cyprus, ending three centuries of shared Arab and Byzantine rule over the island.

naumburg.s: Naumburg is a town on the Saale river in Saxony-Anhalt, Germany. It became the seat of a bishopric moved from Zeitz in 1028 and grew into a trading town.

nicolas-avellaneda.s: Nicolás Avellaneda was an Argentine lawyer and statesman who served as president from 1874 to 1880. Earlier Sarmiento's minister of education, he continued the expansion of schools, encouraged immigration and backed the Conquest of the Desert against the Indigenous peoples of…

nagorno-karabakh.s: Nagorno-Karabakh is a mountainous region in the south-east of the Lesser Caucasus, within Azerbaijan, historically with an Armenian majority. Made an autonomous oblast of Soviet Azerbaijan in 1923, it became the focus of the Karabakh movement and of a war in which Armenian…

national-liberation-movement-ghana.s: The National Liberation Movement was a political party in the Gold Coast founded in Kumasi in 1954 to defend Asante interests against Kwame Nkrumah's Convention People's Party. Backed by the Asantehene and led in parliament by Kofi Abrefa Busia, it demanded a federal…

novempopulania.s: Novempopulana was a late Roman province in south-western Gaul, between the Garonne and the Pyrenees, formed around 300 from the southern part of Aquitania. Its name, 'nine peoples', referred to its Aquitanian tribes, though it later contained twelve civitates.

nagorno-karabakh-autonomous-oblast.s: The Nagorno-Karabakh Autonomous Oblast was an autonomous region of the Azerbaijan SSR, created in 1923 for the mountainous part of Karabakh, which had an Armenian majority. Its demand in 1988 for transfer to Soviet Armenia began the Karabakh conflict.

nakhchivan-autonomous-soviet-socialist-r.s: The Nakhchivan Autonomous Soviet Socialist Republic was an autonomous republic of the Azerbaijan SSR, created in 1924 for the Nakhchivan region, separated from the rest of Azerbaijan by Armenian territory. Its status followed the treaties of Moscow and Kars of 1921, which…

nali-poet.s: Nali, the pen name of Mala Khidr Ahmad Shawaysi, was a Kurdish poet of the early 19th century from the Sharazur region, associated with the Baban court at Sulaymaniyah. With Salim and Kurdi he pioneered poetry in the Sorani dialect of Kurdish, which through their work became a…

noor-mahal.s: Noor Mahal is a palace in Bahawalpur, Pakistan, built for Nawab Sadiq Muhammad Khan IV between 1872 and 1875. Designed in an Italianate style with Islamic domes, it served as a state guest house and a venue for the nawabs' durbars and official receptions.

nitra.s: Nitra is a city in western Slovakia on the Nitra river, one of the oldest towns in the country. In the early 9th century it was the seat of the Slavic prince Pribina, before Mojmír I of Moravia drove him out around 833 and joined it to Great Moravia, and a bishopric was first…

naveta-des-tudons.s: The Naveta des Tudons is a prehistoric stone tomb near Ciutadella on Menorca, shaped like an upturned boat. Built of large dressed stones without mortar in the late Bronze Age, it was a collective burial chamber on two levels, in which the remains of dozens of people were found.

nubians.s: The Nubians are a people of the Nile valley in southern Egypt and northern Sudan who speak Nubian languages. Their ancestors created the kingdoms of Kerma and Kush and the Christian states of Nobadia, Makuria and Alodia, before gradual Islamisation and Arabisation from the…

nahal-hever.s: Nahal Hever is a dry ravine in the Judaean Desert running down to the western shore of the Dead Sea. In its Cave of Letters, excavated by Yigael Yadin in 1960–1961, refugees of the Bar Kokhba revolt left letters from Simon bar Kokhba, legal documents and the private archive of…

nasi-title.s: Nasi is a Hebrew title meaning 'prince' or 'leader', used in the Hebrew Bible for tribal chiefs. Simon bar Kokhba took the title Nasi of Israel during the revolt of 132–135 CE.

nijmegen.s: Nijmegen is a city in the province of Gelderland in the Netherlands, on the Waal, and claims to be the oldest city in the country. It grew from the Batavian settlement and Roman town of Ulpia Noviomagus, became an imperial residence under Charlemagne and later a city of the…

ngamiland.s: Ngamiland is the region of north-western Botswana around Lake Ngami and the Okavango Delta, named after the lake. It was the territory of the Batawana chiefdom and was brought into the Bechuanaland Protectorate in the late 19th century.

ninurta-kudurri-usur-i.s: Ninurta-kudurri-usur I was king of Babylon for about three years in the late 10th century BCE, the second ruler of the Bazi Dynasty after Eulmash-shakin-shumi. He was succeeded by Shirikti-Shuqamuna, who reigned only a few months.

ninurta-kudurri-usur-of-suhu.s: Ninurta-kudurri-usur was governor of Suhu and Mari on the middle Euphrates in the 8th century BCE, son and successor of Shamash-resha-usur. His long Akkadian inscriptions, found in the region of Anah, describe building works, irrigation and his defeat of an Aramaean tribal…

narnala.s: Narnala is a hill fortress in the Satpura range in the Akola district of Maharashtra, India. Of early origin, it was rebuilt by the Bahmani Sultanate and strengthened by the Imad Shahi sultans of Berar, who held it alongside Gawilgarh.

nikephoros-iii-botaneiates.s: Nikephoros III Botaneiates was Byzantine emperor from 1078 to 1081. An elderly general, he rebelled against Michael VII and took the throne, but his reign saw continued Turkish advances in Anatolia, revolts by rival generals and financial collapse.

nabu-mukin-zeri.s: Nabu-mukin-zeri was a chief of the Chaldean tribe of Bit-Amukani who seized the throne of Babylon in 731 BCE after a period of turmoil following the death of Nabonassar. Tiglath-pileser III of Assyria campaigned against him, besieged his tribal centre of Sapia and by 729 BCE…

noreia.s: Noreia was the chief town of the Norici in the eastern Alps, mentioned by Roman writers but never firmly located. Near it the Cimbri defeated a Roman army under Gnaeus Papirius Carbo in 113 BCE, and Caesar records that the Boii besieged it before joining the Helvetii.

nama-people.s: The Nama are a Khoekhoe people of southern Namibia and the north-western Cape of South Africa, traditionally pastoralists who speak Khoekhoegowab, a click language. In the 19th century many Nama communities lived under kapteins, often alongside Oorlam groups and Christian…

national-truth-commission-brazil.s: The National Truth Commission was a body set up by Brazil under President Dilma Rousseff to investigate human rights violations, especially those of the military dictatorship of 1964–1985. Its final report, published in December 2014, documented hundreds of killings and…

north-yorkshire.s: North Yorkshire is the largest county in England, created in 1974 from most of the old North Riding and parts of the West and East Ridings of Yorkshire. It includes the Yorkshire Dales, the North York Moors and the city of York, and contains many Roman, Anglo-Saxon and…
