nicolas-de-ovando.s: Nicolás de Ovando was a Spanish knight of the Order of Alcántara and governor of the Indies at Santo Domingo from 1502 to 1509. He rebuilt Santo Domingo after a hurricane, organised the forced labour of the Taíno and crushed their chiefdoms, notably by the massacre at Jaragua…

nunavut.s: Nunavut is the largest and northernmost territory of Canada, created on 1 April 1999 from the eastern part of the Northwest Territories under the Nunavut Land Claims Agreement of 1993. Most of its roughly 40,000 people are Inuit, and Inuktitut is an official language alongside…

nidwalden.s: Nidwalden is a canton of central Switzerland south of Lake Lucerne, with its capital at Stans; together with Obwalden it formed the old canton of Unterwalden. In September 1798 it rose against the constitution of the Helvetic Republic and was crushed by French troops, who…

nine-rank-system.s: The nine-rank system was a method of selecting officials introduced in 220 under Cao Pi, the first emperor of Cao Wei. Local assessors graded candidates into nine ranks according to their character and ability, and appointments followed the grades.

nervion.s: The Nervión is a river of the Basque Country in northern Spain, rising on the borders of Álava and Burgos and flowing north to Bilbao. There it joins the Ibaizabal to form the Estuary of Bilbao, which runs to the Bay of Biscay.

nonantola-abbey.s: Nonantola Abbey is a Benedictine monastery near Modena in northern Italy, founded in 752 by Anselm, a former Duke of Friuli and brother-in-law of the Lombard king Aistulf. Favoured by Lombard and Carolingian rulers, it grew into one of the richest abbeys of Italy, with a…

numantia.s: Numantia was a Celtiberian hill town of the Arevaci near modern Soria in northern Spain. It resisted Roman armies for two decades during the Celtiberian Wars until Scipio Aemilianus surrounded it with siege works in 134–133 BCE; starving, its defenders surrendered or took…

nertobriga-beturia.s: Nertobriga was an ancient town of the Celtici in Beturia, near Fregenal de la Sierra in the province of Badajoz, south-western Spain. Pliny the Elder lists it among the Celtic towns of the region, and under Rome it bore the name Concordia Iulia.

ndjamena.s: N'Djamena is the capital and largest city of Chad, at the confluence of the Chari and Logone rivers on the border with Cameroon. It was founded by the French in 1900 as Fort-Lamy, named after the officer François Lamy, who was killed at the Battle of Kousséri that year, and…

nadol.s: Nadol, the medieval Naddula, is a town in Pali district of Rajasthan, India. Around 950 Lakshmana, a member of the Chahamanas of Shakambhari, founded a kingdom there that ruled southern Marwar until the early 13th century, usually as feudatories of the Chaulukyas of Gujarat.

nagpur.s: Nagpur is a city in eastern Maharashtra, India, near the geographical centre of the country. Founded around 1702 by Bakht Buland Shah of the Gond kingdom of Deogarh, it became from the 1740s the capital of the Bhonsle Marathas, whose kingdom stretched to Odisha.

nannuka.s: Nannuka was the founder of the Chandela dynasty in the early 9th century, ruling around Khajuraho in Bundelkhand, then called Jejakabhukti, probably as a feudatory of the Gurjara-Pratiharas. Chandela inscriptions name him as the first of the line, which became an independent…

nanchang.s: Nanchang is the capital of Jiangxi province in south-eastern China, on the Gan River south-west of Lake Poyang. A walled city since the Han dynasty, it withstood a long siege by Chen Youliang in 1363, defended for Zhu Yuanzhang by his nephew Zhu Wenzheng.

new-echota.s: New Echota was the capital of the Cherokee Nation from 1825 until removal in the 1830s, near modern Calhoun in north-west Georgia, United States. Laid out as a planned town with a council house, a supreme court and a printing office, it published the Cherokee Phoenix.

nanih-waiya.s: Nanih Waiya is a large flat-topped earthen platform mound in Winston County, Mississippi, built during the Middle Woodland period, roughly between 1 and 300 CE. The Choctaw regard it as their sacred place of origin, the "Mother Mound", from which, in one tradition, their…

nataraja.s: Nataraja, "lord of dance", is the Hindu god Shiva shown as the cosmic dancer who creates and destroys the universe. In the classic form, perfected in Chola bronzes of the 10th to 12th centuries, he dances within a ring of flames, holding a drum and fire, with one foot on a…

naha.s: Naha is the capital of Okinawa Prefecture, Japan, on the south-west coast of Okinawa Island. It grew as the port of the Ryukyu Kingdom, handling tribute trade with China and trade with Japan, Korea and South-East Asia, below the royal castle of Shuri, which is now part of the…

nohoch-mul.s: Nohoch Mul is the main pyramid of the Maya city of Cobá in Quintana Roo, Mexico. About 42 metres high, it rises in stepped terraces to a small temple at the top decorated with descending-god figures in Postclassic style, similar to those at Tulum.

nnamdi-azikiwe.s: Nnamdi Azikiwe, known as Zik, was a leading Nigerian nationalist and journalist and the first President of Nigeria. Through his newspapers, starting with the West African Pilot in 1937, and the National Council of Nigeria and the Cameroons, he campaigned for independence.

nlakapamux.s: The Nlaka'pamux, formerly called the Thompson people, are an Interior Salish First Nation of southern British Columbia, living along the Fraser River around the Fraser Canyon and along the lower Thompson River. They lived by salmon fishing, hunting and gathering.

norman-manley.s: Norman Manley was a Jamaican lawyer and statesman who founded the People's National Party in 1938, after the labour unrest of that year. He led the campaign for self-government and universal suffrage, served as chief minister and then premier of Jamaica from 1955 to 1962, and…

newfoundland-company.s: The Newfoundland Company, formally the London and Bristol Company, was an English joint-stock company chartered by James I in 1610 to colonise Newfoundland. Its first governor, John Guy, founded a settlement at Cupids in Conception Bay that year, the first English colony on…

new-zealand-constitution-act-1852.s: The New Zealand Constitution Act 1852 was an act of the British Parliament that granted self-government to the colony of New Zealand. It created a General Assembly with an elected House of Representatives and an appointed Legislative Council, and six provinces with their own…

newport-rhode-island.s: Newport is a city on Aquidneck Island in Narragansett Bay, Rhode Island. Founded in 1639 by settlers including William Coddington and John Clarke, it became one of the leading ports of colonial America, prospering from Atlantic trade, including the slave trade, and was home to…

nobel-prize.s: The Nobel Prizes are international awards founded under the will of the Swedish chemist and industrialist Alfred Nobel and first awarded in 1901. They are given each year for physics, chemistry, physiology or medicine, literature and peace, and since 1969 also for economic…

nanaimo.s: Nanaimo is a city on the east coast of Vancouver Island in British Columbia, Canada. The Hudson's Bay Company opened coal mines there in the early 1850s, bringing miners from Britain, and it became the leading coal-mining centre of the colony and later province.

notion-ancient-city.s: Notion, or Notium, was an ancient Greek city on the coast of Ionia in Asia Minor, serving as the port of Colophon, near the sanctuary of Claros. A Spartan fleet defeated the Athenians there in 406 BCE during the Peloponnesian War.

nokoni.s: The Nokoni were a division of the Comanche, whose name is usually translated as Those Who Turn Back or Wanderers. They ranged over north-central Texas between the Red River and the Brazos.

nicola-pisano.s: Nicola Pisano was an Italian sculptor who worked in Pisa and is often seen as a founder of modern sculpture. His pulpits for the Pisa Baptistery, finished in 1260, and Siena Cathedral drew on Roman sarcophagi to give figures new weight and realism.

niccolo-iii-deste.s: Niccolò III d'Este was marquis of Ferrara from 1393 to 1441, ruling Ferrara, Modena and from 1409 Reggio. A skilled diplomat, he made his court a centre of humanist learning and hosted the Council of Ferrara in 1438.

niue.s: Niue is a raised coral island in the South Pacific, east of Tonga, one of the largest coral islands in the world. It became a British protectorate in 1900, was annexed to New Zealand with the Cook Islands in 1901 and given its own administration in 1904.

nottinghamshire.s: Nottinghamshire is a county in the East Midlands of England, centred on the city of Nottingham and the valley of the River Trent. In the late Iron Age it lay in the territory of the Corieltauvi, and Nottingham was later one of the Five Boroughs of the Danelaw.

nominoe.s: Nominoe was the first ruler of a united Brittany, a Breton noble and count of Vannes whom Louis the Pious appointed as his representative there in 831. After Louis's death he broke with Charles the Bald, defeated him at Ballon in 845 and made Brittany independent of the…

nova-gorica.s: Nova Gorica is a town in western Slovenia, built from 1947 on the Yugoslav side of the new border that left Gorizia in Italy. Planned as a modern socialist town to replace Gorizia as the regional centre, it grew up beside its Italian neighbour, and since Slovenia joined the…

nienburg-weser.s: Nienburg is a town in Lower Saxony, Germany, on the Weser between Bremen and Minden. It was a residence of the counts of Hoya until their line died out in 1582, after which it passed to the Guelph dukes of Brunswick-Lüneburg and was fortified as a stronghold on the Weser.

nassau-castle.s: Nassau Castle is a hilltop castle above the town of Nassau on the Lahn in Rhineland-Palatinate, Germany, built around 1125 by the counts of Laurenburg. The family took its name from the castle, becoming the House of Nassau, whose branches later produced the Dutch royal family…

nicard-dialect.s: Niçard, or Nissart, is the variety of Occitan traditionally spoken in Nice and its former county, usually classed as a sub-dialect of Provençal. Under Savoyard rule it was the everyday language of the population, while Italian was used in administration from the 16th century.

nordlinger-ries.s: The Nördlinger Ries is a roughly circular basin about 24 km across in western Bavaria, formed by a meteorite impact about 15 million years ago. Its fertile floor made it a rich farming region, divided in the Middle Ages between the counts of Oettingen and the imperial city of…

nogent-le-rotrou.s: Nogent-le-Rotrou is a town in the Eure-et-Loir department on the Huisne, in the Perche region of north-western France. It takes its name from the Rotrou counts of Perche, whose castle of Saint-Jean overlooks the town.

nuno-mendes.s: Nuno Mendes was the last count of the first County of Portugal, descended from Vímara Peres. Seeking greater independence, he rebelled against King García II of Galicia and was defeated and killed at the Battle of Pedroso in 1071.

noguera-ribagorzana.s: The Noguera Ribagorzana is a river of the central Pyrenees that rises near the Aragon–Catalonia border and flows south into the Segre. For much of its course it marks the boundary between Aragon and Catalonia, and its valley belonged to the medieval county of Ribagorza.

new-braunfels.s: New Braunfels is a city in central Texas, between San Antonio and Austin, on the Comal and Guadalupe rivers. It was founded in 1845 by German settlers of the Adelsverein led by Prince Carl of Solms-Braunfels and named after Braunfels in Hesse.

nahe.s: The Nahe is a left tributary of the Rhine, about 125 km long, rising in the Saarland and joining the Rhine at Bingen. Its valley, between the Hunsrück and the North Palatinate uplands, passes Idar-Oberstein and Bad Kreuznach and is known for its wines.

neuwied.s: Neuwied is a town on the right bank of the Rhine in Rhineland-Palatinate, Germany, north-west of Koblenz. Founded in 1653 by Count Frederick III of Wied, it grew as a planned residence town that welcomed religious minorities, among them Mennonites, Moravian Brethren and Jews.

neckar.s: The Neckar is a river in south-western Germany, about 360 km long, that rises near Villingen-Schwenningen at the edge of the Black Forest and flows north through Tübingen, Stuttgart and Heilbronn to join the Rhine at Mannheim. Its valley was the heartland of Württemberg and is…

nidda.s: Nidda is a small town in the Wetterau district of Hesse, Germany, on the river of the same name. In the Middle Ages it was the centre of the County of Nidda, which passed to the counts of Ziegenhain and, when their line died out in 1450, to the landgraves of Hesse.

nicosia.s: Nicosia is the capital of Cyprus, in the centre of the island on the Pedieos river. It became the capital in the Byzantine period and was the seat of the Lusignan kings, whose Gothic cathedral of St Sophia survives as the Selimiye Mosque.

nuuk.s: Nuuk is the capital of Greenland, on the south-west coast at the mouth of a large fjord system. The missionary Hans Egede founded it in 1728 as Godthåb ('good hope'), moving his mission and trading post there, and it became the centre of Danish administration.

niksar.s: Niksar is a town in Tokat Province, northern Turkey, on the Kelkit river. As ancient Neocaesarea it was a city of Pontus and the home of the bishop Gregory Thaumaturgus.

nekrasov-cossacks.s: The Nekrasov Cossacks were Don Cossacks and Old Believers who followed Ignat Nekrasov into exile after the failure of the Bulavin Rebellion in 1708. They settled first in the Kuban under the Crimean Khanate and later in Ottoman lands, in the Danube delta and Anatolia, where…

narona.s: Narona was an ancient town on the lower Neretva, at modern Vid near Metković in southern Croatia. It began as a Greek trading post dealing with the Illyrian peoples of the interior and became an important Roman colony and administrative centre of the province of Dalmatia.

nigg-stone.s: The Nigg Stone is a Pictish cross-slab of around 800 CE, kept in the old parish church of Nigg in Easter Ross, Scotland. One face bears a cross filled with interlace and spiral ornament, the other a hunting scene and figures, including a scene of the hermits Paul and Anthony…

national-convention.s: The National Convention was the elected assembly that governed France from September 1792 to October 1795. On its first full day it abolished the monarchy and proclaimed the French Republic, and in 1793 it tried and executed Louis XVI.

naryn-kala.s: Naryn-Kala is the citadel of Derbent, in Dagestan, Russia, on a hill above the city and the Caspian Sea. Together with the long parallel walls that ran from the citadel to the shore, it was built of stone under the Sasanian Persian king Khosrow I in the 6th century to close…

nugaal-valley.s: The Nugaal Valley is a long valley in northern Somalia running south-east from the Sool region to the Indian Ocean near Eyl. Seasonal water and grazing make it important to pastoral clans.

nafpaktos.s: Nafpaktos, ancient Naupaktos and Venetian Lepanto, is a port town on the northern shore of the Gulf of Corinth in western Greece, guarded by a Venetian castle and a walled harbour. It served as an Athenian naval base in the Peloponnesian War, was sold to Venice in 1407 and…

nikephoros-ii-orsini.s: Nikephoros II Orsini was the last Orsini ruler of the Despotate of Epirus, reigning from 1335 to 1340 and again from 1356 to 1359. His first reign ended when the Byzantines annexed Epirus, and in 1356 he regained part of it from the Serbs after the death of Stefan Dušan.

nabadwip.s: Nabadwip, also called Nadia, is a town in West Bengal, India, on the Bhagirathi river. It was a seat of the Sena kings, and its surprise capture by Muhammad Bakhtiyar Khalji around 1204 began Muslim rule in Bengal.

ninh-binh-province.s: Ninh Bình is a province in northern Vietnam, on the southern edge of the Red River delta, with its capital at the city of Ninh Bình. It contains Hoa Lư, the capital of the Đinh and Early Lê dynasties in the 10th century, and the limestone karst landscape of Tràng An, a UNESCO…

novocherkassk.s: Novocherkassk is a city in Rostov oblast, southern Russia, founded in 1805 by Ataman Matvei Platov as the new capital of the Don Cossack Host. It was a centre of the anti-Bolshevik Don Cossacks in the Russian Civil War, and in 1962 a workers' protest there was put down with…

nerio-i-acciaioli.s: Nerio I Acciaioli was a Florentine noble who made himself Duke of Athens. From his base at Corinth he took Athens from the Catalan Company in 1388, ending Catalan rule, and was recognised as duke by King Ladislaus of Naples in 1394, shortly before his death.

nancy.s: Nancy is a city on the Meurthe in north-eastern France and the historic capital of the Duchy of Lorraine. The dukes made it their residence from the 12th century, and outside its walls René II defeated Charles the Bold in 1477.

north-rhine-westphalia.s: North Rhine-Westphalia is the most populous state of Germany, with its capital at Düsseldorf. It was created by the British occupation authorities in 1946 from the northern part of the Prussian Rhine Province and the Province of Westphalia, and the Free State of Lippe joined…

neubrandenburg.s: Neubrandenburg is a city in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, Germany, on Lake Tollense. It was founded in 1248 by the margraves of Brandenburg and passed to Mecklenburg around 1300 with the Lordship of Stargard.

neustrelitz.s: Neustrelitz is a town in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, Germany, founded in 1733 by Duke Adolphus Frederick III as the new residence of the dukes of Mecklenburg-Strelitz. Laid out as a baroque planned town with streets radiating from a central market square, it remained the…

niemodlin.s: Niemodlin (German: Falkenberg) is a small town in the Opole Voivodeship of south-western Poland, west of Opole. It grew around a castle of the Piast dukes of Opole and in the 14th century was the seat of a separate Duchy of Niemodlin.

nysa.s: Nysa (German: Neisse) is a town in the Opole Voivodeship of southern Poland, on the Nysa Kłodzka river. From the 12th century it belonged to the bishops of Wrocław, who ruled it as the capital of their duchy.

nikortsminda-cathedral.s: Nikortsminda Cathedral is an Orthodox church in the Racha region of north-western Georgia, built in 1010–1014 under King Bagrat III, the first ruler of a united Georgian kingdom. Dedicated to Saint Nicholas, it is known for its richly carved stone facades with biblical scenes.

niccolo-machiavelli.s: Niccolò Machiavelli was a Florentine diplomat, historian and political theorist. As secretary of the Second Chancery of the Florentine Republic from 1498 to 1512 he served on missions to Cesare Borgia, the French king and the emperor.

neu-augustusburg.s: Neu-Augustusburg is a Baroque palace in Weissenfels, Saxony-Anhalt, begun in 1660 for Duke Augustus of Saxe-Weissenfels on the site of an older castle. It was the residence of the dukes of Saxe-Weissenfels until the line died out in 1746, and its chapel and court hosted a…

nemanjic-dynasty.s: The Nemanjić dynasty ruled Serbia from 1166 to 1371. Its founder, Stefan Nemanja, united Serbian lands, and his son Stefan the First-Crowned became king in 1217, while another son, Saint Sava, won the Serbian Church's autocephaly in 1219.

nagapattinam.s: Nagapattinam is a port town on the coast of Tamil Nadu, India, south of the Kaveri delta. Under the Cholas it was a major harbour with a Buddhist monastery built with the support of the Srivijaya kings.

nabonassar.s: Nabonassar, in Akkadian Nabu-nasir, was king of Babylon from 747 to 734 BCE. His reign marks the start of the Babylonian Chronicles and of regular astronomical records, and Ptolemy's list of kings, used by later astronomers, counted its years from his accession, the Era of…

nabu-apla-iddina.s: Nabu-apla-iddina was king of Babylon from about 888 to 855 BCE, one of the longest reigns of the period. He restored temples damaged in earlier Aramean and Sutean raids, notably renewing the cult image of the sun god Shamash at Sippar, an event recorded on the Sun-god Tablet.

nabu-mukin-apli.s: Nabu-mukin-apli was king of Babylon from about 978 to 943 BCE and the first ruler of the Dynasty of E. His long reign was troubled by Aramean incursions, and the chronicles record that in several years the New Year festival could not be held because the road to Babylon was cut.

newcastle-west.s: Newcastle West is a market town in western County Limerick, Ireland. It grew around a castle of the FitzGerald earls of Desmond, who made it one of their main seats in western Munster.

norn-language.s: Norn was the North Germanic language spoken in Orkney, Shetland and Caithness, descended from the Old Norse of the Viking settlers. It remained the everyday language of the islands for centuries after they passed from Norway to Scotland in 1468 and 1469, but gave way to Scots…

nedunjeliyan-ii.s: Nedunjeliyan II was a Pandya king of the Sangam age in southern India, celebrated for his victory at Talaiyalanganam over the Chera and Chola kings and five chieftains. Sangam poems such as the Maduraikkanci, which describes his capital Madurai, praise his reign.

nannaya.s: Nannaya was the court poet of the Eastern Chalukya king Rajaraja Narendra at Rajahmundry in the 11th century. He began the translation of the Mahabharata into Telugu, the Andhra Mahabharatam, completing about two and a half of its eighteen books, which were later finished by…

narasimhadeva-i.s: Narasimhadeva I was a king of the Eastern Ganga dynasty of Odisha in India, ruling from 1238 to 1264. He took the offensive against the Muslim rulers of Bengal, defeating them in the 1240s and raiding their territory.

nanjing.s: Nanjing is the capital of Jiangsu province, on the lower Yangtze in eastern China. As Jianye and Jiankang it was the capital of Eastern Wu and the southern dynasties, and it later served as capital of the Southern Tang, the early Ming dynasty, the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom and…

neferkauhor.s: Neferkauhor was a king of the Eighth Dynasty of Egypt who reigned briefly at Memphis late in the 22nd century BCE. He is known mainly from a series of decrees found at Coptos, which grant offices and honours to the vizier Shemay and his son Idy.

nusrat-al-din-abu-bakr.s: Nusrat al-Din Abu Bakr was atabeg of Azerbaijan from 1191 to 1210, a member of the Eldiguzid dynasty. He took power after the murder of his uncle Qizil Arslan and ruled mainly from Tabriz and Nakhchivan, but his authority weakened.

nakhchivan.s: Nakhchivan is a city and region in the South Caucasus, now an autonomous republic of Azerbaijan separated from the rest of the country by Armenia and bordering Iran and Turkey. The city was a residence of the Eldiguzid atabegs in the 12th century and later the seat of a…

nymphenburg-palace.s: Nymphenburg Palace is a Baroque palace in western Munich, begun in 1664 as a summer residence for Elector Ferdinand Maria and his wife Henriette Adelaide of Savoy after the birth of their heir, Max Emanuel. Enlarged by later electors, it has a large landscaped park with…

narbonne.s: Narbonne is a city in the Aude department of southern France, near the Mediterranean coast. Founded as Narbo Martius in 118 BCE, the first Roman colony in Gaul outside Italy, it became the capital of the province of Gallia Narbonensis and stood on the Via Domitia.

nakbe.s: Nakbe is a Maya archaeological site in the Mirador Basin of northern Guatemala, about 13 kilometres south-east of El Mirador. One of the earliest Maya cities, it had large platforms and temples in the Middle Preclassic period, from about 800 BCE, among the oldest monumental…

nasrullah-khan-emir-of-bukhara.s: Nasrullah Khan was emir of Bukhara from 1827 to 1860, of the Manghit dynasty. He seized the throne after his father's death, eliminating his brothers, and spent his reign centralising power at the expense of the tribal nobility and fighting the Khanate of Kokand.

najd.s: Najd is the central plateau region of the Arabian Peninsula, today the heart of Saudi Arabia, with Riyadh as its main city. A land of oases, wadis and desert, it was the birthplace of the 18th-century reform movement of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab and the home of the successive…

nekor.s: Nekor was a town in the Rif of northern Morocco, near modern Al Hoceima, founded in the early 9th century as the capital of the Emirate of Nekor. It stood in the fertile valley of the Nekor river, a short distance from the sea, and traded with al-Andalus.

noto-sicily.s: Noto is a town in south-eastern Sicily. In the Islamic period it gave its name to the Val di Noto, one of the island's three administrative districts, and it was the last Muslim stronghold to fall to the Normans, in 1091.

noto-province.s: Noto Province was a province of Japan covering the Noto Peninsula on the Sea of Japan coast, now the northern part of Ishikawa Prefecture. In the 16th century Uesugi Kenshin invaded it and took its main castle at Nanao.

ntusi.s: Ntusi is an archaeological site in western Uganda, the remains of a large settlement occupied from about the 11th to the 15th century. Excavations have found evidence of cattle herding, grain farming, pottery and iron working, and large artificial reservoirs.

nikephoros-blemmydes.s: Nikephoros Blemmydes was a Byzantine monk, scholar and teacher in the Empire of Nicaea. He wrote textbooks on logic and physics, theological works and an autobiography, and he taught the future emperor Theodore II Laskaris.

nymphaion.s: Nymphaion was a town in western Asia Minor, east of Smyrna, now Kemalpaşa near İzmir in Turkey. The emperors of Nicaea often resided there, and John III Doukas Vatatzes built a palace whose ruins survive.

national-union-portugal.s: The National Union was the single legal political organisation of Portugal's Estado Novo, founded in 1930 by António de Oliveira Salazar. Rather than a mass party, it served to organise support for the regime and to select candidates for the National Assembly.

nannan.s: Nannan was a chief of Ezhimala on the coast of northern Kerala, known from Sangam poetry in Tamil of the early centuries CE. Poets praise his wealth, his hill fortress and his generosity, but also remember him as harsh and ruthless.

nepali-congress.s: The Nepali Congress is a social democratic political party in Nepal, formed in 1950 from earlier anti-Rana movements. With King Tribhuvan and Indian backing it helped end the rule of the Rana prime ministers in 1951, and its leader B.

negros.s: Negros is the fourth-largest island of the Philippines, in the central Visayas, divided between the provinces of Negros Occidental and Negros Oriental. From the mid-19th century its western plains became the centre of the country's sugar industry, dominated by large haciendas.

nizwa.s: Nizwa is an oasis city in the interior of Oman, at the foot of the Hajar Mountains. It was the capital of the Ibadi imamate from the 9th century and long a centre of religious scholarship, and the imams of the Ya'aruba dynasty built its massive round fort in the 17th century.

nayanars.s: The Nayanars were sixty-three Tamil poet-saints devoted to Shiva, active in south India mainly between the 6th and 8th centuries. The hymns of the greatest of them, Appar, Sambandar and Sundarar, were collected as the Tevaram and form the core of the Tirumurai, the canon of…

nanda-bayin.s: Nanda Bayin was king of the First Toungoo Empire of Burma from 1581 to 1599, the son and successor of Bayinnaung. He inherited the largest empire in the history of mainland Southeast Asia but faced revolts, and his repeated failed campaigns against Siam under Naresuan, which…

nottingham.s: Nottingham is a city in the East Midlands of England on the River Trent. The Viking Great Heathen Army wintered there in 867–868, and it became one of the Five Boroughs of the Danelaw until it was taken by Edward the Elder in 918.

nehesy.s: Nehesy was a king of the Fourteenth Dynasty of Egypt, which ruled the eastern Nile Delta in the Second Intermediate Period, and is the best-attested ruler of that line. His name means the Nubian.

neugablonz.s: Neugablonz is a district of Kaufbeuren in Bavaria founded after 1945 by German refugees expelled from Gablonz, now Jablonec nad Nisou, in Bohemia. Built on the site of a former explosives factory, it revived the glass and costume-jewellery industry of its founders' home town…

nazi-party.s: The Nazi Party, the National Socialist German Workers' Party, was the far-right party led by Adolf Hitler from 1921. Founded in 1920 from the German Workers' Party, it rose during the Depression to become the largest party in the Reichstag in 1932, and after Hitler became…

national-liberation-front-algeria.s: The National Liberation Front (FLN) is an Algerian nationalist party founded in 1954. On 1 November 1954 it launched the armed struggle that became the Algerian War of Independence against French rule, fought by its army, the ALN, and by urban networks.

noel-ballay.s: Noël Ballay was a French physician, explorer and colonial administrator. He accompanied Pierre Savorgnan de Brazza's expeditions in the Ogooué and Congo region from 1875, then served as lieutenant-governor of Gabon and from 1890 as the first governor of French Guinea, making…

nouakchott.s: Nouakchott is the capital and largest city of Mauritania, near the Atlantic coast. The French colony had been governed from Saint-Louis in Senegal, so from 1957 a new capital was built on the site of a small village for the soon-to-be independent country, planned for about…

neo-destour.s: The Neo-Destour was a Tunisian nationalist party founded at Ksar Hellal in March 1934 by Habib Bourguiba and other young members who broke with the Destour. Building a mass organisation with trade-union support, it led the struggle that won independence from France in 1956 and…

nero-claudius-drusus.s: Nero Claudius Drusus, known as Drusus the Elder, was a Roman general, stepson of the emperor Augustus and younger brother of Tiberius. From 12 to 9 BCE he led campaigns across the Rhine against the Sugambri, Chatti, Cherusci and other Germanic peoples, reaching the Elbe, and…

nihon-shoki.s: The Nihon Shoki, or Chronicles of Japan, completed in 720, is the second-oldest book of Japanese history after the Kojiki. Written in classical Chinese and compiled under Prince Toneri, it narrates events from the age of the gods to the reign of Empress Jitō.

ngungunhane.s: Ngungunhane was the last king of the Gaza kingdom in southern Mozambique, ruling from 1884. He moved his capital south to Mandlakazi in 1889 and tried to play Britain against Portugal.

nongqawuse.s: Nongqawuse was a Xhosa girl whose prophecy in 1856 started the Xhosa cattle-killing movement. She said that if the people killed their cattle and destroyed their crops, the dead would rise and the British would be swept into the sea.

north-gyeongsang-province.s: North Gyeongsang is a province in south-eastern South Korea, with its government at Andong since 2016. Its lands include Gyeongju, the old capital of Silla, the Gaya centre of Goryeong and the cities of Pohang, Gumi and Sangju.

national-university-of-cordoba.s: The National University of Córdoba is the oldest university in Argentina, founded by the Jesuits in Córdoba in 1613 and given university status in 1622. After the expulsion of the Jesuits in 1767 it passed to the Franciscans and later to the state.

napoleon-louis-bonaparte.s: Napoléon Louis Bonaparte was the son of Louis Bonaparte, King of Holland, and Hortense de Beauharnais, and the elder brother of the future Napoleon III. Made Grand Duke of Berg as a small child in 1809, he was briefly proclaimed King of Holland as Louis II when his father…

nikolai-bobrikov.s: Nikolai Bobrikov was a Russian general who served as Governor-General of Finland from 1898. He drove the Russification of the grand duchy, imposing the February Manifesto of 1899, which allowed imperial laws to override Finnish ones, the language manifesto of 1900 and a…

november-uprising.s: The November Uprising was a Polish revolt against Russian rule in Congress Poland that began in Warsaw on 29 November 1830 with an attack by officer cadets on the Belweder Palace. The Sejm deposed Nicholas I as king of Poland in January 1831, but the Polish army was defeated…

nainsukh.s: Nainsukh was an Indian painter of the Pahari school, the younger son of Pandit Seu of Guler. He worked mainly for Raja Balwant Singh of Jasrota, recording his patron's daily life in paintings of great naturalism and subtle observation.

north-cape.s: The North Cape, or Nordkapp, is a cliff on the island of Magerøya in Finnmark, northern Norway, often described as the northernmost point of Europe. Around 890 the Hålogaland chieftain Ohthere sailed round it to the White Sea and described the voyage to King Alfred of Wessex.

nagabhata-i.s: Nagabhata I was the founder of the imperial line of the Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty, ruling in western India in the mid-8th century from a base probably at Ujjain or in the Jalor region. Inscriptions credit him with repelling the Arab armies advancing from Sindh around 738,…

nahavand.s: Nahavand is a city in Hamadan province of western Iran, in the Zagros Mountains on the route between Mesopotamia and the Iranian plateau. It is known for the battle of 642 in which the Arab Muslim armies defeated the last great field army of the Sasanian Empire.

neches-river.s: The Neches River is a river of East Texas in the United States that flows south-east through the Piney Woods to Sabine Lake near the Gulf of Mexico. Its upper valley and that of its tributary, the Angelina, were the heartland of the Hasinai Caddo, among whom Spain founded its…

natchitoches-confederacy.s: The Natchitoches confederacy was one of the three Caddo confederacies, centred on the Red River in north-western Louisiana. The French founded a trading post among them in 1714, which grew into the town of Natchitoches.

natchitoches-louisiana.s: Natchitoches is a town in north-western Louisiana, founded in 1714 by the French officer Louis Juchereau de St. Denis as a trading post among the Natchitoches Caddo.

national-liberation-front-greece.s: The National Liberation Front (EAM) was the largest Greek resistance movement during the Axis occupation, founded in September 1941 under the leadership of the Communist Party of Greece. Its army, ELAS, controlled much of the mountainous interior by 1944.

nanbu-clan.s: The Nanbu clan was a Japanese warrior family of northern Mutsu, descended from the Minamoto, which ruled from Morioka as daimyo under the Tokugawa shogunate. Confirmed in its lands by Toyotomi Hideyoshi in 1590, it lost the Tsugaru region to its vassal Ōura Tamenobu, causing a…

nesactium.s: Nesactium was the chief stronghold of the Histri, an Iron Age people of Istria, near the village of Vizače east of Pula in modern Croatia. Its rich graves show contacts with Italy and the Adriatic world, and the Romans stormed it in 177 BCE.

nakijin-castle.s: Nakijin Castle is a gusuku, or Okinawan fortress, on the Motobu Peninsula of Okinawa, Japan. It was the seat of the kings of Hokuzan until Shō Hashi of Chūzan captured it in 1416, and it later served as the residence of a royal warden for the north.

nahuas.s: The Nahuas are a group of Indigenous peoples of Mexico and Central America who speak Nahuatl. In the late pre-Hispanic period they included the Mexica of the Aztec Empire, the Tlaxcalans and many other city-states of central Mexico.

nyaneka.s: The Nyaneka are a Bantu-speaking people of south-western Angola, living mainly in Huíla province. Closely related to the Nkhumbi, with whom they are often grouped as the Nyaneka-Nkhumbi, they combine cattle-keeping with farming.

norfolk.s: Norfolk is a county in East Anglia, England, with Norwich as its county town and a long coastline on the North Sea. It was the heartland of the Iceni in the Iron Age and of the Anglo-Saxon kingdom of East Anglia.

ninja.s: Ninja, or shinobi, were warriors of pre-modern Japan who specialised in espionage, scouting, infiltration and surprise attacks, especially in the Sengoku period of the 15th and 16th centuries. The best-known came from the provinces of Iga and Kōka, whose warrior leagues hired…

nsukka.s: Nsukka is a town in Enugu State, south-eastern Nigeria, in the northern part of Igboland. Its area has a long history of iron smelting and trade with the Igala kingdom to the north.

nagarjuna-sagar-dam.s: The Nagarjuna Sagar Dam is a large masonry dam on the Krishna river on the border of Telangana and Andhra Pradesh, India, built between 1955 and 1967 for irrigation and hydroelectric power. Its reservoir flooded the valley of Nagarjunakonda, site of the ancient Ikshvaku…

nagarjunakonda.s: Nagarjunakonda is a historic Buddhist site in the Krishna valley of Andhra Pradesh, India, named after the Buddhist philosopher Nagarjuna. In the 3rd and 4th centuries CE the valley held Vijayapuri, capital of the Ikshvaku dynasty, whose royal women endowed many stupas,…

neretva.s: The Neretva is a river of the western Balkans that flows about 225 kilometres from the mountains of Bosnia and Herzegovina past Mostar into the Adriatic in southern Croatia. In antiquity its valley held the Daorsi and the Roman trading town of Narona.

nicolas-perrenot-de-granvelle.s: Nicolas Perrenot de Granvelle was a lawyer from Franche-Comté who rose to become one of the chief ministers of the Emperor Charles V, serving as his keeper of the seals and principal adviser on imperial affairs from the 1530s. He built the Palais Granvelle in Besançon, now a…

nagasena.s: Nagasena was a Buddhist monk who, according to the Milindapanha, debated questions of doctrine with King Milinda, the Indo-Greek ruler Menander I, and won him over to Buddhism. His arguments, notably the image of a chariot to explain that there is no permanent self, became…

nusantara.s: Nusantara is the planned new capital of Indonesia, under construction since 2022 in East Kalimantan on the island of Borneo. The project, announced by President Joko Widodo, aims to relieve crowded and sinking Jakarta and to spread development beyond Java.

ninisina.s: Ninisina was the Mesopotamian goddess of healing and the patron deity of the city of Isin, 'Lady of Isin'. She was regarded as a physician who cured illness, and dogs were her sacred animals; excavations at her temple uncovered dog burials and figurines.

nawaz-sharif.s: Nawaz Sharif is a Pakistani industrialist and politician who served three times as prime minister, in 1990–93, 1997–99 and 2013–17. Leader of the Pakistan Muslim League (N), he ordered Pakistan's nuclear tests in 1998.

nallur.s: Nallur is a suburb of Jaffna in northern Sri Lanka that served as the royal capital of the Jaffna kingdom under the Aryacakravarti dynasty from the late 13th century until the Portuguese conquest of 1619. Its palace remains are scant, but the town is still the religious centre…

nallur-kandaswamy-kovil.s: Nallur Kandaswamy Kovil is a Hindu temple dedicated to the god Murugan at Nallur, near Jaffna in northern Sri Lanka. The original temple, linked with the kings of Jaffna, was destroyed by the Portuguese in the 17th century; the present building was raised in the 18th century…

nartiang.s: Nartiang is a village in the West Jaintia Hills of Meghalaya, north-east India, once a summer seat of the Jaintia kings. It is known for one of the largest groups of megaliths in the region: hundreds of standing stones and flat table stones raised as memorials by clans and…

nanny-of-the-maroons.s: Nanny of the Maroons was a leader of the Windward Maroons of eastern Jamaica in the early 18th century, during the First Maroon War against the British. Remembered as a spiritual leader and military strategist, she led the community at Nanny Town in the Blue Mountains.

naikda.s: The Naikda are an Adivasi community of eastern Gujarat, India, living mainly in the hills and forests of the Panchmahal and Vadodara districts, where they have traditionally farmed and gathered forest produce. Officially recognised as a Scheduled Tribe, they rose against…

nagarkurnool-district.s: Nagarkurnool is a district of southern Telangana, India, formed in 2016 from part of Mahbubnagar district. It lies along the Krishna river and includes much of the Nallamala forest and the Amrabad Tiger Reserve.

nakdong-river.s: The Nakdong River is the longest river in South Korea, flowing about 510 kilometres south through the Gyeongsang region to the sea near Busan. Its basin was home to the Gaya confederacy and the core of Silla.

narwar.s: Narwar is a town in the Shivpuri district of Madhya Pradesh, India, on the Sindh river, below a large hilltop fort. Associated in legend with King Nala of the Mahabharata, it was held by a branch of the Kachchhapaghatas and later by the Jajapellas, Tomaras, Mughals and…

nayaka.s: Nayaka, meaning leader or chief, was a title for military commanders in medieval South India. Under the Kakatiya dynasty and the Vijayanagara Empire, Nayakas held land and revenues in return for providing troops, and many later became hereditary rulers.

new-book-of-tang.s: The New Book of Tang is an official history of the Tang dynasty of China, compiled by Ouyang Xiu and Song Qi and completed in 1060. Written to replace the earlier Old Book of Tang, it is one of the Twenty-Four Histories.

nichiren.s: Nichiren was a Japanese Buddhist monk who taught that the Lotus Sutra alone held the truth and that chanting its title brought salvation. He attacked other schools and warned the Kamakura shogunate that neglect of the sutra would bring foreign invasion, a warning many saw…

narakasura.s: Narakasura is a demon king of Hindu legend, said to have ruled Pragjyotisha, the ancient name of Kamarupa in Assam. The Puranas tell how he was killed by Krishna, an event celebrated in the festival of Naraka Chaturdashi during Diwali.

nilambar.s: Nilambar was the last king of the Khen dynasty of Kamata, ruling from Kamatapur near modern Cooch Behar in the late 15th century. He controlled a large territory between the Karatoya and the Brahmaputra and resisted the Bengal Sultanate, but around 1498 Alauddin Husain Shah…

neukamerun.s: Neukamerun was the name of the territories that France ceded to Germany in 1911, after the Agadir Crisis, to enlarge the colony of Kamerun in exchange for German recognition of French control of Morocco. Taken from French Equatorial Africa, the lands gave Kamerun access to the…

nadaun.s: Nadaun is a town on the Beas river in the Hamirpur district of Himachal Pradesh, India. Under the Katoch raja Sansar Chand of Kangra in the late 18th and early 19th centuries it was a court residence, and painters working there helped create the Kangra school of miniature…

nivkh-people.s: The Nivkh are an Indigenous people of the lower Amur river and northern Sakhalin in the Russian Far East, numbering a few thousand. They traditionally lived by fishing, sea-mammal hunting and dog-sled travel, and their language is an isolate unrelated to its neighbours.

nukus.s: Nukus is the capital of the Republic of Karakalpakstan in north-western Uzbekistan, on the Amu Darya. A small settlement until the Soviet period, it replaced Turtkul as capital in 1939 and grew into an industrial city.

nanyadeva.s: Nanyadeva was the founder of the Karnat dynasty of Mithila, establishing himself in the Tirhut plain of northern Bihar around 1097. A chief of Karnata origin, he probably came north with the armies of the Chalukyas of Kalyani, and he made Simraungadh his capital.

nerik.s: Nerik was a Hittite holy city in northern Anatolia, sacred to the storm god of Nerik, usually identified with the mound of Oymaağaç near Vezirköprü. The Kaska overran it in the 15th century BCE, and for generations the Hittite kings could not hold it.

nikita-khrushchev.s: Nikita Khrushchev was leader of the Soviet Union from the mid-1950s to 1964, as first secretary of the Communist Party and, from 1958, also premier. His secret speech of 1956 denounced Stalin and began a partial thaw, while he crushed the Hungarian uprising and brought the…

nasir-khan-i-of-kalat.s: Mir Nasir Khan I was Khan of Kalat from 1749 to 1794 and the most powerful ruler of the khanate. After a failed war in 1758 he accepted the overlordship of Ahmad Shah Durrani while keeping internal independence.

nodira.s: Nodira was an Uzbek poet and the wife of Umar Khan of Kokand. She wrote in Chagatai Turkic and Persian, and after her husband's death in 1822 she had great influence during the reign of her son Muhammad Ali Khan, supporting poets and founding schools.

nuapada-district.s: Nuapada is a district in western Odisha, India, bordering Chhattisgarh, with its headquarters at the town of Nuapada. It was created in 1993 from part of Kalahandi district.

nongkrem-dance.s: The Nongkrem dance, Shad Nongkrem, is the main annual religious festival of the Khasi people of Meghalaya, India, held in autumn at Smit, the seat of the Syiem of Khyrim. A thanksgiving for the harvest and a prayer for prosperity, it includes the sacrifice of a goat and dances…

north-ossetia-alania.s: North Ossetia–Alania is a republic of the Russian Federation in the North Caucasus, with its capital at Vladikavkaz on the Terek river. Most of its people are Ossetians, an Iranian-speaking people descended from the medieval Alans, whose name the republic added to its official…

nicholas-i-mystikos.s: Nicholas I Mystikos was Patriarch of Constantinople from 901 to 907 and again from 912 until his death. He was deposed for opposing the fourth marriage of Emperor Leo VI, then restored, and led the regency for the young Constantine VII in 913–914, when he crowned Simeon I of…

ntare-v-of-burundi.s: Ntare V, born Charles Ndizeye, was the last king of Burundi. He deposed his father Mwambutsa IV in July 1966 and was crowned, but in November of the same year his prime minister, Captain Michel Micombero, overthrew him and proclaimed a republic.

ntare-i-of-burundi.s: Ntare I Rushatsi is remembered in Burundian tradition as the founder of the kingdom's royal dynasty, usually placed in the late 17th century. Accounts describe him uniting chiefdoms in the hills east of Lake Tanganyika and establishing the sacred kingship of the mwami.

narmada-river.s: The Narmada is a river of central India, flowing about 1,300 kilometres westwards from Amarkantak in Madhya Pradesh through a rift valley between the Vindhya and Satpura ranges to the Gulf of Khambhat. It has long marked the traditional boundary between northern India and the…

nafana-people.s: The Nafana are a people of west-central Ghana and eastern Côte d'Ivoire who speak a Senufo language. They founded the kingdom of Banda in the hills north-west of the Bono state, close to the trading town of Begho on the gold and kola routes, and they remain the main people of…

neuschwanstein-castle.s: Neuschwanstein Castle is a 19th-century palace built for King Ludwig II of Bavaria on a rugged hill above the village of Hohenschwangau near Füssen. Begun in 1869 as a romantic imitation of a medieval castle and inspired by the operas of Richard Wagner, it was still unfinished…

nyatapola-temple.s: Nyatapola is a five-storeyed pagoda temple in Taumadhi Square, Bhaktapur, in the Kathmandu Valley of Nepal. Built by King Bhupatindra Malla in 1702, it stands about 30 metres high on a five-tiered plinth flanked by pairs of guardian figures, and is the tallest temple in the…

nicomedes-i-of-bithynia.s: Nicomedes I was king of Bithynia in north-western Anatolia from about 278 to 255 BCE. To fight his brother and the Seleucid king Antiochus I, he invited bands of Celtic warriors across the Bosporus as mercenaries in 278 BCE; they later settled in central Anatolia as the…

nicomedia.s: Nicomedia was an ancient city at the head of the Gulf of Izmit in north-western Anatolia, founded in 264 BCE by Nicomedes I as the capital of Bithynia. Under Rome it became the chief city of the province of Bithynia, and Diocletian made it his main residence and an eastern…

new-bussa.s: New Bussa is a town in Niger State, Nigeria, built in the 1960s to house the people of old Bussa and nearby villages displaced by the reservoir of the Kainji Dam. It is the seat of the Emir of Borgu and the main town of the Kainji Lake area, with its national park and…

norodom-ranariddh.s: Norodom Ranariddh was a Cambodian prince and politician, a son of King Norodom Sihanouk and leader of the royalist FUNCINPEC party. After FUNCINPEC won the UN-supervised elections of 1993 he became first prime minister, sharing power with Hun Sen as second prime minister.

neriglissar.s: Neriglissar was king of Babylon from 560 to 556 BCE. A leading official and son-in-law of Nebuchadnezzar II, he took the throne after the murder of Amel-Marduk, which he probably organised.

na-nyagse.s: Na Nyagse was a ruler of Dagbon, in present-day northern Ghana, remembered in tradition as the king who created the kingdom in its lasting form, probably in the 15th century. Leading Dagomba horsemen, he conquered the peoples of the White Volta basin, killed or displaced many…

nioro-du-sahel.s: Nioro du Sahel is a town in the Kayes Region of western Mali, close to the border with Mauritania. It became the capital of the Bambara kingdom of Kaarta, was taken by the Toucouleur leader El Hadj Umar Tall in 1854 and served as a stronghold of his empire until the French…

nanaya.s: Nanaya was a Mesopotamian goddess of love and war, worshipped from the 3rd millennium BCE and closely linked with Inanna-Ishtar. Her cult spread east to Elam, Iran and Central Asia, where she was venerated at temples in Elymais and Susa, and later as Nana among the Kushans and…

neoptolemus.s: Neoptolemus, also called Pyrrhus, was in Greek mythology the son of Achilles, who joined the Trojan War after his father's death and killed King Priam during the sack of Troy. Legend made him the founder of the Molossian royal house of Epirus through his union with Andromache,…

ngbanya.s: The Ngbanya are the ruling estate of Gonja in northern Ghana, descendants of the Mande horsemen who conquered the region under Ndewura Jakpa in the 17th century. They hold the chieftaincies of Gonja's divisions, while Muslim scholars and the older commoner peoples form the…

nimlot-of-hermopolis.s: Nimlot, also read Namart, was a king of Hermopolis in Middle Egypt in the later 8th century BCE, during the break-up of Egypt's Third Intermediate Period. He joined Tefnakht of Sais against the Kushite king Piye, who besieged Hermopolis and forced his surrender.

nayaks-of-kandy.s: The Nayaks of Kandy were the last royal dynasty of Sri Lanka, ruling the Kingdom of Kandy from 1739 to 1815. Of south Indian origin and related by marriage to the Nayak rulers of Madurai, they came to the throne when the last Sinhalese king died without a son, and became…

ndembu-people.s: The Ndembu, or Southern Lunda, are a people of north-western Zambia and neighbouring parts of Angola and the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Their chiefdoms, headed by senior titles such as Kanongesha, were founded by Lunda nobles who moved south from the court of the Mwata…

namgyal-dynasty.s: The Namgyal dynasty ruled the kingdom of Ladakh from the 15th century until its conquest by the Dogras of Jammu in the 1830s and 1840s. Its kings, notably Sengge Namgyal, built Leh Palace and patronised Buddhist monasteries such as Hemis, while balancing between Tibet, the…

nokalakevi.s: Nokalakevi is an archaeological site in western Georgia, identified with Archaeopolis, the chief fortress and capital of the kingdom of Lazica in late antiquity. Its walls, gates and churches date mainly from the 4th to 6th centuries, when it was a key stronghold during the…

ningthouja-dynasty.s: The Ningthouja dynasty, of the Mangang clan of the Meitei, ruled Manipur from the founding traditionally dated to 33 CE until the kingdom merged with India in 1949. Its kings, starting with Nongda Lairen Pakhangba, gradually brought the other Meitei clans of the Imphal valley…

nongda-lairen-pakhangba.s: Nongda Lairen Pakhangba is the first king of Manipur in the royal chronicle, the Cheitharol Kumbaba, which dates his accession to 33 CE. He is regarded as founder of the Ningthouja dynasty and of the Meitei state centred on Kangla in the Imphal valley.

nyau.s: Nyau is a secret society of the Chewa people of Malawi, Zambia and Mozambique, whose initiated men perform masked dances at funerals, initiations and memorial rites. The dancers represent ancestral spirits and animals, and the society historically balanced the power of chiefs.

nyabingi.s: Nyabingi is a spirit cult of the borderlands of Rwanda and south-western Uganda, centred on a female spirit associated in tradition with a queen of the kingdom of Ndorwa. Priestesses and mediums of the cult gained wide political influence, and between about 1910 and 1928…

nepalese-civil-war.s: The Nepalese Civil War was an armed conflict from 1996 to 2006 between the Communist Party of Nepal (Maoist), led by Pushpa Kamal Dahal (Prachanda), and the Nepali monarchy and government. Some 17,000 people were killed.

norici.s: The Norici were a Celtic people of the eastern Alps, in what is now Carinthia and Styria in Austria. In the 2nd century BCE they led a union of tribes that formed the kingdom of Noricum, which traded its famous iron with Rome.

northern-isles.s: The Northern Isles are the archipelagos of Orkney and Shetland off the north coast of Scotland. Settled by Norse Vikings from the 9th century, they formed the Earldom of Orkney under Norwegian overlordship.

ngonnso.s: Ngonnso is the founding queen of the Nso kingdom in Nso tradition, said to have been a Tikar princess who left her homeland with followers in about the late 14th century. Her name is borne by the Nso people and their language, Lamnso.

nehale-lyampingana.s: Nehale lyaMpingana was ruler of eastern Ondonga, one of the Ovambo kingdoms of northern Namibia, from 1884 until his death in 1908. On 28 January 1904, during the Herero uprising, his warriors attacked the German fort at Namutoni and forced the small garrison to abandon it.

namibia.s: Namibia is a country in south-western Africa, bordering the Atlantic, Angola, Botswana and South Africa, with its capital at Windhoek. It was the German colony of South West Africa from 1884, where the Herero and Nama genocide took place in 1904–08, and was ruled by South…

namutoni.s: Namutoni is a fort on the eastern edge of the Etosha Pan in northern Namibia, built by German colonial troops at a spring around 1900. On 28 January 1904 Ovambo warriors of Nehale lyaMpingana attacked it, and its small garrison abandoned the fort.

ndonga-dialect.s: Oshindonga is a dialect of the Ovambo language spoken by the Ndonga people of northern Namibia. Finnish Lutheran missionaries made it a written language in the late 19th century, and Martti Rautanen completed a translation of the Bible into it.

nea-paphos.s: Nea Paphos was a harbour city on the south-west coast of Cyprus, founded in the late 4th century BCE by Nicocles, the last king of Paphos. It became the capital of Cyprus under the Ptolemies and the Romans, and the Acts of the Apostles places Paul's meeting with the governor…

nicocles-of-paphos.s: Nicocles was the last king of Paphos in Cyprus, ruling in the late 4th century BCE. He founded the harbour city of Nea Paphos and built sanctuaries.

nestor.s: Nestor is a legendary king of Pylos in Greek mythology, son of Neleus. In Homer's Iliad he is the oldest of the Greek leaders at Troy, a wise counsellor fond of recalling his youthful deeds, and in the Odyssey he receives Telemachus at Pylos.

nyiginya-dynasty.s: The Nyiginya dynasty was the royal line of the Kingdom of Rwanda, whose kings bore the title mwami. Court traditions recorded by Alexis Kagame trace it back many centuries, though historians date its rise near Lake Muhazi to the 16th or 17th century.

nicocreon.s: Nicocreon was the last king of Salamis in Cyprus, ruling from about 332 BCE. He supported Alexander the Great and then Ptolemy I in the wars of the Successors, and Ptolemy made him general of Cyprus in 312 BCE.

nikola-pasic.s: Nikola Pašić was a Serbian statesman and a founder of the People's Radical Party who served many times as prime minister of Serbia and of the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes. He led Serbia through the Balkan Wars and the First World War and signed the Corfu Declaration…

nibelungenlied.s: The Nibelungenlied is a Middle High German epic poem written around 1200, probably in the region of Passau. It tells of the hero Siegfried, his murder at the Burgundian court of Worms, and the revenge of his widow Kriemhild, which ends in the destruction of the Burgundians at…

norse-gaels.s: The Norse–Gaels were people of mixed Scandinavian and Gaelic descent and culture who emerged in Ireland, the Hebrides and western Scotland from the 9th century. They dominated the Kingdom of the Isles and the Isle of Man, and their Gaelic name, Gall-Ghàidheil, survives in…

neptune.s: Neptune was the Roman god of fresh water and the sea, identified with the Greek Poseidon. His festival, the Neptunalia, was held in Rome on 23 July.

noviomagus-reginorum.s: Noviomagus Reginorum was the Roman town at Chichester in West Sussex, capital of the civitas of the Regni. It grew up after the conquest of 43, probably under the client king Togidubnus, and had a forum, baths, an amphitheatre and later stone walls.

nukualofa.s: Nukuʻalofa is the capital of Tonga, on the north coast of the main island of Tongatapu. George Tupou I made it his capital after uniting the islands in the 1840s, and it holds the Royal Palace of 1867 and the royal tombs.

nendrum-monastery.s: Nendrum is an early Christian monastic site on Mahee Island in Strangford Lough, County Down, Northern Ireland, traditionally founded by Saint Mochaoi in the 5th century. Its remains include three concentric stone enclosures, the stump of a round tower and a church.

najera.s: Nájera is a town in La Rioja, northern Spain, on the Najerilla river. Taken from the Muslims in the 920s, it became a royal seat of the kingdom of Pamplona, which was often called the kingdom of Nájera in the 11th century.

naaba-kango.s: Naaba Kango was king of Yatenga, a Mossi kingdom in the north of present-day Burkina Faso, in the second half of the 18th century. Driven out in a succession conflict, he regained the throne with the help of Bambara troops from Ségou.

ngaruawahia.s: Ngāruawāhia is a town in the Waikato region of New Zealand's North Island, at the meeting of the Waikato and Waipā rivers. In 1858 Pōtatau Te Wherowhero was installed there as the first Māori King, and it became the centre of the King movement.

north-island-main-trunk.s: The North Island Main Trunk is the railway line linking Wellington and Auckland in New Zealand, completed in 1908. Its central section ran through the King Country, which was closed to Europeans until Māori leaders allowed surveys in the 1880s.

nihal-chand.s: Nihal Chand was an Indian painter who worked at the court of Kishangarh in Rajasthan in the 18th century, chiefly under Raja Sawant Singh. He is credited with creating the Kishangarh style of miniature painting, with its elongated figures, wide landscapes and scenes of the…

nair.s: The Nair are a Hindu community of Kerala, India, who formed the warrior and landholding class of the region's kingdoms, serving as soldiers, administrators and local chiefs. They were known for their martial training in kalaripayattu and for matrilineal inheritance, in which…

naimbana.s: Naimbana was king of Koya, a Temne state on the Sierra Leone estuary, in the late 18th century. In 1788 he confirmed the grant of land on the peninsula made by his subordinate King Tom to British abolitionists for the Province of Freedom, the origin of Freetown.

north-macedonia.s: North Macedonia is a landlocked country in the central Balkans, with its capital at Skopje. Part of the Ottoman Empire until 1912, the region was divided after the Balkan Wars, and its northern part became a republic of Yugoslavia in 1944.

nsheng.s: Nsheng, also known as Mushenge, is the royal capital of the Kuba kingdom in the Kasai region of the Democratic Republic of the Congo. As the seat of the king, or nyimi, and his council of titled officials, it was a centre of Kuba art, including carved royal statues, masks and…

nandi-hinduism.s: Nandi is the sacred bull who serves as the mount and gatekeeper of the Hindu god Shiva. Statues of a seated Nandi face the sanctum in most Shiva temples, and the bull appears on the coins of many dynasties devoted to Shiva, from the Kushans and Kushano-Sasanians to the Hindu…

ningirsu.s: Ningirsu was a Sumerian warrior god, the patron of the city of Girsu and of the state of Lagash, associated with thunderstorms, floods and the fertility of the fields. The rulers of Lagash presented themselves as his stewards, and his main temple, the Eninnu, was rebuilt by…

namara-inscription.s: The Namara inscription is an Old Arabic text carved in Nabataean script on a tomb lintel at al-Namara in southern Syria and dated to 328 CE. It commemorates Imru al-Qays, son of Amr, as king of all the Arabs, and is usually linked to the early Lakhmid rulers of al-Hira.

naab.s: The Naab is a river in the Upper Palatinate in Bavaria, Germany, and a left tributary of the Danube. It is formed by the meeting of the Waldnaab and Haidenaab and flows south for about 100 kilometres to join the Danube just above Regensburg.

naplanum.s: Naplanum was an Amorite chief traditionally counted as the first king of Larsa in southern Mesopotamia, ruling around 2025 BCE after the decline of the Third Dynasty of Ur. Little is known of him beyond the king lists, and he probably held only Larsa and its surroundings.

nellore.s: Nellore is a city in Andhra Pradesh, India, on the Penna river near the Bay of Bengal coast. In the 12th and 13th centuries it was the seat of the Telugu Chodas, and the Pandya king Jatavarman Sundara Pandya I performed a victory coronation there.

nguyen-canh-chan.s: Nguyễn Cảnh Chân was a Vietnamese general of the Later Tran resistance against the Ming occupation of Vietnam after 1407. With Dang Tat he commanded the army that defeated the Ming at Bo Co in 1408.

nghe-an-province.s: Nghệ An is a province of north-central Vietnam, stretching from the South China Sea coast to the Lao border, with its capital at Vinh. Long a frontier region between Dai Viet and Champa, it was a base for resistance movements against Chinese and later French rule, and the Tay…

nearchus.s: Nearchus was a Cretan-born officer and boyhood friend of Alexander the Great. In 325 and 324 BCE he commanded the fleet that sailed from the mouth of the Indus along the coasts of the Arabian Sea and Persian Gulf to Mesopotamia, while Alexander marched through the Gedrosian…

national-pact.s: The National Pact is an unwritten agreement made in 1943 by Lebanon's first president, Bechara El Khoury, a Maronite, and prime minister, Riad Al Solh, a Sunni Muslim. Christians agreed not to seek Western protection and Muslims not to seek union with Syria, and the main…

nicopolis-epirus.s: Nicopolis was a city in Epirus, on the peninsula north of modern Preveza in western Greece, founded by Octavian (Augustus) to commemorate his victory over Antony and Cleopatra at Actium in 31 BCE. Augustus moved the people of nearby towns, including Ambracia and much of…

nicopolis-lesser-armenia.s: Nicopolis was a city in Lesser Armenia, in modern north-eastern Turkey, founded by Pompey on the site of his victory over Mithridates VI of Pontus in 66 BCE and settled with his wounded and veteran soldiers and local people. It became a regional centre of Roman Armenia Minor…

nin.s: Nin is a small town on a lagoon islet in northern Dalmatia, Croatia, near Zadar. As Aenona it was a Liburnian and then a Roman town, and in the early Middle Ages it was a seat of the Croatian dukes and kings and, from the 9th century, of a bishopric whose bishop Gregory of Nin…

narendradeva.s: Narendradeva was a Licchavi king of Nepal who regained the throne in the 640s with Tibetan help after a period of exile in Tibet. His reign saw close ties with both Tibet and Tang China: Chinese envoys visited his court, and Nepalese troops joined a Tibetan expedition in 648…

nepal-sambat.s: Nepal Sambat is a lunar calendar era of Nepal that begins in 879 CE. Used for centuries in inscriptions, documents and coins of the Thakuri and Malla periods, it remains the traditional calendar of the Newar people of the Kathmandu Valley, whose new year falls in October or…

neville-family.s: The Nevilles were a powerful English noble family from the north of England, earls of Westmorland and Salisbury. Through his marriage to the Beauchamp heiress, Richard Neville, Earl of Warwick, known as the Kingmaker, gained the lordship of Glamorgan and became the leading…

new-ross.s: New Ross is a town on the River Barrow in County Wexford, in south-east Ireland. It was developed around 1200 by William Marshal, lord of Leinster, as a port, and became one of the leading harbours of medieval Ireland.

nafplio.s: Nafplio, historically Nauplia, is a port town in the Argolid in the north-eastern Peloponnese, overlooked by the fortresses of Acronauplia and Palamidi. In the Middle Ages it was held by Leo Sgouros, then by Frankish lords and from 1388 by Venice, which made it a principal…

northern-sporades.s: The Northern Sporades are a group of Greek islands in the north-western Aegean Sea, off the coasts of Thessaly and Euboea. The main islands are Skiathos, Skopelos, Alonnisos and Skyros.

nereid-monument.s: The Nereid Monument is a temple-shaped tomb built at Xanthos in Lycia around 390–380 BCE, probably for the dynast Arbinas (Erbbina). It sets an Ionic Greek temple on a tall Lycian podium, with statues of sea nymphs (Nereids) between its columns and friezes of battle and court…

nung-people.s: The Nùng are a Tai-speaking people of north-eastern Vietnam, especially the border provinces of Cao Bằng and Lạng Sơn, closely related to the Tày and to the Zhuang of China. In the 11th century the Nùng chief Nùng Trí Cao rebelled against both Đại Việt and Song China.

nalanda.s: Nalanda was a great Buddhist monastery and centre of learning in Bihar, eastern India, which flourished from the 5th to the 12th century. Supported by the Gupta kings, Harsha and the Pala Empire, it drew students from across Asia, including the Chinese pilgrims Xuanzang and…

nsenga.s: The Nsenga are a Bantu-speaking people of eastern Zambia and neighbouring parts of Mozambique and Zimbabwe, living mainly in the Luangwa valley. In the 19th century they suffered raids for ivory and captives by Chikunda warbands and by the Ngoni of Mpezeni.

narmadapuram-district.s: Narmadapuram district, known as Hoshangabad district until 2022, is a district of Madhya Pradesh in central India along the Narmada river. Its headquarters, the town of Hoshangabad (now Narmadapuram), was named after Hoshang Shah of the Malwa Sultanate.

namdhari.s: The Namdharis, also called Kukas, are a Sikh sect of the 19th-century Punjab, given its form by Satguru Ram Singh from 1857. They stress simple living, vegetarianism and the recitation of God's name, and they boycotted British goods and institutions.

newar-people.s: The Newars are the historic inhabitants of the Kathmandu Valley in Nepal, speaking Nepal Bhasa (Newari), a Sino-Tibetan language, and following both Hindu and Buddhist traditions. Under the Malla kings their cities of Kathmandu, Patan and Bhaktapur flourished as centres of…

nalerigu.s: Nalerigu is a town in northern Ghana, capital of the North East Region and the seat of the Nayiri, paramount chief of the Mamprusi. The Mamprugu court moved there from Gambaga around 1700 under Na Atabia.

nanumba.s: Nanumba is a traditional kingdom of the Nanumba people in northern Ghana, with its capital at Bimbilla. Mole-Dagbani tradition holds that it was founded by a descendant of Na Gbewaa, making it a sister state of Mamprugu and Dagbon.

nakba.s: The Nakba, Arabic for catastrophe, is the Palestinian name for the flight and expulsion of roughly 700,000 Palestinian Arabs from their homes during the war surrounding Israel's creation in 1948, and for the destruction of hundreds of their villages. It made refugees of more…

noorbakhshia.s: The Noorbakhshia is a Sufi order and Muslim community that traces its teaching to Sayyid Muhammad Nurbakhsh (1393–1464), a Persian Sufi of the Kubrawiya tradition. Spread to Kashmir and Baltistan in the late 15th century by Mir Shams al-Din Iraqi, it combines Sufi and Shia…

nikolaus-ludwig-von-zinzendorf.s: Count Nikolaus Ludwig von Zinzendorf was a German Pietist nobleman who in 1722 allowed Protestant refugees from Moravia to settle on his estate in Upper Lusatia, where they founded Herrnhut. He led the renewed Moravian Church, became its bishop and sent missionaries to the…

nasr-al-dawla-ibn-marwan.s: Nasr al-Dawla Ahmad ibn Marwan was the Kurdish Marwanid ruler of Diyar Bakr from 1011 to 1061, ruling from Mayyafariqin. During his fifty-year reign he kept peace with the Byzantine Empire, the Fatimids and the rising Seljuks through diplomacy and gifts.

nyanja-people.s: The Nyanja are a Bantu-speaking people living around Lake Malawi and the Shire valley in Malawi, Mozambique and Zambia, closely related to the Chewa. Their language, Chinyanja or Chichewa, is widely spoken across the region.

nannus.s: Nannus was, according to the foundation legend of Massalia, king of the Segobrigii, a people living near the site of Marseille. In the story told by the Roman historian Justin, he welcomed Greek settlers from Phocaea, and when his daughter Gyptis chose their leader Protis as…

nice.s: Nice is a city on the Mediterranean coast of south-eastern France and capital of the Alpes-Maritimes department. It began as Nikaia, a Greek trading post founded by Massalia, while the Romans built Cemenelum on the hill above.

niassa-province.s: Niassa is the largest and most thinly populated province of Mozambique, in the north-west of the country between Lake Malawi and the Lugenda river, with its capital at Lichinga. Its highlands were home to Yao chiefdoms such as that of Mataka in the nineteenth century.

najaf.s: Najaf is a city in central Iraq, south of Kufa, built around the shrine of Ali ibn Abi Talib, the fourth caliph and first Shia imam. It is one of the holiest cities of Shia Islam and for centuries has been a major centre of Shia learning, with its great seminaries and the vast…

north-american-free-trade-agreement.s: The North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) was a treaty between Canada, Mexico and the United States that created one of the world's largest free trade areas. Signed in 1992, it came into force on 1 January 1994, the day the Zapatista rising began in Chiapas.

napirisha.s: Napirisha, 'great god', was one of the chief deities of ancient Elam in south-western Iran, worshipped with the goddess Kiririsha and the god Inshushinak of Susa. In the Middle Elamite period he headed the state pantheon, and the king Untash-Napirisha, whose name honours him,…

naucratis.s: Naucratis was a Greek trading city in the western Nile Delta of Egypt, founded in the 7th century BCE. Under Pharaoh Amasis in the 6th century it became the only port where Greek merchants were allowed to trade, and cities such as Miletus, Samos, Aegina, Chios and Mytilene…

neleus-son-of-codrus.s: Neleus, son of the Athenian king Codrus, was the legendary founder of Miletus. Greek tradition held that after his father's death he quarrelled with his brother over the kingship and led a party of Ionian settlers across the Aegean around 1000 BCE.

novae.s: Novae was a Roman legionary fortress and town on the south bank of the Danube near modern Svishtov in northern Bulgaria. Founded in the 1st century CE, it was long the base of the First Italian Legion and part of the Danube frontier of the province of Moesia.

nemocon.s: Nemocón is a town on the high plateau north of Bogotá in Cundinamarca, Colombia. With nearby Zipaquirá it was one of the main salt-producing centres of the Muisca, whose brine-boiled salt was traded widely for gold, cotton and other goods.

nasiriyah.s: Nasiriyah is a city on the Euphrates in southern Iraq and the capital of Dhi Qar Governorate. It was founded in the early 1870s by Nasir Pasha al-Sa'dun, chief of the Muntafiq confederation, as the seat of the new Ottoman sanjak, and named after him.

najran.s: Najran is an oasis city in south-western Saudi Arabia near the Yemeni border. In late antiquity it was a major Christian centre of Arabia, whose community was massacred by the Himyarite king Dhu Nuwas in about 523.

naypyidaw.s: Naypyidaw is the capital of Myanmar, a planned city built in secret by the military government in central Myanmar from about 2002. The government moved there from Yangon in November 2005, and its name, meaning 'abode of kings', was announced in 2006.

ne-win.s: Ne Win was a Burmese general and dictator who seized power in a coup in 1962 and ruled Burma for twenty-six years. His Burma Socialist Programme Party pursued the 'Burmese Way to Socialism', nationalising the economy, expelling many foreigners and isolating the country, which…

national-league-for-democracy.s: The National League for Democracy is a political party of Myanmar founded in 1988 after the pro-democracy uprising, led by Aung San Suu Kyi. It won the 1990 election, which the military ignored, and the elections of 2015 and 2020.

niigata.s: Niigata is a port city on the Sea of Japan coast of Honshu, at the mouth of the Shinano River, and the capital of Niigata Prefecture. It was one of the five ports opened to foreign trade under the treaties of 1858, actually opening in 1869.

niigata-prefecture.s: Niigata Prefecture is a prefecture of Japan on the Sea of Japan coast of Honshu, formed after the Meiji Restoration from the old province of Echigo and the island of Sado. Watered by the Shinano, Japan's longest river, it is one of the country's main rice-growing regions.

nagod.s: Nagod is a town in Satna district of Madhya Pradesh, India, between Rewa and Panna. It became the capital of the Parihar Rajput state of Nagod in the 18th century, replacing the earlier seat of Unchahara, and remained so until the state joined Vindhya Pradesh in 1948.

nagpur-province.s: Nagpur Province was a province of British India formed after the East India Company annexed the Maratha kingdom of Nagpur under the doctrine of lapse in 1853. Governed from Nagpur by a commissioner, it covered much of the former Bhonsle territory in central India.

nantes.s: Nantes is a city of western France on the lower Loire, about 50 km from the Atlantic. Beginning as the Gallo-Roman port of Condevicnum, or Portus Namnetum, of the Namnetes, it became a bishopric and a seat of the dukes of Brittany.

natal-province.s: Natal Province was one of the four provinces of the Union of South Africa and later the Republic of South Africa, formed from the Colony of Natal in 1910 and governed from Pietermaritzburg. Its population was mainly Zulu, with a large community of Indian origin and an…

navajo-code-talkers.s: The Navajo Code Talkers were Navajo men recruited by the US Marine Corps in the Second World War to send radio messages in a code based on the Navajo language. Some 400 served in the Pacific, including at Iwo Jima, and the Japanese never broke the code.

nayarit.s: Nayarit is a state on the Pacific coast of western Mexico, with its capital at Tepic. It takes its name from Nayar, a Cora ruler whose remains were venerated in the mountains of the Sierra del Nayar.

nazca-lines.s: The Nazca Lines are huge geoglyphs scraped into the desert surface between the Nazca and Palpa valleys of southern Peru, made mostly between about 500 BCE and 500 CE by the Paracas and Nazca cultures. They include hundreds of straight lines and geometric shapes and some 70…

nyabela.s: Nyabela was king of the Ndzundza Ndebele in present-day Mpumalanga, South Africa. In 1882 he sheltered the Pedi rebel Mampuru II and refused to hand him over to the South African Republic, whose forces besieged his stronghold at KwaMaza for months.

negara-bali.s: Negara is a town in western Bali, Indonesia, the capital of Jembrana Regency. It grew as the seat of the kingdom of Jembrana, and Bugis settlers from Sulawesi founded the nearby Muslim community of Loloan in the 17th and 18th centuries.

niagara-escarpment.s: The Niagara Escarpment is a long ridge of resistant dolomitic limestone running from New York State through southern Ontario and around the Great Lakes to Wisconsin. The Niagara River plunges over it at Niagara Falls.

niagara-river.s: The Niagara River flows about 58 km north from Lake Erie to Lake Ontario, forming part of the border between the United States and Canada. Midway along its course it drops over Niagara Falls.

noumea.s: Nouméa is the capital and largest city of New Caledonia, a French territory in the south-west Pacific. Founded in 1854 as the military post of Port-de-France, it was renamed in 1866 and grew as the administrative centre, the port of the penal colony and a nickel-processing town.

noumea-accord.s: The Nouméa Accord, signed on 5 May 1998 by the French state and New Caledonia's independence and loyalist movements, set out a gradual transfer of powers to the territory over twenty years. It recognised Kanak identity, created a New Caledonian citizenship and provided for up…

nagriamel.s: Nagriamel is a political and customary movement founded on Espiritu Santo in the New Hebrides in the mid-1960s by Jimmy Stevens and Chief Paul Buluk. It demanded the return of uncultivated land claimed by European planters and defended customary ways of life.

new-netherland-company.s: The New Netherland Company was a Dutch trading company chartered by the States General in 1614 with a monopoly of the fur trade in North America between latitudes 40 and 45 degrees north. It built Fort Nassau on Castle Island near present-day Albany.

ngo-xuong-ngap.s: Ngo Xuong Ngap was the eldest son of Ngo Quyen, founder of the Ngo dynasty in Vietnam. When Duong Tam Kha usurped the throne in 944 he went into hiding, and after his brother Ngo Xuong Van overthrew the usurper in 950 the two ruled jointly, Ngap with the title Thien Sach Vuong.

nizar-ibn-al-mustansir.s: Nizar ibn al-Mustansir was the eldest son of the Fatimid caliph al-Mustansir. On his father's death in 1094 the vizier al-Afdal passed him over in favour of his younger brother al-Musta'li.

nogais.s: The Nogais are a Turkic people of the North Caucasus and the steppes north of the Caspian and Black Seas, traditionally named after Nogai, a 13th-century commander of the Golden Horde. From the 15th century they formed the Nogai Horde, a nomadic confederation between the Volga…

nocera-inferiore.s: Nocera Inferiore is a town in the province of Salerno, Campania, Italy, in the Sarno valley. It stands on the site of ancient Nuceria Alfaterna, head of a league of towns that became an ally of Rome after 308 BCE; Hannibal destroyed it in 216 BCE.

nueces-river.s: The Nueces River is a river of southern Texas that flows south-east into Nueces Bay and Corpus Christi Bay on the Gulf of Mexico. Under Spanish rule it marked the approximate northern limit of the province of Nuevo Santander.

nyasaland-african-congress.s: The Nyasaland African Congress was the first nationwide African political organisation in the British protectorate of Nyasaland, founded in 1944.
