It campaigned against the Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland and, after Hastings Kamuzu Banda took the lead in 1958, was banned…

nyungu-ya-mawe.s: Nyungu ya Mawe was a Nyamwezi warlord of the 19th century in what is now western Tanzania. A member of the ruling house of Unyanyembe, he broke with his kin and the Arab traders of Tabora in the 1860s and from around 1870 used bands of ruga-ruga to conquer the Kimbu chiefdoms…

ninomiya-sontoku.s: Ninomiya Sontoku was a Japanese agrarian reformer and moral philosopher from Sagami Province. Rising from a ruined farming family, he restored villages for the Ōkubo lords of Odawara and later for the shogunate through careful accounting, frugality, mutual aid and land…

nyaya.s: Nyaya is one of the six orthodox schools of Hindu philosophy, concerned above all with logic, the means of valid knowledge and the theory of argument. Its founding text, the Nyaya Sutras, is attributed to Gautama and dates from the early centuries CE.

napo-river.s: The Napo River is a tributary of the Amazon that rises on the slopes of the Ecuadorian Andes and flows south-east through Ecuador and Peru to join the Amazon below Iquitos. Francisco de Orellana followed it downstream in 1541–1542 on the first European descent of the Amazon.

national-party-uruguay.s: The National Party, whose members are known as the Blancos, is one of Uruguay's two traditional parties, founded in 1836 by supporters of President Manuel Oribe. Rooted in rural and conservative interests, it fought the Colorados in the Guerra Grande of 1839–1851 and in later…

narses.s: Narses was an Armenian eunuch who rose to high office at the court of Justinian I and became one of his leading generals. He helped suppress the Nika riots in 532 and, in command of the Gothic War from 551, defeated Totila at Taginae and Teia at Mons Lactarius.

nagato-province.s: Nagato Province was an old province of Japan at the western tip of Honshu, now the western part of Yamaguchi Prefecture, including the strait port of Shimonoseki. It was held by the Ōuchi and then the Mōri, whose Chōshū Domain combined Nagato with neighbouring Suō under the…

nagoya.s: Nagoya is the capital of Aichi Prefecture and one of the largest cities of Japan. It grew from the castle built from 1610 on Tokugawa Ieyasu's orders, to which the town of Kiyosu was moved, and served as the seat of the Owari Tokugawa, the senior Gosanke house.

nuno-alvares-botelho.s: Nuno Álvares Botelho was a Portuguese naval commander in Asia who briefly shared the government of Portuguese India. In 1629 he led the fleet that relieved Malacca from the great siege by Iskandar Muda of Aceh, destroying the Acehnese armada with help from Johor and Patani.

nuruddin-ar-raniri.s: Nuruddin ar-Raniri was a Muslim scholar from Ranir in Gujarat who worked at the court of Aceh from 1637 to 1644. Under Sultan Iskandar Thani he wrote the Bustan al-Salatin and other Malay works, and he condemned the mystical teachings of Hamzah Fansuri and Syamsuddin of Pasai…

nabis.s: Nabis was the last ruler of independent Sparta, from 207 to 192 BCE. He carried out radical reforms, freeing helots, redistributing land and enlarging the citizen body, and gave Sparta its first full city walls.

nicocles-of-sicyon.s: Nicocles was tyrant of Sicyon in 251 BCE, ruling for only four months after the murder of his predecessor Paseas. He was overthrown in a night attack by the young exile Aratus, who recalled the exiles and brought Sicyon into the Achaean League as its first non-Achaean member.

nart-sagas.s: The Nart sagas are a body of epic tales from the North Caucasus, told among the Ossetians, Circassians, Abkhaz, Abazins, Karachays, Balkars, Chechens and Ingush. They recount the deeds of the Narts, a race of heroes including Sosruquo, Batradz and the wise matriarch Satanaya,…

nannienus.s: Nannienus was a Roman general in Gaul in the later fourth century. As count he fought Saxon raiders in 370, and in 378 he shared command with the Frankish king Mallobaudes in the emperor Gratian's victory over the Alemannic Lentienses at Argentovaria in Alsace, where the…

nova-reforma.s: The Nova Reforma, or New Reform, was a reform of the institutions of Andorra approved by its co-princes in 1866 and led by the syndic Guillem d'Areny-Plandolit. It replaced the narrow oligarchic system of government with a Consell General elected by the heads of household of…

nestor-kirchner.s: Néstor Kirchner was an Argentine Peronist politician, governor of Santa Cruz province, who served as president from 2003 to 2007 after the crisis of 2001. His government restructured the defaulted debt, paid off the IMF and presided over rapid growth driven by commodity…

nunca-mas.s: Nunca Más ('Never Again') is the report of Argentina's National Commission on the Disappearance of Persons, CONADEP, chaired by the writer Ernesto Sabato and delivered to President Raúl Alfonsín in September 1984. It documented nearly 9,000 disappearances and hundreds of…

national-autonomist-party.s: The National Autonomist Party was the conservative party that dominated Argentine politics from 1874 until 1916, led above all by Julio Argentino Roca. It ruled through an alliance of provincial governors and limited, often fraudulent elections, and it presided over the…

naresuan.s: Naresuan was king of Ayutthaya from 1590 to 1605. Raised as a hostage at the Burmese court after Ayutthaya fell in 1569, he renounced allegiance to Burma in 1584, defeated a series of Burmese invasions, and in 1593 won the Battle of Nong Sarai.

neungsan-ri.s: Neungsan-ri is a site in Buyeo, South Korea, with a group of royal tombs of the Sabi period of Baekje (538–660) and the remains of a temple next to them. In 1993 excavators of the temple site found the Gilt-bronze Incense Burner of Baekje, a masterpiece of East Asian metalwork.

ning-an.s: Ning'an is a city in the south-east of Heilongjiang province, China, on the Mudan River. Nearby are the ruins of Sanggyeong, the Upper Capital of Balhae from the eighth century until 926.

nalikwanda.s: The Nalikwanda is the royal barge of the Litunga, the king of the Lozi of Barotseland in western Zambia. Painted in black and white stripes and topped by a model elephant, it is paddled by about a hundred men during the Kuomboka ceremony, when the Litunga moves from Lealui on…

nalolo.s: Nalolo is a settlement on the Barotse floodplain of the upper Zambezi in Western Province, Zambia, south of Mongu. It is the seat of the Mulena Mukwae, the royal princess who rules the southern part of Barotseland, with her own court and council, under the Litunga.

ngambela.s: The Ngambela is the chief councillor, or prime minister, of the Lozi kingdom of Barotseland. He leads the kuta, the council of titled officials, and is regarded as the representative of the people, entitled to speak for them and to oppose the Litunga.

nkoya-people.s: The Nkoya are a Bantu people of central western Zambia, between the Kafue and the Barotse floodplain. Their own kingdoms paid tribute to the Lozi of Barotseland in the nineteenth century, and under colonial rule much of their land was placed under Lozi authority, a…

nasiruddin-mahmud-shah.s: Nasiruddin Mahmud Shah was sultan of Bengal from about 1435 to 1459, a descendant of Shamsuddin Ilyas Shah who restored the Ilyas Shahi dynasty after the end of Raja Ganesha's line. His reign was peaceful; he rebuilt Gaur as the capital and built mosques, bridges and…

nasiruddin-nusrat-shah.s: Nasiruddin Nusrat Shah was sultan of Bengal from 1519 to 1533, the son of Alauddin Husain Shah. He supported the Afghan chiefs of Bihar against the Mughals and lost to Babur at the Battle of Ghaghra in 1529, then made peace.

nymphaeum-crimea.s: Nymphaeum was an ancient Greek city on the Crimean shore of the Kerch Strait, south of Panticapaeum, founded in the sixth century BCE. It paid tribute as a member of the Athenian-led Delian League in the fifth century BCE before passing under the control of the Bosporan kings.

non-cooperation-movement.s: The Non-cooperation movement was a mass campaign led by Mahatma Gandhi and the Indian National Congress between 1920 and 1922 against British rule in India. Launched after the Rowlatt Act and the Jallianwala Bagh massacre and in alliance with the Khilafat movement, it called…

naval-defence-act-1889.s: The Naval Defence Act 1889 was a British law that formally adopted the two-power standard, under which the Royal Navy was to be at least as strong as the next two largest navies combined, then those of France and Russia. It provided about 21.5 million pounds for the…

nahj-al-balagha.s: The Nahj al-Balagha, 'The Peak of Eloquence', is a collection of sermons, letters and sayings attributed to Ali ibn Abi Talib, the fourth caliph and first Shia Imam. It was compiled in Baghdad by al-Sharif al-Radi and completed around 1009.

normandy-landings.s: The Normandy landings of 6 June 1944, known as D-Day, were the Allied amphibious and airborne invasion of German-occupied France that opened Operation Overlord. American, British and Canadian forces landed on five beaches, code-named Utah, Omaha, Gold, Juno and Sword, after…

national-policy.s: The National Policy was the economic programme introduced by John A. Macdonald's Conservative government in Canada in 1879.

nato.s: The North Atlantic Treaty Organization is a military alliance founded by the North Atlantic Treaty, signed in Washington on 4 April 1949 by twelve countries of North America and western Europe, including Canada. Its members pledge that an armed attack on one is an attack on all.

northern-cape.s: The Northern Cape is the largest province of South Africa by area and the least populous, created in 1994 from the north-western part of the former Cape Province. Its capital is Kimberley, centre of the diamond rush of the 1870s.

nij.s: Nij is a large village in the Qabala district of northern Azerbaijan and the main centre of the Udi people. Their language, Udi, belongs to the Lezgic group and is the descendant of the language of Caucasian Albania, which scholars were able to read through comparison with it.

nala-dynasty.s: The Nala dynasty ruled parts of central India, around the Bastar region of modern Chhattisgarh and neighbouring Odisha, from about the fifth century. Known from coins and inscriptions, the Nalas fought the Vakatakas and were among the powers defeated by Kirtivarman I of the…

nikolai-yevdokimov.s: Count Nikolai Yevdokimov was a Russian general who rose from the ranks to command in the North Caucasus. After the surrender of Imam Shamil in 1859 he directed the final conquest of the western Caucasus, in which Circassian villages were systematically destroyed and their…

nyangwe.s: Nyangwe is a town on the Lualaba River in Maniema in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo. In the nineteenth century it was a major market of the Swahili-Arab trade in ivory and slaves, where David Livingstone witnessed a massacre in 1871.

nile-valley.s: The Nile Valley is the narrow strip of fertile land along the River Nile through Sudan and Egypt, watered by its annual flood. It supported the civilisations of ancient Egypt and Nubia and the later states of Kush, the Christian Nubian kingdoms and the Funj.

nasir-ad-din-qabacha.s: Nasir al-Din Qabacha was a Turkic slave commander of the Ghurids who made himself ruler of Multan and Uch in Sindh after the death of Muhammad of Ghor in 1206. A rival of the Delhi sultan Iltutmish, he held out for two decades, but when Iltutmish besieged Uch in 1228 he…

nizamuddin-auliya.s: Nizamuddin Auliya was a Sufi saint of the Chishti order who lived in Delhi for most of his life under the Delhi Sultanate. Teaching love, humility and service to the poor, he drew followers from every class, including the poet Amir Khusrau.

niels-juel.s: Niels Juel was a Danish-Norwegian admiral, born in Christiania, who led the navy of Denmark-Norway in the Scanian War of 1675–1679. He won a series of victories over the Swedish fleet, above all the Battle of Køge Bay in 1677, which gave Denmark command of the Baltic.

notre-dame-la-grande.s: Notre-Dame-la-Grande is a Romanesque collegiate church in Poitiers, in western France, built mainly in the late eleventh and twelfth centuries. Its west front, covered with carved figures of prophets, apostles and scenes of the Annunciation and Nativity, is one of the…

nivelles.s: Nivelles is a town in Walloon Brabant, Belgium, south of Brussels. It grew around an abbey founded about 650 by Itta, widow of Pepin of Landen, and her daughter Saint Gertrude, whose Romanesque collegiate church, consecrated in 1046, still dominates the town.

north-brabant.s: North Brabant is a province in the south of the Netherlands, with 's-Hertogenbosch as its capital and Eindhoven, Tilburg and Breda as its largest cities. It corresponds roughly to the northern part of the medieval Duchy of Brabant, which the Dutch Republic conquered in the…

nantes-cathedral.s: Nantes Cathedral, dedicated to Saints Peter and Paul, is the Gothic cathedral of Nantes in western France, begun in 1434 under Duke John V of Brittany and completed only in 1891. It contains the Renaissance tomb of Duke Francis II of Brittany and his wife Marguerite of Foix by…

nicolas-rolin.s: Nicolas Rolin was chancellor of the Burgundian state under Philip the Good from 1422 until shortly before his death in 1462. A lawyer from Autun, he directed the government of lands stretching from Burgundy to Holland and negotiated the Treaty of Arras of 1435.

nicolas-remy.s: Nicolas Rémy was a magistrate and procurator-general of the Duchy of Lorraine and one of the most notorious witch-hunters of early modern Europe. He claimed to have sent some 900 people to their deaths for witchcraft over fifteen years.

naviglio-grande.s: The Naviglio Grande is a canal in Lombardy, about 50 km long, that carries water from the Ticino to Milan. Begun in the late twelfth century as an irrigation channel and made navigable in the thirteenth, it irrigated the surrounding plain and brought marble for Milan Cathedral…

niccolo-piccinino.s: Niccolò Piccinino was an Italian condottiere from Perugia, a pupil of Braccio da Montone, who led the armies of Filippo Maria Visconti, duke of Milan, from the 1420s to the 1440s. He fought Venice, Florence and the Papacy and was defeated by the Florentines and papal forces at…

norman-architecture.s: Norman architecture is the Romanesque style of building developed in Normandy in the eleventh century and carried to England after 1066 and to southern Italy and Sicily. It is marked by massive walls, round arches, cylindrical piers and early rib vaults, as seen at the abbeys…

netherlands-trading-society.s: The Netherlands Trading Society (Nederlandsche Handel-Maatschappij) was a trading and financial company founded in 1824 on the initiative of King William I to revive Dutch commerce. Under the Cultivation System it held the monopoly on shipping and selling in the Netherlands…

netherlands-new-guinea.s: Netherlands New Guinea was the western half of New Guinea, which the Netherlands kept when it transferred sovereignty over the rest of the East Indies to Indonesia in 1949. The Dutch prepared it for separate self-government, but Indonesian military pressure and American…

napir-asu.s: Napir-Asu was a queen of Elam in the fourteenth century BCE, wife of King Untash-Napirisha. She is known chiefly from her life-size bronze statue found at Susa in 1903, cast over a solid core and weighing about 1,750 kilograms, now in the Louvre.

naum-of-ohrid.s: Naum of Ohrid (c. 830–910) was a Slavonic scholar and one of the disciples of Cyril and Methodius expelled from Moravia in 885–886.

norddeutscher-lloyd.s: Norddeutscher Lloyd was a shipping company founded in Bremen in 1857. Operating from Bremerhaven, it carried millions of emigrants to the United States and became one of the largest shipping companies in the world, winning the Blue Riband with liners such as the Kaiser Wilhelm…

national-liberation-army-algeria.s: The National Liberation Army (ALN) was the armed wing of the Algerian FLN during the war of independence of 1954–1962. It fought a guerrilla war inside Algeria while large forces were held in Tunisia and Morocco, cut off by the fortified Morice and Challe lines.

nghe-tinh-soviets.s: The Nghệ-Tĩnh Soviets were a peasant uprising in the provinces of Nghệ An and Hà Tĩnh in central Vietnam in 1930–1931, organised with the help of the new Indochinese Communist Party during the Depression. Villagers set up local councils, seized land and stopped paying taxes.

norodom-of-cambodia.s: Norodom was King of Cambodia from 1860 to 1904. Under pressure from Siam and Vietnam, he accepted a French protectorate in 1863, and a convention imposed in 1884 handed most real power to French officials.

naju.s: Naju is a city in South Jeolla province in south-western South Korea. In the early tenth century Wang Geon seized it for Taebong, and in 1011 King Hyeonjong of Goryeo fled there when the Khitan burned Kaegyong.

neris.s: The Neris is a river of Belarus and Lithuania, about 510 kilometres long, known in Belarus as the Viliya. It rises in Belarus, flows through Vilnius and joins the Neman at Kaunas.

nassau-family-pact.s: The Nassau Family Pact was a succession agreement concluded in 1783 between the branches of the House of Nassau. It provided that their lands would pass to the other branch if one line died out in the male line.

narasimha-i-hoysala.s: Narasimha I was king of the Hoysala dynasty from 1152 to 1173, the son and successor of Vishnuvardhana. He inherited a large and wealthy kingdom but lacked his father's energy, and the Hoysalas remained in the shadow of the Kalachuris who had seized the Western Chalukya…

narasimha-ii-hoysala.s: Narasimha II was king of the Hoysala dynasty from 1220 to 1235, the son of Veera Ballala II. He intervened repeatedly in the Tamil country to support the weakened Chola king Rajaraja III, freeing him from the Kadava chief Kopperunchinga, and established Hoysala influence along…

narasimha-iii-hoysala.s: Narasimha III was king of the Hoysala dynasty who ruled the Karnataka homeland from Dwarasamudra, while his half-brother Ramanatha held the Tamil territories. The division led to rivalry and war between the brothers.

nripa-kama-ii.s: Nripa Kama II was one of the earliest Hoysala chiefs known from inscriptions, ruling a small territory in the Malnad hills of Karnataka around Sosevur in the early 11th century. He fought the Cholas and their allies and acted as a subordinate of larger powers.

nasir-jung.s: Nasir Jung was a son of Asaf Jah I who succeeded his father as Nizam of Hyderabad in 1748. Backed by the British, he fought the claims of his nephew Muzaffar Jung and the French in the Carnatic.

northern-circars.s: The Northern Circars were a coastal region of eastern India, along the Bay of Bengal in present-day Andhra Pradesh and southern Odisha, made up of several districts of the Deccan. The Nizam of Hyderabad assigned them to the French in 1753, the British took them from the French…

nahdlatul-ulama.s: Nahdlatul Ulama (NU) is an Indonesian Islamic organisation founded in 1926 by Hasyim Asy'ari and other religious scholars of East Java. It defends traditional Sunni scholarship and local religious practice, and is rooted in the pesantren boarding schools of rural Java.

north-china.s: North China is the region of China north of the Huai River and the Qinling Mountains, centred on the Yellow River basin and the North China Plain. Farmed mainly for wheat and millet, it was the cradle of early Chinese states and long the seat of government.

namhansanseong.s: Namhansanseong is a mountain fortress south-east of Seoul, rebuilt in its present form in the 1620s as an emergency refuge for the Joseon court. During the Manchu invasion of 1636 King Injo took shelter there and withstood a siege of some forty-seven days before surrendering…

nongsa-jikseol.s: The Nongsa jikseol ('Straight Talk on Farming') is a Korean farming manual compiled in 1429 by order of King Sejong. Officials gathered the methods of experienced farmers in each province so that agriculture could follow Korean soils and climate rather than Chinese handbooks.

nuwa-mbaguta.s: Nuwa Mbaguta was the enganzi, or chief minister, of Ankole in the early colonial period. He backed the young Kahaya II in the succession conflict after Ntare V's death in 1895 and signed the Ankole Agreement of 1901 with the British.

ntare-v.s: Ntare V was Omugabe, or king, of Nkore in the late nineteenth century, coming to power after a war of succession following the death of Mutambuka. Under him Nkore reached its greatest extent, extending its influence over Buhweju, Igara and the remnants of Mpororo.

namugongo.s: Namugongo is a place north-east of Kampala in Uganda, a former royal execution ground. On 3 June 1886, on the orders of Kabaka Mwanga II, many young Christian converts were burned alive there.

nyangire-revolt.s: The Nyangire revolt was a protest movement in Bunyoro in 1907 against the Ganda chiefs that the British had appointed over Nyoro districts. Its name means "I refuse".

nyamutukura-kyebambe-iii.s: Nyamutukura Kyebambe III was omukama of Bunyoro in the late eighteenth and early nineteenth centuries. Near the end of his reign, around 1830, his son Prince Kaboyo Olimi broke away to found the Kingdom of Toro, taking rich pastures and the salt lakes of the south-west.

niels-bohr.s: Niels Bohr was a Danish physicist who proposed the Bohr model of the atom in 1913, applying quantum ideas to the structure of electrons. He received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1922.

nikos-kazantzakis.s: Nikos Kazantzakis was a Greek writer and philosopher from Crete. He wrote poetry, plays, travel books and novels, among them Zorba the Greek (1946), Christ Recrucified and The Last Temptation of Christ, which the Orthodox and Catholic churches condemned.

nazareth.s: Nazareth is a city in Lower Galilee in northern Israel, known in Christian tradition as the childhood home of Jesus. Its Basilica of the Annunciation stands where the angel Gabriel is said to have appeared to Mary.

narayanhiti-palace.s: Narayanhiti Palace in Kathmandu was the main residence of the kings of Nepal. The present building, designed by the American architect Benjamin Polk, was completed around 1970 on the site of an older palace.

nuwakot.s: Nuwakot is a historic hill town north-west of Kathmandu, commanding the route between the Kathmandu Valley and Tibet. Prithvi Narayan Shah of Gorkha captured it in 1744 as the first step in his encirclement of the valley, and he built a seven-storey palace there.

nuno-alvares-pereira.s: Nuno Álvares Pereira was a Portuguese general who served John I as constable of Portugal. During the crisis of 1383–1385 he defeated the Castilians at Atoleiros in 1384, Aljubarrota in 1385 and Valverde, securing Portuguese independence.

nguyen-trai.s: Nguyễn Trãi was a Vietnamese scholar, poet and strategist who served as Lê Lợi's chief adviser in the war against Ming occupation. He wrote the Bình Ngô đại cáo, the proclamation of victory of 1428, and poetry in both classical Chinese and vernacular Nôm.

national-womens-monument.s: The National Women's Monument is a memorial in Bloemfontein, South Africa, unveiled on 16 December 1913. It commemorates the Boer women and children, some 26,000 by common estimate, who died in British concentration camps during the Second Boer War.

nga-yaman-kan.s: Nga Yaman Kan was the governor of Pegu (Bago) in Lower Burma under the Pagan Kingdom, a boyhood companion of King Sawlu. In 1084 he rebelled, defeated the royal army and killed the captured Sawlu.

narasimhavarman-i.s: Narasimhavarman I, known as Mamalla, 'great wrestler', was king of the Pallava dynasty from about 630 to 668. He defeated the Chalukya king Pulakeshin II and in 642, with his general Paranjothi, captured the Chalukya capital Vatapi, taking the title Vatapikonda.

nao-chi.s: Nao Chi was a general of the State of Chu during the Warring States period. In 284 BCE, when a coalition led by Yue Yi of Yan overran Qi, Chu sent him with an army nominally to help King Min of Qi, who made him chief minister.

nicolaus-von-jeroschin.s: Nicolaus von Jeroschin was a priest of the Teutonic Order and a Middle High German poet in Prussia. In the 1330s he translated Peter of Dusburg's Latin Chronicle of the Prussian Land into German verse as the Kronike von Pruzinlant, adding some material of his own.

narciso-claveria.s: Narciso Clavería was a Spanish general and Governor-General of the Philippines from 1844 to 1849. In 1848 he led an expedition with steam gunboats that destroyed the strongholds of the Balangingi raiders in the Sulu archipelago.

national-museum-of-indonesia.s: The National Museum of Indonesia, popularly called Museum Gajah, is the main archaeological and historical museum of Indonesia, in Jakarta. It grew from the collections of the Batavian Society of Arts and Sciences, founded in 1778, and holds stone inscriptions, Hindu-Buddhist…

national-party-of-suriname.s: The National Party of Suriname (NPS) is a political party founded in 1946 that long represented mainly the Afro-Surinamese Creole population. Under Johan Adolf Pengel and Henck Arron it led governments in the 1960s and 1970s and took Suriname to independence in 1975.

narrative-of-a-five-years-expedition.n: Narrative of a Five Years Expedition against the Revolted Negroes of Surinam
narrative-of-a-five-years-expedition.s: The Narrative of a Five Years Expedition against the Revolted Negroes of Surinam is John Gabriel Stedman's account of his service against the maroons of Suriname from 1773 to 1777, published in London in 1796. Illustrated with engravings by William Blake and others, it…

ngwane-v.s: Ngwane V, also known as Bhunu, was king of Swaziland from 1889, ruling under the regency of his mother Labotsibeni until 1895, and died in December 1899. His reign saw the kingdom pass under the administration of the South African Republic by the Swaziland Convention of 1894.

ndvungunye.s: Ndvungunye was a king of the Dlamini-led chiefdom that became the Swazi Kingdom, succeeding his father Ngwane III and ruling in the region of the Pongola river in the late eighteenth and early nineteenth centuries. His chiefdom remained small among the competing Nguni…

ndwandwe.s: The Ndwandwe were a Nguni kingdom between the Pongola and Mfolozi rivers in what is now KwaZulu-Natal, the strongest power in the region in the 1810s under their king Zwide. They pressed the Swazi northwards and killed the Mthethwa ruler Dingiswayo, but were defeated by…

ngwenya-mine.s: The Ngwenya Mine, in the hills of north-western Eswatini near the border with South Africa, contains ancient workings for haematite and specularite, minerals used as pigment and cosmetic. Dates from Lion Cavern suggest mining there tens of thousands of years ago, making it one…

national-redoubt-switzerland.s: The National Redoubt was the Swiss defence plan announced by General Henri Guisan in July 1940, after the fall of France left Switzerland almost surrounded by the Axis. The army was to give up the populated lowlands and hold a fortified Alpine core, centred on the fortresses…

nagda-rajasthan.s: Nagda is an ancient town beside Bagela Lake near Kailashpuri, about 20 km north of Udaipur in Rajasthan. It was the early capital of the Guhila rulers of Mewar until the Delhi sultan Iltutmish sacked it in the 1220s.

nathdwara.s: Nathdwara is a town in the Rajsamand district of Rajasthan, about 45 km north of Udaipur, which grew around the temple of Shrinathji. The image of Krishna was brought there in 1672 from the Mathura region, to protect it from Aurangzeb's hostility, under the protection of…

national-resistance-army.s: The National Resistance Army was the armed wing of Yoweri Museveni's National Resistance Movement, which waged a guerrilla war, the Bush War, against the governments of Milton Obote and Tito Okello from 1981. Growing from a small band of fighters, it took Kampala in January…

natives-land-act-1913.s: The Natives Land Act of 1913 was a law of the Union of South Africa that barred Africans from buying or renting land outside designated reserves, which then covered about 7 per cent of the country. It ended African sharecropping on white-owned farms in much of the country and…

northern-england.s: Northern England, or the North of England, is the northern part of England, from the Scottish border to the Midlands, including cities such as Manchester, Liverpool, Leeds, Sheffield and Newcastle. The heartland of the Industrial Revolution, with cotton, wool, coal, steel and…

northern-ireland-assembly.s: The Northern Ireland Assembly is the devolved legislature of Northern Ireland, created under the Good Friday Agreement of 1998 and meeting at Stormont in Belfast. Its executive must share power between unionist and nationalist parties, and the Assembly has been suspended…

northcote-trevelyan-report.s: The Northcote–Trevelyan Report of 1854, written by Stafford Northcote and Charles Trevelyan, recommended that the British home civil service be recruited by open competitive examination and promoted by merit rather than patronage. Its proposals were introduced gradually, with…

nonconformism.s: Nonconformism is the term for the Protestant churches in England and Wales that did not conform to the established Church of England, such as the Baptists, Congregationalists, Methodists, Presbyterians and Quakers. Long subject to legal restrictions, Nonconformists gained full…

nathan-prophet.s: Nathan was a prophet at the court of King David according to the Hebrew Bible. He conveyed God's promise of an enduring dynasty to David, rebuked him with a parable for his adultery with Bathsheba and the killing of Uriah, and, with Bathsheba, secured the succession of Solomon…

new-deal.s: The New Deal was the series of programmes, reforms and public works launched by President Franklin D. Roosevelt between 1933 and 1939 in response to the Great Depression.

nineteenth-amendment-to-the-united-state.n: Nineteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution
nineteenth-amendment-to-the-united-state.s: The Nineteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution, ratified in August 1920, prohibits the federal government and the states from denying citizens the right to vote on account of sex. It was the culmination of the women's suffrage movement that had begun at the Seneca…

national-museum-of-iraq.s: The National Museum of Iraq, or Iraq Museum, in Baghdad holds one of the world's most important collections of Mesopotamian antiquities from Sumerian, Akkadian, Babylonian and Assyrian sites. Founded from collections assembled under Gertrude Bell in the 1920s, it was looted…

narasa-nayaka.s: Narasa Nayaka was a general of the Vijayanagara Empire and the father of Krishnadevaraya. After the death of Saluva Narasimha he acted as regent for the young Saluva heir and was the real ruler of the empire from about 1491 until his death in 1503, campaigning against the…

nevryuy.s: Nevryuy was a Mongol commander of the Golden Horde who in 1252 led a punitive expedition into north-eastern Rus' against Grand Prince Andrei Yaroslavich of Vladimir. His army defeated Andrei near Pereslavl-Zalessky and ravaged the area, and Andrei fled to Sweden.

nagavarma-ii.s: Nagavarma II was a Kannada poet and grammarian of the twelfth century who served at the court of the Western Chalukya king Jagadhekamalla II. His Karnataka Bhashabhushana, a grammar of Kannada written in Sanskrit, together with his works on prosody, vocabulary and poetics,…

noin-ula.s: Noin-Ula (Noyon Uul) is a group of elite Xiongnu burial mounds in the hills north of Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia. First excavated by Pyotr Kozlov's expedition in 1924–1925, its tombs preserved woollen carpets, embroidered textiles, Chinese silks and lacquerware, which are among the…

nongsang-jiyao.s: The Nongsang jiyao ('Essentials of Agriculture and Sericulture') is a Chinese agricultural handbook compiled by the Yuan government's Office for the Stimulation of Agriculture and issued in 1273. Drawing on earlier treatises, it covered grain farming, silkworm raising,…

neopalatial-period.s: The Neopalatial or New Palace period is the high point of Minoan civilisation on Crete, from about 1700 to 1450 BCE, when the palaces of Knossos, Phaistos, Malia and Zakros were rebuilt on a grander scale and Minoan art, trade and influence spread across the Aegean. It ended…

nikolaos-platon.s: Nikolaos Platon was a Greek archaeologist who excavated the Minoan palace of Zakros in eastern Crete from 1961, finding one of the few palaces never looted, with its treasury of stone ritual vessels intact. He was director of the Heraklion museum and devised the division of…

neumarkt-in-der-oberpfalz.s: Neumarkt in der Oberpfalz is a town in the Upper Palatinate, Bavaria, south-east of Nuremberg. In the 15th century it was the residence of Palatine princes, first of Count Palatine John and then, from 1448, of the Palatinate-Mosbach line.

neuburg-an-der-donau.s: Neuburg an der Donau is a town on the Danube in Bavaria, Germany. From 1505 it was the capital of the principality of Palatinate-Neuburg, created for the grandsons of Duke George of Bavaria-Landshut.

narseh.s: Narseh was king of the Sasanian Empire from 293 to 302, a son of Shapur I. He seized the throne from Bahram III and recorded his victory in the Paikuli inscription, which lists the vassal kings who supported him.

nanterre.s: Nanterre is a town west of Paris and the prefecture of the Hauts-de-Seine department. Excavations since the 1990s have uncovered a large Gallic settlement of the 3rd to 1st centuries BCE there, which some archaeologists propose as the main centre of the Parisii.

nicaea.s: Nicaea, modern İznik in north-western Turkey, was an ancient and Byzantine city on the eastern shore of Lake Ascania. It hosted the First Council of Nicaea in 325, which produced the Nicene Creed, and the Second Council in 787.

neolithic.s: The Neolithic, or New Stone Age, is the period in which human communities adopted farming, the herding of domesticated animals and settled village life while still using stone tools. It began in the Fertile Crescent around 10,000 BCE and spread over the following millennia…

nikola-petkov.s: Nikola Petkov was a Bulgarian politician, leader of the Bulgarian Agrarian National Union and of the opposition to communist rule after the Second World War. A minister in the Fatherland Front government of 1944–45, he broke with the communists and led the opposition in the…

narragansett-people.s: The Narragansett are an Algonquian-speaking Native American people of what is now Rhode Island, around Narragansett Bay. In the 17th century they were one of the most powerful nations of southern New England, sold land to Roger Williams for Providence in 1636 and fought beside…

nazrin-shah-of-perak.s: Nazrin Shah is the Sultan of Perak, Malaysia, who succeeded his father Sultan Azlan Shah in 2014. Before his accession he served for many years as Raja Muda, the heir to the throne, and he holds a doctorate in political economy from Harvard University.

nedong.s: Nedong is a district in the Yarlung valley of the Lhoka region of central Tibet, now part of the city of Shannan. From the 1350s it was the seat of the Phagmodrupa rulers, who governed most of central Tibet from their palace there after Changchub Gyaltsen overthrew the Sakya…

nimbalkar.s: The Nimbalkars are a Maratha family who ruled the jagir and later princely state of Phaltan in the Satara region of Maharashtra. Claiming to have held Phaltan since the late 13th century, they are counted among the oldest Maratha houses and served the Deccan sultanates, the…

nakhon-ratchasima.s: Nakhon Ratchasima, commonly called Korat, is a city in north-eastern Thailand and the capital of the country's largest province, on the south-western edge of the Khorat Plateau. Founded as a fortified Siamese frontier town in the 17th century, it was the gateway to the Lao and…

novilara-stele.s: The Novilara stele is an inscribed sandstone slab found in the 19th century at Novilara, near Pesaro in the northern Marche, Italy. Its text, written in a variant of the Etruscan-derived alphabet, is in a language known as North Picene, which remains undeciphered and may not…

norfolk-island.s: Norfolk Island is a small island in the South Pacific between Australia, New Zealand and New Caledonia, now an external territory of Australia. Settled by the British in 1788, it served as a harsh penal colony until 1855.

nero.s: Nero was Roman emperor from 54 to 68 CE, the last of the Julio-Claudian dynasty, adopted heir of Claudius. His reign saw the revolt of Boudica in Britain, the settlement with Parthia that placed Tiridates on the Armenian throne, the Great Fire of Rome in 64 and the persecution…

nogat.s: The Nogat is a distributary of the Vistula in northern Poland, about 62 kilometres long, which branches off the main river and flows north-east past Malbork into the Vistula Lagoon. It bounded the land of the Prussian Pomesanians, and the Teutonic Order built its chief castle,…

natwarsinhji-bhavsinhji.s: Natwarsinhji Bhavsinhji was the last ruling Maharaja of Porbandar in Kathiawar, from 1908 until the state joined India in 1948. A keen cricketer, he captained the Indian team on its tour of England in 1932, the first by an official Indian side, although he stood down for the…

national-liberation-front-of-angola.s: The National Liberation Front of Angola (FNLA) is an Angolan nationalist movement led for decades by Holden Roberto, with its base among the Bakongo of the north. Formed from earlier Bakongo movements and renamed in 1962, it fought Portuguese rule from bases in Zaire after the…

nicholas-of-cusa.s: Nicholas of Cusa was a German philosopher, theologian and cardinal, author of On Learned Ignorance. A reformer at the Council of Basel who later sided with the pope, he became bishop of Brixen in 1450, where his efforts to recover church rights led to bitter conflict with Duke…

notger.s: Notger was bishop of Liège from 972 to 1008 and the founder of the prince-bishopric of Liège. A Swabian cleric loyal to the Ottonian emperors, he received the county of Huy in 985 and other secular rights, rebuilt Liège with new walls and churches, and made its schools famous…

nicholas-of-amsdorf.s: Nicholas of Amsdorf was a German Lutheran theologian and a close colleague of Martin Luther at Wittenberg. In 1542 the Elector of Saxony installed him as bishop of Naumburg against the chapter's Catholic choice, Julius von Pflug, and Luther consecrated him, but he was driven…

naumburg-cathedral.s: Naumburg Cathedral, dedicated to Saints Peter and Paul, is the cathedral of Naumburg in Saxony-Anhalt, Germany, built mainly in the 13th century. Its west choir holds twelve life-size statues of the cathedral's founders, among them Uta and Ekkehard, by the Naumburg Master.

naumburg-master.s: The Naumburg Master is the name given to an anonymous sculptor and architect, trained in northern France, who worked at Mainz, Naumburg and Meissen in the mid-13th century. His statues of the founders in the west choir of Naumburg Cathedral, made around 1250, are among the…

nedersticht.s: The Nedersticht ("lower bishopric") was the western part of the secular territory of the prince-bishops of Utrecht, around the city of Utrecht, roughly the present Dutch province of Utrecht. It was separated from the eastern Oversticht by the lands of Guelders.

new-athos.s: New Athos (Novy Afon) is a small town on the Black Sea coast of Abkhazia, north-west of Sukhumi. Above it stand the ruins of the medieval fortress of Anacopia.

naples.s: Naples is the largest city of southern Italy, on the Bay of Naples in Campania. Founded by Greek settlers from Cumae as Neapolis, it kept its Greek character under Rome, and in the early Middle Ages it was a self-governing Byzantine duchy.

narshakhi.s: Narshakhi (Abu Bakr Muhammad Narshakhi) was a historian from the Bukhara oasis who in 943 or 944 wrote a History of Bukhara in Arabic for the Samanid ruler Nuh I. The work survives only in a shortened Persian translation of 1128 with later additions.

nis.s: Niš is a city in southern Serbia on the Nišava river, one of the oldest cities of the Balkans. As Roman Naissus it was the birthplace of Constantine the Great.

niccolo-paganini.s: Niccolò Paganini was an Italian violinist and composer from Genoa, the most celebrated virtuoso of his age. From 1805 to 1809 he served at the court of Elisa Bonaparte in Lucca, before touring Italy and, from 1828, the rest of Europe, where his technique and stage presence…

niksic.s: Nikšić is the second-largest city of Montenegro, on a karst plain in the west of the country. Known in the Middle Ages as Onogošt, it was an Ottoman fortress town until Montenegro captured it in 1877, a gain confirmed by the Congress of Berlin in 1878.

neuchatel.s: Neuchâtel is a city in western Switzerland on the north shore of Lake Neuchâtel, capital of the canton of the same name. First recorded in 1011, it was ruled by its counts and later the Orléans-Longueville family, and from 1707 by the kings of Prussia as princes.

novosil.s: Novosil is a small town in Oryol Oblast, Russia, on the Zusha river. First mentioned in the 12th century, it became the senior seat of the Upper Oka principalities, held by descendants of Mikhail of Chernigov, until it was ruined in the 14th century and its princes moved their…

niketas-choniates.s: Niketas Choniates was a Byzantine official and historian. His History covers the years 1118 to 1206 and is the main Greek source for the reigns of the Komnenian and Angelos emperors, the Bulgarian revolt of the Asen brothers and the Fourth Crusade.

nordwestmecklenburg.s: Nordwestmecklenburg is a rural district in the north-west of the German state of Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, on the Baltic coast and the border with Schleswig-Holstein. Formed in 1994, it has its seat in the Hanseatic town of Wismar.

narapati-i-of-ava.s: Narapati I was King of Ava in Upper Burma from 1442 until his death. His reign was largely peaceful, though he faced rebellions and conflicts on the frontiers with Ming China and the Shan states.

naqada.s: Naqada is a town on the west bank of the Nile in Upper Egypt, north of Luxor. Nearby lie the ancient town of Nubt and large prehistoric cemeteries excavated by Flinders Petrie in the 1890s, which gave their name to the Naqada culture of about 4000 to 3000 BCE, the predynastic…

nekhen.s: Nekhen, known to the Greeks as Hierakonpolis, was an ancient city on the west bank of the Nile in southern Upper Egypt and one of the largest settlements of the Predynastic Naqada period. It was the cult centre of the falcon god Horus and a seat of early kings of Upper Egypt.

narmer-palette.s: The Narmer Palette is a carved siltstone palette of about 3100 BCE found in the temple of Hierakonpolis (Nekhen) in 1897–1898. It shows King Narmer wearing the white crown of Upper Egypt on one side and the red crown of Lower Egypt on the other, smiting an enemy and inspecting…

new-hampshire-grants.s: The New Hampshire Grants were land grants made between 1749 and 1764 by Governor Benning Wentworth in the territory west of the Connecticut River, which New York also claimed. In 1764 the Crown ruled for New York, leading to conflict with the settlers, who organised the Green…

noemvriana.s: The Noemvriana were the events of 1 December 1916 (18 November Old Style) in Athens, when Greek royalist troops and militias clashed with British and French forces landed to enforce Allied demands on King Constantine I. The Allies withdrew after losses, and royalists then…

national-consultative-assembly.s: The National Consultative Assembly, known as the Majlis, was the parliament of Iran from 1906 to 1979. Created by the Constitutional Revolution, it was closed by force in 1908 and 1911, but in 1925 it deposed the Qajar dynasty and opened the way for Reza Khan to become shah.

neguder.s: Negüder was a Mongol commander of the Golden Horde who led Jochid troops sent to the Middle East with Hülegü's expedition in the 1250s. When war broke out between the Golden Horde and the Ilkhanate in 1262, his men, cut off in eastern Iran and Afghanistan, became an…

naser-khan-qashqai.s: Naser Khan Qashqai was paramount chief (ilkhan) of the Qashqai confederation of southern Iran in the mid-20th century, the eldest son of Ismail Khan Solat al-Dowleh, who died in prison under Reza Shah. After Reza Shah's abdication in 1941 he returned to the tribe and, with his…

nombre-de-dios-panama.s: Nombre de Dios is a town on the Caribbean coast of Panama, founded in 1510 by Diego de Nicuesa. After the founding of Panama City in 1519 it became the Atlantic end of the treasure route across the isthmus, where Peruvian silver was traded at great fairs when the Spanish…

national-front-colombia.s: The National Front was a power-sharing agreement in Colombia from 1958 to 1974, under which the Liberal and Conservative parties alternated in the presidency every four years and divided public offices equally. Agreed after the fall of the dictator Gustavo Rojas Pinilla, it…

national-front-czechoslovakia.s: The National Front was the coalition of parties that governed Czechoslovakia from 1945 under the Košice Programme. After the Communist takeover of February 1948 it became an umbrella through which the Communist Party controlled all permitted parties and mass organisations.

newlands-resolution.s: The Newlands Resolution was the joint resolution of the United States Congress, introduced by Representative Francis G. Newlands, by which the United States annexed the Republic of Hawaii in July 1898.

ndlambe.s: Ndlambe was a Xhosa chief, son of Rharhabe, who acted as regent for his nephew Ngqika. Their rivalry split the Rharhabe Xhosa, and in 1818 Ndlambe's forces defeated Ngqika at Amalinde.

ngqika.s: Ngqika was paramount chief of the Rharhabe Xhosa, grandson of Rharhabe, who struggled with his uncle and regent Ndlambe for power. He sought British support, and after his defeat at Amalinde in 1818 the Cape intervened on his side, but in return he had to cede land between the…

nicolas-charles-victor-oudinot.s: Nicolas Charles Victor Oudinot, 2nd Duke of Reggio, was a French general and son of Napoleon's marshal of the same name. In 1849 he commanded the French expedition sent by Louis-Napoleon Bonaparte against the Roman Republic; after an initial repulse he besieged Rome and took…

norcia.s: Norcia, ancient Nursia, is a town in the Apennines of south-eastern Umbria, Italy. Originally a Sabine settlement, it became a Roman municipality and is known as the birthplace, around 480, of Saint Benedict, founder of Western monasticism, and his sister Scholastica.

nabeshima-katsushige.s: Nabeshima Katsushige was the first daimyo of the Saga domain in Hizen, Kyushu. The son of Nabeshima Naoshige, he fought on the western side in the Sekigahara campaign of 1600 but was pardoned by Tokugawa Ieyasu, and after the last Ryuzoji heir died in 1607 he became lord in…

nabeshima-clan.s: The Nabeshima were a samurai family of Hizen province in Kyushu who ruled the Saga domain throughout the Edo period. Originally chief retainers of the Ryuzoji, they took over their lords' lands under Nabeshima Naoshige after 1584.

new-democratic-party-saint-vincent-and-t.n: New Democratic Party (Saint Vincent and the Grenadines)
new-democratic-party-saint-vincent-and-t.s: The New Democratic Party is a centre-right political party in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, founded in 1975 by James Mitchell. It governed from 1984 to 2001 under Mitchell and then Arnhim Eustace, before spending 24 years in opposition to the Unity Labour Party.

nagara-river.s: The Nagara is a river of central Japan that flows about 166 kilometres from the mountains of Gifu Prefecture through the city of Gifu to Ise Bay. In 1556 Saito Dosan was killed in battle beside it by the forces of his son Yoshitatsu.

nur-mountains.s: The Nur Mountains, the ancient Amanus, are a range in southern Turkey running north-east from the Mediterranean coast near İskenderun and separating Cilicia from northern Syria. Their passes, the Syrian and Amanian Gates, carried the main routes between Anatolia and the…

nasr-i-samanid.s: Nasr I was the Samanid ruler of Transoxiana, governing from Samarkand from 875 until his death in 892. Appointed by the Abbasid caliph, he joined the family's scattered governorships into one realm, but quarrelled with his brother Isma'il ibn Ahmad, governor of Bukhara, who…

navajo.s: The Navajo, who call themselves Diné, are an Athabaskan-speaking Native American people of the south-western United States, related to the Apache. Herders of sheep and skilled weavers and silversmiths, they raided and traded with the Spanish and Pueblo settlements of New…

naganika.s: Naganika was a queen of the Satavahana dynasty, the wife of Satakarni I, who ruled the western Deccan probably in the 2nd or 1st century BCE. Her long Prakrit inscription in a cave at the Naneghat pass records the Vedic sacrifices performed by the royal family, including horse…

nahapana.s: Nahapana was the most powerful ruler of the Kshaharata line of the Western Satraps, who held Gujarat, Malwa and much of the western Deccan in the late 1st or early 2nd century CE. Inscriptions of his son-in-law Ushavadata in the caves at Nashik and Karla record his rule and…

nashik.s: Nashik is a city in Maharashtra, India, on the Godavari river north-east of Mumbai. The Pandavleni caves nearby, cut between the 1st century BCE and the 3rd century CE, preserve inscriptions of the Satavahanas, the Western Satraps and the Abhiras that are key sources for the…

neman.s: The Neman, or Nemunas, is a river of eastern Europe about 900 kilometres long, rising in Belarus and flowing through Lithuania to the Curonian Lagoon on the Baltic Sea. Its lower course forms the border between Lithuania and the Kaliningrad region of Russia.

national-liberation-alliance.s: The National Liberation Alliance was a left-wing popular front in Brazil founded in 1935, opposing fascism, imperialism and large landowners, with the communist leader Luís Carlos Prestes as honorary president. The Vargas government banned it in July 1935, and in November…

nabu-shumu-libur.s: Nabu-shumu-libur was the last king of the Second Dynasty of Isin, ruling Babylonia from about 1033 to 1026 BCE. Little is known of his reign, which was troubled by Aramean incursions, though an inscribed stone duck weight bearing his name survives.

nationalist-faction-spanish-civil-war.s: The Nationalists were the side in the Spanish Civil War that rose against the Second Spanish Republic in July 1936, uniting army officers, the Falange, monarchists, Carlists and conservative Catholics. Led from October 1936 by General Francisco Franco and aided by Nazi Germany…

nameisis.s: Nameisis was a Semigallian leader who led a major revolt against the Livonian Order after the Order's defeat by Lithuania at Aizkraukle in 1279. His forces raided as far as Riga, and the Semigallians held out for several years.

novi-sad.s: Novi Sad is the second-largest city of Serbia and the capital of the province of Vojvodina, on the Danube opposite the Petrovaradin fortress. Founded at the end of the 17th century, it became a centre of Serb culture under Habsburg rule.

novhorod-siverskyi.s: Novhorod-Siverskyi is a town on the Desna in Chernihiv Oblast, northern Ukraine. In the Middle Ages it was the seat of the Principality of Novgorod-Seversky, whose prince Igor led the 1185 campaign against the Cumans told in the Tale of Igor's Campaign.

nablus.s: Nablus is a city in the northern West Bank between Mount Ebal and Mount Gerizim, next to the site of ancient Shechem. It was founded as Flavia Neapolis by the Romans in 72 CE, and its name derives from Neapolis.

nasr-al-madhkur.s: Nasr Al-Madhkur was the Arab sheikh of Bushehr on the Persian coast of the Gulf in the mid-18th century, governing in the name of the Persian state. He extended his family's power across the Gulf by taking Bahrain in 1753.

nyikang.s: Nyikang is the legendary founder and culture hero of the Shilluk people of South Sudan. According to tradition he led his people north along the White Nile and settled them on its west bank, becoming their first reth, or king.

nanzhong.s: Nanzhong was the historical name for the region south of Sichuan, covering parts of modern Yunnan, Guizhou and southern Sichuan in China. Inhabited by many non-Han peoples, it rebelled against Shu Han after Liu Bei's death and was pacified by Zhuge Liang's southern campaign of…

ninlil.s: Ninlil was a Sumerian goddess, the wife of Enlil and mother of the moon god Nanna. Worshipped beside Enlil at Nippur, she was identified with Sud, the patron goddess of Shuruppak.

naymlap.s: Naymlap is the legendary founder of a dynasty in the Lambayeque valley of northern Peru. According to a tradition recorded by the Spanish chronicler Miguel Cabello Valboa in 1586, he arrived by sea with a fleet of balsa rafts, a large retinue and an idol of green stone, and…

nebiryraw-i.s: Nebiryraw I was a king of ancient Egypt in the Second Intermediate Period, ruling from Thebes around 1600 BCE; in Kim Ryholt's reconstruction he is one of the better-attested kings of the Sixteenth Dynasty, while others place him in the Seventeenth. He is named in the Turin…

nestos.s: The Nestos, called the Mesta in Bulgaria, is a river of the Balkans that rises in the Rila mountains of Bulgaria and flows about 230 km south-east between the Rhodope and Pirin ranges into the Aegean Sea opposite the island of Thasos. In antiquity it marked the border between…

national-salvation-front-romania.s: The National Salvation Front was the body that took power in Romania during the revolution of December 1989, after the fall of Nicolae Ceaușescu. Led by Ion Iliescu and dominated by former communists, it turned itself into a political party and won the elections of May 1990 by…

northern-frontier-district.s: The Northern Frontier District was a vast, arid region of northern Kenya under British rule, inhabited largely by Somali and Oromo pastoralists. A British commission found in 1962 that most of its Somali population wished to join Somalia, but the territory stayed with Kenya at…

nicolas-salmeron.s: Nicolás Salmerón (1838–1908) was a Spanish philosopher and republican politician who served as president of the executive power of the First Spanish Republic from July to September 1873. He suppressed the Cantonal Rebellion but resigned rather than sign death sentences for…

national-peoples-power.s: The National People's Power is a left-wing political alliance in Sri Lanka formed in 2019 around the Janatha Vimukthi Peramuna together with trade unions, professional and civil-society groups. Led by Anura Kumara Dissanayake, it grew after the economic crisis and protests of…

nanyang-henan.s: Nanyang is a city in south-western Henan province, China, at the centre of the Nanyang basin, which links the North China Plain with the Han River valley. In ancient times it was the site of the State of Shen and a key approach between Chu and the northern states, and under…

nevada.s: Nevada is a state in the western United States, largely within the arid Great Basin, with its capital at Carson City. Acquired from Mexico in 1848 and first part of Utah Territory, it boomed after the discovery of the Comstock Lode silver deposits in 1859 and was admitted as a…

nzakara.s: The Nzakara are a people of the south-east of the Central African Republic, living along the Mbomou River around Bangassou. From the 18th century they were ruled by the Bandia, a dynasty related to the rulers of the Zande, whose sultanate of Bangassou traded in ivory and…

niamey.s: Niamey is the capital and largest city of Niger, on the Niger River in the south-west of the country. A small village when the French arrived, it replaced Zinder as the capital of the Colony of Niger in 1926 and grew rapidly after independence in 1960.

ndele.s: Ndélé is a town in the north of the Central African Republic, capital of Bamingui-Bangoran prefecture. It was built from the 1890s as the fortified capital of Muhammad al-Sanusi, sultan of Dar al-Kuti, whose slave raids fed the trade routes to the north.

ndyuka.s: The Ndyuka are a maroon people of eastern Suriname and French Guiana, descended from enslaved Africans who escaped from Dutch plantations into the rainforest in the 18th century. After years of conflict the colonial government made a peace treaty with them in 1760, recognising…

ndlovukati.s: Ndlovukati, meaning she-elephant, is the title of the queen mother of the Swazi Kingdom (Eswatini). She rules jointly with the king, the Ngwenyama, keeping her own royal village at Lobamba, taking part in national rituals such as the Incwala and Umhlanga, and acting as a check…

ngwane-iii.s: Ngwane III was a chief of the Dlamini clan who, according to Swazi tradition, led his people around 1745 to settle near the lower Pongola river in what is now southern Eswatini, founding the nucleus of the Swazi Kingdom. The Swazi still call their country kaNgwane, the land of…

ngwenyama.s: Ngwenyama, meaning lion, is the title of the king of the Swazi Kingdom (Eswatini). The Ngwenyama reigns jointly with the queen mother, the Ndlovukati, and is regarded as the embodiment of the nation, central to rituals such as the Incwala.

neva-river.s: The Neva is a short but powerful river of north-western Russia, flowing about 74 kilometres from Lake Ladoga to the Gulf of Finland. It formed a key route between the Baltic and Novgorod and was long contested between Novgorod, later Russia, and Sweden; Alexander Nevsky won…

nyenskans.s: Nyenskans was a Swedish fortress built in 1611 at the confluence of the Okhta and Neva rivers, on the site of present-day Saint Petersburg. It guarded the town of Nyen, a trading post for commerce with Russia, and was the centre of Swedish Ingria.

niebla.s: Niebla is a town on the Río Tinto in the province of Huelva, Andalusia, Spain. Its walls of reddish stone, largely of the Almohad period, are among the best preserved in Spain.

nurek-dam.s: The Nurek Dam is an earth-fill hydroelectric dam on the Vakhsh river in Tajikistan, about 300 metres high and for decades the tallest dam in the world. Built by the Soviet Union between 1961 and 1980, it supplies most of the country's electricity and water for irrigation in…

nuba-peoples.s: The Nuba are a group of diverse peoples of the Nuba Mountains in South Kordofan, Sudan, speaking many languages from several language families. Living mostly as hill farmers, they were long raided for slaves by neighbouring states and later suffered heavily in Sudan's civil wars.

nguyen-lu.s: Nguyễn Lữ was the youngest of the three Tây Sơn brothers who rose against the Nguyễn lords in 1771, together with Nguyễn Nhạc and Nguyễn Huệ. After their victories he was given a royal title and responsibility for the far south, but he proved a weaker commander than his…

narendranagar.s: Narendranagar is a town in the Tehri Garhwal district of Uttarakhand, India, in the hills above Rishikesh. It was founded in the early 20th century by Maharaja Narendra Shah of Tehri Garhwal State, who moved his capital there from Tehri and named it after himself.

naidatham.s: The Naidatham is a 16th-century Tamil poem by the Pandya king Ativira Rama Pandya of Tenkasi. Based on the Sanskrit Naishadhiya Charita of Sriharsha, it retells the story of Nala and Damayanti from the Mahabharata.

north-maluku.s: North Maluku is a province of eastern Indonesia covering the northern Maluku Islands, including Halmahera, Ternate, Tidore, Bacan and Morotai. Its small volcanic islands were the original home of cloves and the seat of the sultanates of Ternate, Tidore, Bacan and Jailolo.

nezahualpilli.s: Nezahualpilli was the ruler of Texcoco from 1472 to 1515, son and successor of Nezahualcoyotl. A partner in the Aztec Triple Alliance, he was famed as a wise judge, astrologer and poet, and is said to have foretold disasters for the Mexica.

newar-buddhism.s: Newar Buddhism is the form of Buddhism practised by the Newar people of the Kathmandu Valley in Nepal. It preserves Mahayana and Vajrayana traditions in Sanskrit, with a hereditary, married clergy of Vajracharyas and Shakyas who serve monastic courtyards called bahals.

nafud.s: The Nafud is a large sand desert in the north of the Arabian Peninsula, in northern Saudi Arabia. Covering some 65,000 square kilometres, it is known for its high red dunes and harsh climate.

ngangelizwe.s: Ngangelizwe was king of the Thembu in the present-day Eastern Cape, South Africa, in the second half of the 19th century. His reign saw wars with the Gcaleka Xhosa under Sarhili, and he accepted British authority to secure support, opening Thembuland to Cape magistrates.

ngubengcuka.s: Ngubengcuka was king of the Thembu in the present-day Eastern Cape, South Africa, in the early 19th century, until his death in 1832. He strengthened the kingdom and sought alliances with the Cape Colony and missionaries against raiders displaced by the wars of the period.

nikephoros-phokas-the-elder.s: Nikephoros Phokas the Elder was a Byzantine general of the late 9th century and the grandfather of the emperor Nikephoros II Phokas. Sent to southern Italy in 885, he recovered much of Calabria and Apulia from the Arabs, laying the basis of the theme of Longobardia.

nasrid-dynasty.s: The Nasrid dynasty was the last Muslim ruling house of the Iberian Peninsula, founded by Muhammad I ibn Nasr, who rose at Arjona in 1232 and took Granada in 1238. From Granada it ruled a mountainous emirate reaching to Málaga and Almería, often as a tributary of Castile.

namri-songtsen.s: Namri Songtsen was a chief of the Yarlung valley in central Tibet who, with the support of clan leaders who had deserted rival lords, brought much of central Tibet under his authority in the late 6th and early 7th centuries. His conquests laid the foundations of the Tibetan…

nuku-of-tidore.s: Nuku was a prince of Tidore in the Moluccas who led a long revolt against the Dutch East India Company from 1780, after the company had interfered in the Tidorese succession. Operating from Seram, the Raja Ampat Islands and the coasts of New Guinea and aided by the British, he…

nonaka-kenzan.s: Nonaka Kenzan was chief minister of the Tosa domain on Shikoku in the mid-17th century. A follower of the Neo-Confucian teaching of Zhu Xi, he carried out ambitious reforms, building irrigation works and ports, opening new fields and managing forests, which greatly increased…

nam-dinh.s: Nam Dinh is a city in the Red River Delta of northern Vietnam, south-east of Hanoi. The surrounding coastal district was the homeland of the Tran clan, which founded the Tran dynasty in 1225, and the Tran kings built a secondary palace complex at Thien Truong nearby.

neuse-river.s: The Neuse River flows south-east across the coastal plain of North Carolina into Pamlico Sound. Its valley was home to Tuscarora towns and to the Neusiok people, who gave the river its name.

nigde.s: Niğde is a city in central Anatolia, Turkey, the capital of Niğde Province, lying between the volcanic landscape of Cappadocia and the Taurus Mountains. Nearby lie the remains of ancient Tyana, capital of the Neo-Hittite kingdom of Tuwana.

nepherites-i.s: Nepherites I was the founder of the Twenty-ninth Dynasty of Egypt, ruling from about 399 to 393 BCE. A general from Mendes in the Delta, he overthrew Amyrtaeus of the Twenty-eighth Dynasty, who was probably executed.

nectanebo-i.s: Nectanebo I was the founder of the Thirtieth Dynasty, the last native dynasty of Egypt, reigning from 380 to 362 BCE. A general from Sebennytos in the Delta, he deposed Nepherites II of the Twenty-ninth Dynasty.

necho-i.s: Necho I was a ruler of Sais in the western Nile Delta in the 7th century BCE and the father of Psamtik I, founder of the Twenty-sixth Dynasty. He became a vassal of Assyria after Esarhaddon and Ashurbanipal drove the Kushites from Egypt, and was briefly taken to Nineveh before…

nitocris-i.s: Nitocris I was a daughter of Psamtik I of the Twenty-sixth Dynasty of Egypt. In 656 BCE her father sent her to Thebes to be adopted as the future God's Wife of Amun by the Kushite holders of the office, peacefully bringing Upper Egypt under his rule; the event is recorded on…

nagao-clan.s: The Nagao clan was a Japanese warrior family that served as deputies (shugodai) of the Uesugi governors in Echigo and the Kantō region. In the early 16th century Nagao Tamekage overpowered his Uesugi lords in Echigo, and his son Nagao Kagetora took over the province.

national-academy-of-sciences-of-ukraine.n: National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine
national-academy-of-sciences-of-ukraine.s: The National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine is the country's highest scientific body, founded in Kyiv in November 1918 under the Ukrainian State of Pavlo Skoropadsky as the Ukrainian Academy of Sciences. Its first president was the geochemist Volodymyr Vernadsky.

narni.s: Narni is a hill town in southern Umbria, Italy, above a gorge of the Nera river. Rome founded the colony of Narnia on the site of the Umbrian town of Nequinum in 299 BCE to guard the routes into Umbria, and the Via Flaminia later crossed the Nera there on the Bridge of…

new-zealand-national-party.s: The New Zealand National Party is a centre-right party formed in 1936 by a merger of the United and Reform parties in opposition to the first Labour government. It has been one of New Zealand's two main parties ever since, governing under prime ministers including Sidney…

niagara-on-the-lake.s: Niagara-on-the-Lake is a town in Ontario, Canada, where the Niagara River enters Lake Ontario. Settled by Loyalists after the American Revolution and named Newark, it was the first capital of Upper Canada from 1792 until John Graves Simcoe moved the capital to York, later…

nordgau.s: The Nordgau, or Bavarian Nordgau, was a medieval frontier region north of the Danube in the Duchy of Bavaria, roughly corresponding to the later Upper Palatinate and parts of Franconia. It was ruled by margraves in the 10th and 11th centuries.

nunnery-quadrangle.s: The Nunnery Quadrangle is a group of four long buildings around a courtyard at the Maya city of Uxmal in Yucatán, Mexico, built around 900. Spanish visitors gave it its name, imagining a convent, though its purpose may have been residential or administrative.

nusrat-khan.s: Nusrat Khan was a general and minister of Alauddin Khalji, sultan of Delhi. With Ulugh Khan he led the invasion of Gujarat in 1299, sacking Anahilavada and the temple of Somnath and capturing the Vaghela queen Kamala Devi.

nicene-christianity.s: Nicene Christianity is the Christian doctrine defined by the Council of Nicaea in 325 and the Council of Constantinople in 381, which holds that the Son is of the same substance as the Father. Made the official faith of the Roman Empire by Theodosius I in 380, it was opposed…

nicolas-maduro.s: Nicolás Maduro is a Venezuelan politician, a former bus driver and trade unionist who served as foreign minister under Hugo Chávez and succeeded him as president in 2013. His rule saw economic collapse, hyperinflation and the emigration of millions, while disputed elections in…

national-university-of-san-marcos.s: The National University of San Marcos in Lima, Peru, was founded by a royal decree of Charles V on 12 May 1551 and is regarded as the oldest officially established university in the Americas. Run at first by the Dominicans, it trained clergy, lawyers and officials of the…

narva.s: Narva is a city in north-eastern Estonia on the Narva river, which forms the border with Russia. A trading town of Danish Estonia from the 13th century, it passed to the Teutonic Order in 1346, was held by Russia from 1558 and by Sweden from 1581.

nimes.s: Nîmes is a city in the Gard department of southern France. Founded around a sacred spring as Nemausus, the chief town of the Volcae Arecomici, it became a Roman colony under Augustus and keeps outstanding Roman monuments, including an amphitheatre, the Maison Carrée and the…

nerl-klyazma.s: The Nerl is a river of central Russia, about 280 km long, that flows through the Suzdal region and joins the Klyazma near Bogolyubovo, east of Vladimir. Its valley was part of the core of Vladimir-Suzdal, and the Church of the Intercession built near its mouth in 1165 is one…

ndatte-yalla-mbodj.s: Ndatte Yalla Mbodj was the last ruling queen (linger) of Waalo in northern Senegal, holding power from 1846. She resisted French expansion from Saint-Louis and raids by the Trarza Moors, and sought to control trade on the lower Senegal river.

nantucket.s: Nantucket is an island about 50 kilometres south of Cape Cod in Massachusetts, long inhabited by Wampanoag people. English settlers bought land there from 1659, and the island was governed by New York until it passed to the Province of Massachusetts Bay in 1692.

nabongo-mumia.s: Nabongo Mumia was king, or nabongo, of the Wanga kingdom in western Kenya from 1882 until his death in 1949. He welcomed British agents and caravans to his capital, and Wanga served as a base for British expansion into the region.

nizak-tarkhan.s: Nizak Tarkhan (died 710) was a Hephthalite prince of Badghis and Tokharistan who resisted the Umayyad conquest of Central Asia. After first submitting to the Arab governor Qutayba ibn Muslim, he rebelled in 709, holding the yabghu of Tokharistan in his custody and rallying the…

nara.s: Nara is a city in the Kansai region of Japan and the capital of Nara Prefecture. The surrounding Nara basin was the heartland of the early Yamato kingship, and from 710 to 784 the planned capital Heijō-kyō on the site gave its name to the Nara period.

nochixtlan-valley.s: The Nochixtlán Valley is a highland valley in the Mixteca Alta of Oaxaca, Mexico. Settled since early times, it was one of the most densely populated parts of the Mixtec world in the Postclassic period and home to kingdoms such as Yanhuitlan.

namonuito.s: Namonuito is a large atoll in the Caroline Islands, part of Chuuk State in the Federated States of Micronesia. Its people took part in the sawei, the system of tribute and exchange that linked the atolls of the central Carolines to the Gagil district of Yap.

nehemiah.s: Nehemiah was a Jewish official at the Persian court who, according to the Hebrew Bible, became governor of the province of Yehud under Artaxerxes I. Arriving around 445 BCE, he organised the rebuilding of the walls of Jerusalem despite opposition from neighbouring leaders,…

nemequene.s: Nemequene was zipa, ruler of the southern Muisca realm of Bacatá in the highlands of present-day Colombia, in the early sixteenth century. He is remembered for a code of laws, recorded by Spanish chroniclers, that set harsh punishments for crimes such as theft, murder and incest.

northern-crusades.s: The Northern Crusades were the crusades waged by Catholic Danish, Swedish and German rulers and military orders against the pagan peoples around the Baltic Sea from the 12th to the 15th century. They included the Wendish Crusade of 1147, the conquest of Livonia and Estonia and…

north-west-rebellion.s: The North-West Rebellion was a rising in 1885 of Métis and some First Nations people in the District of Saskatchewan against the government of Canada, led by Louis Riel and Gabriel Dumont. After early success at Duck Lake, the rebels were defeated at Batoche in May 1885; Riel…

northwest-indian-war.s: The Northwest Indian War was fought from 1786 to 1795 between the United States and a confederation of Native American nations of the Northwest Territory, including the Shawnee, Miami and Lenape. The confederacy destroyed American armies under Harmar (1790) and St.

norman-conquest.s: The Norman Conquest was the invasion and occupation of England by William, Duke of Normandy, in 1066 and the following years. William defeated and killed Harold Godwinson at the Battle of Hastings on 14 October 1066 and was crowned on Christmas Day.

ndwandwe-zulu-war.s: The Ndwandwe–Zulu War was fought between the Ndwandwe under Zwide and the rising Zulu kingdom of Shaka in what is now KwaZulu-Natal. After the Zulu repulsed an attack at Gqokli Hill in 1818, Shaka defeated the Ndwandwe at the Mhlatuze River in 1819.

northern-seven-years-war.s: The Northern Seven Years' War was fought from 1563 to 1570 between Sweden under Eric XIV and John III and an alliance of Denmark–Norway, Lübeck and Poland-Lithuania. Fought on land in Scandinavia and at sea in the Baltic, it ended in exhaustion with the Treaty of Stettin in 1570.

neapolitan-war.s: The Neapolitan War was fought in 1815 between the Kingdom of Naples under Joachim Murat and the Austrian Empire. During Napoleon's Hundred Days, Murat declared war on Austria and called for Italian unity, but he was defeated at Tolentino in May 1815.
